# EDU 360 V4.0 — Deliverable 1 · Master Product Specification

**Edition:** V4.0 Final — Independently Validated and Corrected
**Date:** 30 October 2026
**Supersedes:** V4.0 Consolidation Review Draft C1 (30 Oct 2026), which superseded the V3.3 set (27 Oct 2026)
**Documentation readiness:** **CONDITIONAL PASS** — complete and consistent enough to start engineering on the areas listed in V4-17; the open decisions in V4-15 must be closed before the affected features are built.
**Application production readiness:** **not established.** No application code, deployed API, penetration test, load test, restore test or user acceptance test exists. This document set is a specification, not evidence of working software.

> **How this document is organised.** Part I (sections V4-1 to V4-19) is the V4.0 layer: scope, authority, the controls every module shares, the module index, workflow index, technical baselines, security, QA, open decisions and readiness. Part II is the **complete V3.3 Master Product Document** — Version 3.2 with every row of the V3.3 Change Table written in at the place it names — and is the normative functional requirement text (business rules, approval chains, module rules, role workflows, notifications, formulas, Section 21 checks, Section 26 action list, Section 27 Phase 1 rules). Part II keeps its original section numbers, so every existing reference such as "§7.1" or "[R2-03]" still resolves. Appendices A–G carry the full action rules, the permission matrix, the historical decision records, the V3.3 application log, the deliverable crosswalk, the history-only Version 1.0 and 2.1 documents and the V3.3 Change Table itself. Where Part I and Part II differ, Part I says so explicitly and gives the reason; otherwise Part II governs.

## V4-1. Executive status

The V4.0 C1 draft carried the V3.3 product and technical baseline forward but left four things unfinished: the V3.3 Master Product Document existed only as Version 3.2 plus a change table; the database scripts were not in the package; most API operations had no error codes; and the design system and prototype were missing. This edition closes those four, corrects 26 further defects (V4-16), and re-runs every check that can run without an application.

## V4-2. Authority, precedence and version control

### V4-2.1 Order of authority

1. **Product Owner decisions** recorded in the decision registers (Final Decisions v1.1, Phase 1 Requirements Decision Register PQ-01–PQ-82, review decisions F-1–F-15, V3.3 decisions C1–C13, answers 1–10, letter-gap decisions, R-1, PO-A1). Appendix C carries the decision-record text.
2. **This document**: Part II (the V3.3 Master Product Document, including Sections 26 and 27) together with the **Master Permission Matrix V3.3** and the **Action List V3.3** (Deliverables 2 and 3). This is the source-of-truth rule C1 (Part II, Document control, row "Source of truth", Change Table A8). Part I adds the V4.0 layer.
3. Within the access model: the **Action List governs access checks**; the matrix letter is a summary; where a letter and a role's Restrictions line disagree, the Restrictions line wins [R2-18, D-003, RL-05].
4. **Deliverable 4** (database) and **Deliverable 5** (API) are the intended technical design. The SQL scripts are the executable form of Deliverable 4; where prose and script differ, the script is the fact and the prose is corrected (V4.0 did this for the FK count and ER types).
5. **Deliverables 7, 9 and 10** (flow map, design system, prototype) are visual aids. Where they differ from 1–4, 1–4 win [C1].
6. Version 2.1 and Version 1.0 are **history only** [C1].
7. The **Letter Gaps Proposal** is evidence of how the letter-gap decisions were made; only its accepted or changed rows (applied through the V3.3 Change Table) carry authority.

### V4-2.2 Sources not available

- **"EDU 360 — Role and Permission Management Rules"** (named in the V4.0 brief) was not among the files supplied. It has not been interpreted. The role-template and custom-role rules in V4-5 and Deliverable 3 are marked *V4.0 recommendation* and rest on the approved V3.3 rules (R2-02, RL-05, ROLE_CUSTOM_MANAGE, D-001, D-003) only.
- The V3.3 Master Product Document was never issued as one file. V4.0 builds it (Part II) by applying the V3.3 Change Table to Version 3.2 exactly as the table instructs ("nothing is deleted; a changed sentence keeps its Version 3.2 wording and the 'Changed in 3.3' note goes beside it" [R2-42]). Every one of the 131 Part A rows is placed and logged in Appendix D. For 28 rows the table names a section but quotes no Version 3.2 sentence (pure additions, "–"); those notes are written at the end of the named section, which is where an addition to that section belongs.

### V4-2.3 Version control

- Immutable identifiers: action codes, role codes, requirement IDs (e.g. R2-03, PQ-66), decision IDs, `operationId`s, database object names, test IDs (DB-nn), finding IDs (V4-F-nn). V4.0 changed none of them.
- Every V4.0 change has a row in the correction log (Deliverable 2, *V4.0 Correction Log*) with before, after, reason, affected deliverables and the check that verified it.
- New proposals are labelled *V4.0 recommendation*; they are not decisions until the Product Owner records them.
- The next edition is V4.1 only for a formal decision batch; corrections that do not change a decision keep V4.0 with a new edition date.

## V4-3. Product shape and release scope

EDU 360 is a multi-tenant education management SaaS. The tenant is the contractual and billed customer: a university group with its colleges and schools, a standalone college, or a standalone school. A standalone institution never creates a university record. Launch market: India only, INR, English only, one responsive installable web application, no native apps in v1 (Part II §1, §3, §24).

| Phase | Modules (Part II §8) |
|---|---|
| Phase 1 (v1) | Sign-in and account; users and roles; institution setup and academic structure; timetable and syllabus; attendance; examinations; results; assignments, homework and study material; fees; leave; communication; community feed and events; complaints; student notes; policies and documents; staff records; risk monitoring; reports and dashboards; data import, search and records; governance and data protection; platform administration |
| Phase 2 | Payroll, library, placement, admissions (WhatsApp channel) |
| Phase 3 | Hostel, transport, alumni, research and publications, API and integration governance |

**Not in Phase 1** (Part II §25; Deliverable 5 info block): refunds, partial payments, tax, re-evaluation, moderation queues, sharing, WhatsApp, report-abuse, custom report builder, alumni login. The database refuses partial allocation (DB-30), a REFUND ledger type (DB-39) and a WhatsApp channel (DB-74). Phase 2/3 tables or reference rows do not make a feature available; module entitlement and action checks decide.

## V4-4. Tenant, institution and academic hierarchy

**Platform → Tenant → University (university-group tenants only) → Institution (college or school) → Department / academic unit → academic structures (program, program year, semester, class, section, subject, course offering, subject group) → users and linked profiles.**

- A user may hold several role assignments inside one tenant, each with its own scope. Exactly one assignment is active per request; permissions from different assignments are never combined (Part II §6, §11.0 [PQ-16, PQ-17, HI-15]).
- Tenant data is isolated by forced, fail-closed row-level security on every `app` table and by composite foreign keys that begin with `tenant_id` (and pin `institution_id` where both exist). In isolated mode every tenant key points at `app.tenant_local` inside the tenant database; no foreign key crosses databases (Deliverable 4 §2, §10; DB-01–DB-05, DB-55–DB-59).
- Institution-level RLS (PTD-I1) is designed and tested (DB-06, DB-56, DB-57) but becomes policy only when OD-03 is approved.
- Institution go-live requires its Principal's-leave approver; a university tenant's go-live also requires the Vice-Chancellor's-leave approver [C7] (DB-07–DB-11).

## V4-5. Roles, permissions, approvals and templates

### V4-5.1 Roles

71 standard roles (6 platform, 3 tenant, 13 university, 33 college, 15 school, 1 external applicant) — full catalogue Part II §6.6 and Deliverable 3, *Role Catalogue*. The Governing Body Approver (added in V3.3 [C6, C13]) exists only where there is no Management and approves only the Principal's, the Vice-Chancellor's or a dedicated Data Protection Contact's own leave (Part II §12.12).

### V4-5.2 Permission letters

| Code | Meaning | Allows |
|---|---|---|
| F | Full | Create, view, edit and delete within scope. Never approval |
| M | Manage | Create, view and edit day-to-day records. No set-up, no approval |
| C | Configure | Set up rules and settings for the area |
| A | Approve | Approve or reject only at the approval-chain step the role holds |
| V | View | Read within scope (field restrictions still apply) |
| R | Request | Submit and track requests for oneself or one's child |
| N | No access | Area hidden |
| X+Y | Combined | e.g. M+C, M+A, V+R, V+C |

These are the V3.3 definitions (Matrix *Legend & Rules*), unchanged; the V4.0 brief's definitions match them. Letters summarise authority over other people's records in an area; self-service actions, delegation, bulk approval and verify/confirm steps appear only in the Action List [D-003]. Every non-N letter is backed by at least one action and an action includes the reads it needs [R-1].

### V4-5.3 Approval and separation of duties (normative, from Part II §7)

- Approval power comes only from approval chains; F and M never approve [RL-03].
- Nobody approves their own request, including the Principal's own leave [AP-04, D-002]; the database refuses it (K-015, DB-12) and, from V4.0, refuses naming the person whose leave it is as that leave's approver (V4-DB-01, DB-77).
- One actor never decides two steps of one request; the step is skipped and logged [AP-04] (K-014, DB-15).
- Reject needs a remark and ends the request; there is no "send back" — the requester submits again (Part II §7.0 [AP-24]). V4.0 aligns the design system with this rule (Deliverable 9, V4-DS-02).
- A decided step never changes; a second simultaneous decision changes nothing [R2-01, TE-09] (DB-16, DB-17).
- Delegation: for set dates, to a same-or-higher role or the one designated deputy (Principal → Vice-Principal); no re-delegation; DPO only to another DPO; merit-list approval never delegated; DPO approvals never bulk-approved [AP-07, AP-08, D-001, C12, WF-37] (DB-18–DB-20).
- Requests never approve themselves; the system only reminds.

### V4-5.3a Missing roles roll down

When a level or role is missing, its permissions roll down to the next level and the level above can change them — **decided by the Product Owner on 30 Oct 2026 (V4-PD-01)**; full rule in V4-19.

### V4-5.4 Role templates and custom roles — *V4.0 recommendation, not yet decided*

- The 71 standard roles stay the compatibility set. Deliverable 3, *Baseline Templates*, holds one draft template per standard role, populated only from the V3.3 Role × Action grid (1,851 grants) and the 71 × 28 matrix.
- Choosing a template copies a **draft** role profile. It never assigns a role to a user and never grants effective access. Saving, activating and assigning are separate, audited operations.
- A custom role is built only from Action List actions (ROLE_CUSTOM_MANAGE: College Admin, School Admin; University Admin for university-office roles only [C4]). The creator cannot grant more than their own authority, scope or chain position; "Never allowed" items stay blocked whatever the custom role says (Part II §26.1 rule 6); platform roles never receive tenant roles [F-12].
- Proposed lifecycle: Draft → Active → Inactive → Archived; roles with assignments or history are never hard-deleted; every permission or scope change is audited and re-validates affected assignments.
- These are recommendations because the "Role and Permission Management Rules" source was not supplied (V4-2.2). Deliverable 3, *Custom Role Governance*, lists each rule with its source or its "V4.0 recommendation" label.

## V4-7. Functional modules

### V4-7.1 Controls every module applies

Every operation checks, on the server, in this order: authenticated identity and trusted tenant (token tenant = subdomain; `X-Tenant-ID` alone is never trusted); module entitlement for the tenant's plan; the active role assignment and its scope; the Action List action code; record state and workflow preconditions; field-level and sensitive-data rules; separation of duties; request schema; idempotency and optimistic concurrency (`If-Match` on every PATCH). Writes run in one transaction under RLS and composite FKs, write an audit event in the same transaction, and dispatch notifications after commit with idempotent retries. UI hiding is never a security boundary. Denied attempts are logged [AU-05]. (Part II §7, §8, §16; Deliverable 5 §3.)

### V4-7.3 Module notes that Part I adds or clarifies

- **Attendance.** Statuses are PRESENT, ABSENT, ON_APPROVED_LEAVE and NOT_HELD (database CHECK; Part II §8.4). There is no "Late" status; the V3.3 prototype showed one and V4.0 removed it (Deliverable 10, DR-04). Corrections are one request header with lines and one approval (K-028, DB-69–DB-72). OD-04 (granularity) and OD-07 (offline sync conflicts) stay open. Board rules such as the CBSE 75% eligibility threshold are configurable per institution, not a product-wide default.
- **Examinations and results.** School results: teacher submits → Class Teacher review → Principal approval → School Principal or School Admin publishes; college publisher depends on the mode (Controller under an EDU 360 university, College Admin otherwise) and the database refuses the wrong publisher (`WRONG_PUBLISHER_FOR_MODE`). Re-evaluation is not Phase 1. A published result changes only to WITHDRAWN, through its own withdrawal request.
- **Fees.** A structure is frozen when it leaves DRAFT; any change is a new version approved by the Principal (DB-22–DB-26). One open online payment per account. Payment intent stores its target installments before the gateway order; allocation only when PAID; received = allocated + credit (PO-A1). No partial payment, no refund. Ledger append-only; locked months refuse postings; receipts immutable and gap-free. Credit consumption rules OD-05a/b/c stay open.
- **Leave.** The Principal's own leave goes to Management, otherwise the Governing Body Approver, or (college/school under a university) the Registrar or Vice-Chancellor; the approver must be set before go-live and can never be the Principal (V4-DB-01). Leave with a medical attachment is sensitive and every view is logged.
- **Communication.** Notices: direct publication by Admin / Principal (institution) and teachers (class / department); others submit for Principal approval. WhatsApp is Phase 2. **Reference-data gap (V4-F-21):** `ref.notification_template` is loaded with 0 rows although Part II §15 lists the notification catalogue; the templates must be loaded before notifications can be sent (owner: Engineering, before the pilot).
- **Reports.** Fixed reports only; reports need no approval; every generation is logged [C2]. Exports are sensitive operations.

## V4-9. Database

PostgreSQL (15 or later, OD-01; validated on 16.15); schemas `app` (tenant data), `platform` (central), `ref` (reference); shared or isolated tenant mode with the same migration set; forced fail-closed RLS; composite tenant-led keys; append-only ledger, notes, messages and audit; partitioned attendance and ledger. Full specification, data dictionary and evidence: Deliverable 4. Execution order: `01 → 02 → 03 → 03b → 08 → 05`; tests `04 → 07 → 09` on a throw-away database (Deliverable 4, V4.0 revision summary).

## V4-10. API

REST over HTTPS, OpenAPI 3.1.0, `/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/…`, OAuth2/OIDC bearer tokens from Keycloak (realm model OD-10), cursor pagination, `Idempotency-Key` on 45 required operations, `If-Match` on every PATCH, one 89-code error catalogue with database-error mapping, `x-action-codes` on every operation except three blocked by open decisions. Full contract: Deliverable 5.

## V4-11. Security, privacy and compliance

### V4-11.1 Tenant and institution isolation
No cross-tenant read or write by any tenant role; platform schema not granted to the tenant role (DB-59); RLS fails closed when the tenant context is missing, empty or reset (DB-01, DB-55); institution RLS when OD-03 is approved.

### V4-11.2 Application security requirements (V4.0)
OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) and OWASP ASVS as the test taxonomy: object-level authorisation on every ID (return 404 for foreign-tenant objects), function- and property-level authorisation, rate limits (OD-77), SSRF-safe outbound calls, allow-listed file types with scanning, signed gateway callbacks, secrets in a managed vault, parameterised SQL, output encoding, two-step login for the roles in Part II §11.0, lockout after 5 wrong passwords for 15 minutes [NF-07]. These are requirements; none is implemented yet.

### V4-11.3 Indian privacy law — status to be confirmed by counsel
The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025 were notified on 13 November 2025 with phased commencement: institutional provisions immediately, consent-manager provisions after 12 months, and the main obligations (notice, consent, data-principal rights, children's data, security safeguards, breach notification) after 18 months, i.e. about 13 May 2027. In January 2026 MeitY consulted on shortening some deadlines for significant data fiduciaries; as of the sources consulted this was a proposal, not a notified change. EDU 360 processes children's data at scale, so verifiable parental consent, the Rules' provisions for educational institutions, breach notification timelines and retention must be mapped provision by provision by legal counsel before launch (OD-14, OD-06). This document does not claim legal compliance.

### V4-11.4 Accessibility
Target WCAG 2.2 Level AA for every screen and state, tested automatically and manually; the design system's contrast pairs were measured in V4.0 (Deliverable 9, V4-DS-04).

## V4-12. UI/UX, design system and prototype

Deliverable 9 (Master Design System, "Stillwater" tokens, DM Sans / Manrope, Noto Sans Devanagari and Kannada for later locales) is the visual source; Deliverable 10 is the clickable prototype; Deliverable 7 holds the flow map and the screen-state contract. V4.0 corrections: the design system no longer offers "Return for changes" on approvals (no send-back rule), its version label reads 2.1 consistently, and the prototype's 25 open design decisions were checked against V3.3 — 21 resolved from the sources, 4 left open with an owner (Deliverable 10, Decision register). Every screen must show loading, empty, error, success, permission-denied and read-only (trial-ended) states.

**Roles and permissions screens (V4.0).** Eight screens are specified in Deliverable 3, sheet *Roles & Permissions Screens*: RP-01 Roles, RP-02 Role detail, RP-03 Create / edit custom role, RP-04 Assign roles, RP-05 User access, RP-06 Missing roles (roll-down), RP-07 Delegations, RP-08 Access review and role audit. The prototype (Deliverable 10) shows Roles & permissions and Missing roles; decisions taken through roll-down show an "Acting for …" badge (Deliverable 9).

## V4-13. QA and release readiness

### V4-13.1 Executed evidence
97 database tests pass (V4-1.1), including the role roll-down (DB-80–DB-97). They cover isolation, composite keys, approval integrity, delegation, fee-structure immutability, payment allocation, ledger, receipts, attendance and term locks, grading-scheme freeze, correction freeze, leave overlap, complaint finality, channel restrictions, go-live and the V4.0 approver rule. They do not test APIs, screens, integrations, load, backups or deployment.

### V4-13.2 Designed, not executed
1,112 action-level tests (positive, unauthorised actor, out-of-scope record, rule / never-allowed violation for each of 278 actions), 30 cross-cutting end-to-end scenarios and the seven checks the V3.3 Change Table proposed for Section 21 (25–31) as test designs — they are not added to Section 21 until the Product Owner approves them (Part II §25.4). Deliverable 6.

### V4-13.3 Required before launch
API contract tests for every operation; browser end-to-end tests per role; adversarial cross-tenant and cross-institution tests; concurrency tests (approvals, payment callbacks, receipts, locks); WCAG 2.2 AA audit; penetration test; performance against OD-13 thresholds; migration, restore and disaster-recovery rehearsal; UAT with pilot institutions [PQ-78].

## V4-14. Commercial, onboarding and go-to-market

The tenant is billed in INR; India-only launch. Plans and pricing (PLAN_MANAGE: Product Owner sets prices), discounts only by the Product Owner, invoicing by the Billing Manager, overdue flag for suspension review (Part II §24, §8.20). Entitlements control which modules a tenant has; actions control what a user may do; scope controls which records. Metered billing (SMS units, storage) waits for OD-73. Sales material must show Phase 2 and 3 modules as later phases. A rate card is not in the sources and is not invented here.

## V4-19. Role roll-down when a level or role is missing (V4-PD-01)

**Decision V4-PD-01 (Product Owner, 30 Oct 2026; recorded in Deliverable 2, *V4.0 New Decisions*).** If there is no hierarchy above a role, or a role has no active holder, all of that role's permissions are given to the level below, and the higher authority can change them. This generalises rules V3.3 already had for standalone institutions ("Management, or the Principal if there is no Management" [R2-03, HI-11]; the standalone Admin takes over university-level duties; the standalone College Admin publishes results [HI-10]); those rules are unchanged and are now instances of this one.

### V4-19.1 The rule

1. **Who receives the permissions.** A role's **approval** actions (`ref.action_catalog.is_approval_action`) go to the **head of the next level down** (Vice-Chancellor → Principal / School Principal); its **other** actions (setup, configuration, operations) go to the **admin of the next level down** (University Admin → College Admin / School Admin). For a role in the middle of a chain (no HOD, no Vice Principal) the step goes to the next approver of that chain, as V3.3 already does.
2. **When.** A role is missing for an institution when no active user holds it (or a custom role built on it) with that institution or the whole tenant in scope. A standalone college or school therefore always rolls down the university roles; a university tenant rolls down only vacant roles. University-wide items (no institution) roll to the next university officer (for example a vacant Vice-Chancellor → Registrar).
3. **Preference order.** Each missing role has an ordered list of stand-ins per context (college, school, university-wide) and kind; the first stand-in with an active holder is used, and stand-ins themselves roll down if vacant. A loop or an empty list gives **UNRESOLVED**: the item is shown to the level above, which must assign someone.
4. **Who can change it** (`ROLLDOWN_OVERRIDE_SET`, logged with a reason): **Management**; the **Governing Body Approver only where there is no Management** (Changed in V4.0: this is the one right the Governing Body Approver gains beyond C13); in a university tenant the **Vice-Chancellor** (university-wide and every institution under it) and the **University Admin** (non-approval actions only). They may assign another stand-in for all of a role's actions of one kind or for one action, or **withhold** a non-approval action until the role is filled. An approval is never withheld — a request would wait forever.
5. **Who can see it** (`ROLLDOWN_VIEW`): the setters above, the College / School Admin and the Principal / School Principal.
6. **Standalone go-live.** In a standalone college or school, the Principal approves activating the institution (INSTITUTION_ACTIVATE rolls down from the Vice-Chancellor), after the Admin has finished setup and set the Principal's-leave approver (C7); the tenant then goes live through TENANT_ACTIVATE after payment. This closes finding V4-F-31.

### V4-19.2 Guards that no override can change

| ID | Guard | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| RD-G1 | No self-approval | A stand-in never decides their own request; the step goes to the next stand-in, else the level above [D-002]. |
| RD-G2 | Preparer is never the approver | If roll-down makes the preparer of an item also its approver, the approval goes to the next stand-in, else the level above [AP-04, C3]. |
| RD-G3 | Two steps on one person collapse | If two consecutive steps of one chain land on the same person, that person decides once; the step is recorded as COLLAPSED (V3.3: "one Principal approval is enough" [R2-03]). |
| RD-G4 | Own-leave approvers never roll down | The Principal's, Vice-Chancellor's and Data Protection Contact's own leave keep their named approver (Management or Governing Body Approver); the go-live gate is unchanged [C6, C7, V4-DB-01]. |
| RD-G5 | Never to personal or platform roles | Students, parents, applicants, the Governing Body Approver and platform roles are never stand-ins; roll-down never crosses an institution or tenant boundary. |
| RD-G6 | Limits of the stand-in stay | IT roles still assign non-sensitive roles only [MX-04]; a stand-in using a sensitive action must use two-step login; separation-of-duties pairs (Deliverable 3) still apply. |
| RD-G7 | Always visible and logged | Every action taken through roll-down records "acting for <role>" (approval_step.acting_for_role, audit entry) and the screen shows an "Acting for …" badge. |
| RD-G8 | Authority returns automatically | When someone is appointed to the missing role, new items go to them; pending approvals move to them and the Admin is warned [WF-26]. |

## Document control

Version 3.0 is the single, final master specification of EDU 360, and the master copy of everything written so far. It keeps every line of Version 1.0 and of the three original source files. Version 1.0 merged and replaced those files, resolved every contradiction between them, and added the workflows, rules and roles that were missing. Version 3.0 also applies all 447 decisions in *EDU 360 – Final Decisions v1.1*, the answers to its open items, the Version 2.1 change sheet, and the action list per role with its 11 answered questions. Where a decision changed an earlier sentence, only that sentence was changed, and the change is marked in place. Nothing else was removed. Version 3.1 adds, on top of Version 3.0, the 82 answers of the Phase 1 Requirements Clarification (EDU 360 Phase 1 Structured Requirements & Decision Register, 23 October 2026). Each answer is written where it applies and marked “Added in 3.1” with its ID [PQ-01 to PQ-82]; all 82 are listed in Section 27. No Version 3.0 wording was removed or reworded; only the version labels changed. Version 3.2 adds the answers to the review questions of 26 October 2026 (D-001 to D-003, F-3 to F-15 and OI-A; Section 19.13): a changed rule keeps its old wording beside a “Changed in 3.2” note, and new rules are marked “Added in 3.2” or “(3.2)”. EDU 360 v1 launches in India for universities, colleges and schools together. It is built in three phases. **How to read this document**

- Sections 1–5 explain what EDU 360 is, for whom, why it exists and what it covers.
- Sections 6–7 define who the users are: roles, permission letters and the binding business rules every approval follows. Where a workflow and a rule seem to differ, Section 7 wins.
- Sections 8–10 define the modules, what each role gets (features by role), and the full master permission matrix.
- Sections 11–14 give the screen-level, step-by-step workflow of every role, grouped by Platform, University, College and School.
- Sections 15–18 cover notifications, architecture, non-functional requirements (final targets) and terms (glossary).
- Section 19 lists every decision taken while merging the sources and since, with the change log, so nothing is changed silently.
- Sections 20–25 (new in 2.0): default formulas, pass/fail checks, privacy, testing, commercial decisions, and later phases with open items.
- Section 26 (new in 3.0): the action list per role – every action, who may do it, and its limits.
- Section 27 (new in 3.1): the Phase 1 requirement rules – all 82 decisions of the Phase 1 decision register, with their status and where each applies.

**Conventions used**

- Decision IDs in brackets (for example [AP-11], [R2-01]) trace each rule back to the decision behind it.
- Each workflow step lists **Action** (what the user clicks), **Impact** (what changes in the system) and **Affects** (which roles or records feel the change).
- “Admin” on its own means the administrator of the current level: University Admin, College Admin or School Admin. Added in 3.2: “Tenant Admin” means the top Admin of the tenant – the University Admin in a university tenant, the College Admin or School Admin in a standalone tenant [F-12]. Version markers – (new), (changed), (added), (v2.1), (V3), (3.1), (3.2), “Changed in 2.0”, “Added in 3.1”, “Changed in 3.2” and “Added in 3.2” – all name the version in which an item was added or changed; earlier markers are kept as written [F-15]. **Changed in 3.3 [A9]:** Changed in 3.3: Changed in 3.3 marks every Version 3.3 change, including additions.
- “Configurable” means each institution sets its own value; the default shown is what a new institution starts with. Values marked *proposed* in Version 1.0 were defaults chosen during merging; each institution can change them in configuration, and the final values are in Sections 17 and 20.
- *(Phase 2)* and *(Phase 3)* mark rules built in that phase; “Later phase” means not in v1 (Section 25).
- *(added)* marks roles or items Version 1.0 added from the permission tables, the extended modules or the workflows; *(new)* and *(changed)* mark what later versions added or changed; *(v2.1)* and *(V3)* mark changes from those versions.

## 1. Introduction

**EDU 360** is a comprehensive education management platform that centralizes the academic, administrative, financial and human resource operations of universities, colleges and schools in one unified system.

The platform lets institutions manage students, faculty, staff, courses, attendance, examinations, results, fees, payroll, leave and institutional communication through secure, role-based dashboards. EDU 360 supports structured institutional hierarchies, so a university can oversee many colleges and schools while keeping full operational control and data integrity.

EDU 360 provides complete lifecycle management for students and employees: admissions, academic tracking, attendance, examinations, performance evaluation, salary management, leave management and service records. Faculty and staff payroll, leave approvals, workload monitoring and compliance reporting are handled in the same ecosystem. *(Changed in 2.0: payroll and salary management are Phase 2 [OB-02]; admissions is Phase 2; workload and performance monitoring of staff moved to a later phase [OB-03, OB-04].)*

The platform brings academic administration, HR management, finance, communication and reporting into one system. This reduces operational complexity and removes dependence on many disconnected tools. Built for enterprise-grade security, audit readiness and scalability, EDU 360 gives educational institutions reliable, compliant and future-ready digital governance, with security controls tested before launch (Section 23).

EDU 360 acts as the **single source of truth** for each institution, enabling transparent operations, efficient management and better academic outcomes for every stakeholder.

**Product shape (final)**

- **Delivery:** a multi-tenant SaaS product run by the Product Owner, sold on subscription plans (Section 24).
- **Market:** India only in v1; prices in INR. The design must allow other countries to be added later [PR-01].
- **Customers (tenants):** a university together with its colleges and schools, or a standalone college, or a standalone school. All three launch together [PR-02].
- **Access:** one responsive web application used on desktop, tablet and phone browsers, installable on phones, with push notifications [OB-13]. It needs internet; forms save drafts so nothing is lost when the connection drops [PR-03]. There are no separate native Android or iOS apps in v1.
- **School model:** school students do not log in. Their parent or guardian is their digital representative. Exception: a school may switch on login for chosen classes (for example 9–12). Those students see only timetable, homework, study material, attendance and results; no messaging, fees or leave [PR-04, R2-39]. **Changed in 3.3 [A10, Wording (PR-04)]:** (Changed in 3.3: only these, plus the actions listed for Student (School) in Section 26.)
- **College model:** college students and their parents both log in, each with their own access. All college students follow the same rules, whatever their age [PR-05].
- **Outside systems:** v1 exports files in the formats of Tally, UDISE+, AISHE and affiliating-university portals. Direct connections come later [PR-06].
- **Management:** private institutions get a Management role above the Principal (Section 6) [PR-07].
- **Language:** English only in v1 [CM-13].

## 2. Institutional and role hierarchy

EDU 360 runs on these levels: **System → Tenant (University / standalone College / standalone School) → Institution (College / School) → Department → Program → Year → Semester → Section → User** (schools: Class → Section). Version 1.0 described six levels: System → University → College / School → Department / Class → Section → User; Version 2.0 added the tenant, program and semester levels [HI-01, HI-02, RL-01]. Authority, responsibility and data visibility follow this tree. A role sees only its own branch and what sits below it, unless the permission matrix (Section 10) says otherwise.

&#91;embedded content: EDU 360 hierarchy · platform, tenant, college and school branches]

In words (added in 3.2): the Product Owner and the platform staff (Platform Admin, Billing Manager, Support, Release Manager, Data Protection Officer) sit outside every tenant. Each tenant has its own database and holds Management (owner or trust, sees all, sets approvals) and the Data Protection Contact. Under the University (Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Director, Controller of Examinations, University Admin, Accountant, HR Manager, governance roles) are two branches. College: Principal, Vice-Principal, College Admin, Accountant and non-teaching staff → Department (HOD, professors, support staff; Program → Year → Semester → Section) → Students who log in (sections and subject groups, a mentor for each) → Parents (up to 3 guardians: monitor, pay fees, apply for leave). School: School Principal, Vice-Principal, School Admin, Accountant, support staff → Class (Class Teacher, Subject Teachers, sections A to N, no departments) → Students (no login by default; optional view-only login for chosen classes) → Parents (up to 3 guardians, the child's digital representative). A standalone college or school is its own tenant, without the University level. **Changed in 3.3 [A11, C6, C13]:** (Changed in 3.3: and, where there is no Management, the Governing Body Approver, who only approves the Principal's, the Vice-Chancellor's or a dedicated Data Protection Contact's own leave [C6, C13].)

The platform team (the Product Owner's company) sits outside every tenant; inside a tenant, Management and the Data Protection Contact sit beside the university, and colleges and schools branch from the university down to students and parents.

### 2.1 Structure rules

- **Subject groups:** a subject can be taught to a group that mixes students from several sections (electives) [HI-05].
- **Several assignments:** one staff member can hold several assignments (departments, institutions), each with its own scope [HI-06]. Added in 3.1: the staff record is kept separate from the login, so one person with several assignments has one account and never a duplicate; each assignment keeps its own separately scoped roles [PQ-13, PQ-28].
- **Year-end promotion:** the Admin runs bulk promotion; the Principal approves; failed or detained students are left out with a reason [HI-03]. Repeating a year is not supported in v1 [HI-04]. A detained student stays in the same year and section with status “Detained” until repeating is supported (open item 6).
- **Parents:** one parent login shows all their children inside the same tenant; a child in another tenant needs a separate login [HI-07].
- **Staff who are also parents:** two separate accounts. The staff account logs in with email and password; the parent account with a mobile one-time code. The same mobile number may be on both [HI-08, R2-16].
- **Colleges and schools under a university** stay as written [HI-09].
- **External university mode:** a college whose university is not on EDU 360 enters or imports external marks itself and publishes after Principal approval [HI-10].
- **Standalone tenants:** a standalone college or school has the same tree without the University level. Its College Admin or School Admin takes over the university-level duties (academic calendar, policies; result publishing in colleges – Section 7.1). Its Principal holds final approval. *(Changed in 2.0: the fee policy is set by Management, or by the Principal if there is no Management role; the Accountant builds the fee structure; the Principal approves it [HI-11].)*
- A standalone college can later join a university tenant; the platform team moves its data on request [RL-02].

## 3. Objectives

The primary objective of EDU 360 is to provide a unified, secure and scalable education management platform that centralizes the academic, administrative, financial and human resource operations of educational institutions in one integrated system. The objectives are grouped below for clarity and implementation alignment. Items moved to a later phase by a decision are kept and marked.

**3.1 Centralization of institutional operations.** Centralize all institutional activities (academic management, staff administration, finance, library services, placement activities and communication) in one digital platform. This removes dependence on disconnected systems and creates a single source of truth for all institutional data.

**3.2 Support for a structured institutional hierarchy.** Implement a hierarchical model that represents real educational institutions, supporting:

- System-level governance
- Tenant-level management (university, standalone college or standalone school) *(new)* [RL-01]
- University-level control
- College- and school-level management
- Department-level administration
- Program, year, semester, class- and section-level academic operations
- Student- and parent-level access

This ensures that authority, responsibility and data visibility follow institutional boundaries.

**3.3 Role-based access control and data security.** Enforce strict role-based access control (RBAC) where:

- Every user can access only the data their role and scope permit.
- Academic, financial, administrative and governance functions are logically isolated.
- Conflicts of authority are prevented through permission boundaries.
- Approval power comes only from approval chains, and nobody approves their own request [RL-03, AP-04].
- Audit readiness and accountability are maintained across all actions; every action is auditable.

**3.4 Academic management automation.** Automate and manage academic processes:

- Attendance tracking
- Examination scheduling
- Marks entry and result publishing
- Academic performance monitoring
- Timetable and syllabus access
- Assignment and study material management

This ensures accuracy, efficiency and transparency in academic operations.

**3.5 Student lifecycle management.** Provide complete lifecycle management for students:

- Admission *(added from the Admissions module; Phase 2)*
- Academic tracking
- Attendance history
- Examination records
- Result history
- Fee payments and receipts
- Leave application and approval tracking
- Assignment submissions and learning materials
- Graduation and alumni record *(added from the Alumni module; Phase 3)*

This ensures continuous academic visibility from admission to completion and beyond.

**3.6 Faculty and staff management.** Manage faculty and staff records:

- Staff profiles and service records
- Workload monitoring *(later phase [OB-03])*
- Leave management and approvals
- Payroll and salary processing *(Phase 2)*
- Performance monitoring *(later phase [OB-04])*

This ensures effective human resource administration within the institution.

**3.7 Financial management and transparency.** Manage institutional financial activities:

- Fee policy and fee structure management
- Scholarship handling and concessions
- Installment tracking
- Payment and receipt generation
- Payroll processing *(Phase 2)*
- Financial reporting

This ensures transparency, accountability and audit readiness.

**3.8 Placement and career support management** *(Phase 2)*. Support placement operations:

- Company profile management
- Job posting management
- Student eligibility mapping
- Application tracking
- Interview scheduling
- Offer letter management
- Placement reporting

This ensures structured career support for students.

**3.9 Library resource management** *(Phase 2)*. Manage library operations:

- Book catalog management
- Issue and return tracking
- Reservation handling
- Fine calculation
- Digital library records
- Inventory auditing
- Damaged and lost book tracking

This ensures efficient use of, and accountability for, learning resources.

**3.10 Institutional communication.** Provide official communication channels:

- Notices
- Notifications (in-app and push)
- Email and SMS alerts
- Student and parent messaging
- Community feed *(added from the workflows)*

This ensures reliable and traceable institutional communication.

**3.11 Governance, compliance and audit readiness.** Support governance and compliance through:

- Audit logs
- Compliance reporting
- Accreditation documentation
- Approval workflows
- Data protection enforcement

This keeps the institution legally compliant and accreditation-ready.

**3.12 Monitoring and reporting.** Provide reporting and monitoring:

- Academic performance reports
- Attendance summaries
- Examination overviews
- Financial reports
- Institutional performance reports
- Activity logs

This enables informed decisions at every management level.

**3.13 Scalability and future readiness.** Design EDU 360 as a scalable platform that supports:

- Multiple universities
- Multiple colleges and schools
- A growing user base
- Feature expansion
- Other countries later (India only in v1) [PR-01]
- Long-term digital governance

**3.14 Single source of truth.** Establish EDU 360 as the authoritative system for all institutional information, ensuring:

- Data consistency
- Data accuracy
- Controlled access
- Long-term data integrity

### 3.15 Product KPIs [OB-01, MK-19]

| KPI | Formula (Section 20) | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weekly active teachers % | Teachers who logged in in the last 7 days ÷ active teacher accounts × 100 | Set after the pilot term |
| Parents who log in % | Parents who logged in in the last 30 days ÷ parent accounts × 100 | Set after the pilot term |
| Fees paid online % | Amount paid online ÷ total amount paid × 100 | Set after the pilot term |
| Trial-to-paid % | Trials that became paid ÷ trials that ended × 100 | Set after the pilot term |

Scope is now also split by release phase: Phase 1 is v1; Phase 2 and 3 are fully specified and built later; Section 25 lists everything deliberately left out [OB-02]. Sections 4.1–4.4 keep the full functional scope from Version 1.0, with each item's phase marked; Sections 4.5–4.8 give the phase summary.

## 5. System overview

EDU 360 is an enterprise-grade, multi-tenant digital system that manages and governs the complete operational lifecycle of educational institutions. It combines academic administration, human resource management, financial operations, library services, placement management, institutional communication and governance in one ecosystem, and acts as each tenant's **single source of truth**: data stays consistent, secure and transparent at every level.

**5.1 Platform structure.** The system is hierarchical and multi-tenant. It gives centralized governance while each institution operates independently. The hierarchy is: System → Tenant → Institution (College / School) → Department → Program → Year → Semester → Section → User (schools: Class → Section). *(Version 1.0: System → University → College / School → Department → Class / Section → User.)* Each level works within defined authority boundaries, which control data access and operational responsibility.

**5.2 User-centric role architecture.** Every user is assigned one or more roles. The role decides:

- Functional access
- Data visibility
- Approval authority (only through its place in approval chains [RL-03])
- Reporting scope

Roles are grouped into Platform roles, Governance roles, Academic roles, Administrative roles, Support roles, and Student and Parent roles (full catalog in Section 6). A user may hold more than one role (for example a Professor who is also HOD). *(Changed in 2.0: access is no longer the union of those roles.)* Each role keeps its own scope, and the user gets each (role + scope) pair, never a wider mix [HI-14]. The user works in one role at a time with a role switcher; the active role shows in the header and in every audit log entry [HI-15]. Institution Admins can also build fully custom roles (Section 6.3) from the actions in Section 26.

**5.2.1 Active-role switcher — functional rules (added V4.0).** The switcher lets a signed-in user move between their own existing (role + scope) assignments. It is a self-service control, separate from USER_ROLE_ASSIGN/RP-04 (an Admin assigning a role to another user, Section 26.5) — the two must never be combined into one dropdown, and the switcher never creates, assigns or grants a role.

1. The active role and its scope are always shown in the application header.
2. The role dropdown appears only when the user has more than one eligible (role + scope) assignment. With exactly one assignment, the header shows that role with no switch control.
3. Each option in the dropdown identifies both the role and its scope, e.g. "HOD — Computer Science Department" or "Professor — ABC College", so that the same role held in two institutions or departments is still distinguishable.
4. Selecting an option switches to that exact assignment (by assignment ID), not merely to a role name.
5. The server validates, before switching, that the target assignment: belongs to the signed-in user, is active (not expired or revoked), and is within the correct tenant and scope [PQ-17].
6. On a successful switch the system issues an updated token/session context and refreshes the dashboard, navigation, permissions and any page data bound to the previous role — nothing from the previous role's context is retained [PQ-17].
7. On a failed switch (invalid, expired, revoked, or not-owned assignment) the previous valid context is kept active and a clear error is shown; the user is never left with no active role.
8. Every switch — successful or denied — is recorded in the audit trail with both the previous and new assignment context (Section 16.5, Section 21).

**5.3 Modular design.** The system is divided into independent but integrated modules:

- Academic Management
- Student Lifecycle Management
- Faculty and Staff Management
- Financial Management
- Placement Management *(Phase 2)*
- Library Management *(Phase 2)*
- Leave Management
- Communication
- Reporting and Analytics
- Governance and Compliance
- Extended modules: Admissions *(Phase 2)*, Alumni, Hostel, Transport, Research and Publications, API and Integration Governance *(Phase 3)*

Each module works independently while sharing data through the tenant's central database. The Product Owner can switch modules on or off per plan and per tenant. The full list of 29 modules by phase is in Section 8.

**5.4 Data integration and consistency.** All modules use a common data model, which ensures:

- No data duplication
- Real-time data synchronization
- Cross-module reporting
- Historical record preservation

**5.5 Governance and control.** EDU 360 enforces governance through role-based access control, approval chains, audit logs, compliance reporting and data protection enforcement. This ensures operational accountability and regulatory readiness.

**5.6 Institutional operational coverage.**

- Tenant level: Management oversight and data protection *(new)*
- University level: centralized governance
- College and school level: academic and administrative management
- Department level: academic delivery control
- Class level: teaching and learning activities
- Student and parent level: monitoring and participation

**5.7 Communication framework.** Official channels: institutional notices, system notifications (in-app and push), email and SMS alerts, direct messaging between authorized users within the rules of Section 7.10, and the community feed. All communication is transparent and traceable.

**5.8 Reporting and decision support.** Structured reports cover academic performance, attendance, examination results, financial status, institutional performance and activity audits, as fixed reports with filters and PDF / Excel export. Each report is limited to the user's role and authority level. A buyer dashboard serves Management, Principal, Registrar and Vice-Chancellor [MK-11].

**5.9 Scalability and extensibility.** The system supports many institutions on one platform, a growing user base, new features, other countries later, and long-term digital transformation.

**5.10 Operational philosophy.** EDU 360 is a governance platform, not only a management system. It is built for transparency, accountability, operational efficiency, academic quality improvement and institutional compliance.

## 6. Tenants, institutions, roles and permission letters

A **tenant** is one paying customer with its own isolated data: a university (with all its colleges and schools), a standalone college, or a standalone school. The Product Owner and platform staff sit outside every tenant and never see a tenant's academic, financial or personal data. Colleges and schools inside a tenant are institutions. Four roles are added, alumni login is removed, and institution Admins can build fully custom roles. Approval power never comes from a permission letter: it comes only from the approval chains in Section 7.

### 6.1 Tenant and institution [RL-01]

- A **tenant** is the paying customer: a university (or group) with everything under it, a standalone college, or a standalone school. Each tenant has its own database by default; tenants on small plans share one database with row-level security [TE-01]. Added in 3.1: the design also allows new kinds of education providers to be added later without restructuring existing school and college records; these are extensibility targets, not Phase 1 launch scope [PQ-02].
- Colleges and schools inside a tenant are **institutions**. They share the tenant's database but each sees only its own data.
- Only tenants are billed and suspended, and only by the platform. A University Admin can only **block** an institution's access, and only with Vice-Chancellor approval [WF-15].
- A standalone college can later join a university tenant; the platform team moves its data on request [RL-02].
- The platform team (Product Owner and platform roles) sits outside every tenant and never sees a tenant's academic, financial or personal data. The only exception: Support may view one ticket's data read-only for 24 hours when the tenant Admin grants it; every view is logged and the tenant can withdraw it [WF-11].

### 6.2 Permission letters [RL-03, RL-04]

| Letter | Meaning | What it allows in practice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F – Full | Create, view, edit, delete within scope. No approving | Owns the records of the area: e.g. Librarian F on Library manages the whole catalog |
| M – Manage | Create, view, edit day-to-day records. No setup, no approving | Runs daily operations: e.g. Faculty M on Attendance marks attendance |
| C – Configure *(new)* | Set up rules and settings for the area | e.g. attendance rules, exam patterns, grading bands, library settings. In the matrix, Admin cells for Attendance, Exams, Academic and Library are “M + C” |
| A – Approve | View, and approve or reject what others submit | Only at the step the approval chain gives the role |
| V – View | Read within scope | Scope limits apply, e.g. a teacher sees only assigned students |
| R – Request | Submit requests for yourself or your child and track them | e.g. leave, certificate requests, record corrections |
| N – No access | Area hidden | Menu items do not appear |

**Version 1.0 legend, kept for reference:** F – Full Access: create, view, edit, delete, configure and approve within their scope; M – Manage: create, view and edit day-to-day records, no configuration of policy, no final approval; A – Approve: view, and approve or reject what others submit, cannot create or edit the records; V – View Only: read within their scope; R – Request: submit requests for themselves (or their child) and track them; N – No Access: the area is hidden. *(Changed in 2.0 [RL-03, RL-04]: F no longer includes configuring or approving; configuring is the new letter C; approving comes only from approval chains.)*

- **Approval power comes only from the approval chains in Section 7.** F and M never include approving [RL-03]. A combined cell such as “M + A” means the role does both, at the chain step it holds.
- **The letter table is a summary.** Developers build from a detailed action list per role (for example MARKS_ENTER, MARKS_APPROVE_HOD, RESULT_PUBLISH, ATTENDANCE_MARK, FEE_STRUCTURE_CREATE) [RL-05]. The full list is Section 26 and the Action List V3.2 Excel. **Changed in 3.3 [A14, Letter gaps, R-1]:** Replace label: “Action List V3.3”. Add: “Changed in 3.3: every non-N letter is backed by at least one action; an action includes the reads it needs (R-1). Cells with no backing action are N.”
- **Restrictions win.** Where a letter and a role's Restrictions line disagree, the action list follows the Restrictions line. Example: an Admin with M on Exams can set up and monitor exams but cannot enter marks [R2-18].

### 6.3 Custom roles [R2-02]

- Institution Admins can create fully custom roles and give any right to any role, including new roles. Rights are picked from the actions in Section 26. **Changed in 3.3 [A15, C4]:** Changed in 3.3: the University Admin can also build custom roles, for university-office roles only (ROLE_CUSTOM_MANAGE) [C4].
- The standard roles and the permission matrix (Section 10) are the starting template every new institution receives.
- Every rights change is logged and the Principal / Management is notified (safeguard for the accepted risk in Section 25.2).
- Approval chains still apply: a custom role can sit in a chain only where the institution places it, and nobody approves their own request.
- This replaces the earlier rule that tenants cannot change role rights.

Added in 3.2: an institution with nobody above the Principal names a person, such as a trustee, as a Management-type user to approve the Principal's own leave [D-002, OI-A] <br>**Changed in 3.3 [A16, C6, C9, C13, answer 1]:** Changed in 3.3: that person is now the Governing Body Approver role (below), not a Management-type user. Management is a governing body, not staff: it has no self-service, own-leave-cancel or policy-acceptance actions and is not part of All tenant staff [C6, C9, C13]. Apply the same note in §8.1 Edge cases, §13.17 row Security Supervisor, Housekeeping Supervisor, Driver and Section 26.2

All other role assignment is done by the Admin [MX-04, open item 9].

### 6.7 Role name standards

- “Library Admin” in the source is the **Librarian**.
- “Examination Controller” and “Controller of Exams” are the **Controller of Examinations**.
- “Faculty” and “Teacher / Faculty” in college workflows mean any of Professor, Associate Professor or Assistant Professor.
- **Mentor / “Class Coordinator”** is an assignment given by the HOD to a faculty member for one class or section, not a separate role. It carries final approval for short student leave.
- “Accountant” without a level means the College Accountant or School Accountant of that institution.

## 7. Business rules and approval chains

These rules are binding. Every workflow in Sections 11–14 follows them. Approvers approve or reject only, leave approval depends on how long the leave is, and nobody ever approves their own request. A rejection ends the request, and every step notifies the requester (and the parent, where a student is involved).

### 7.0 How every approval works

- **Approve or reject only.** There is no “send back” [R2-01]. A remark is required on reject and optional on approve [AP-24]. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 let each step approve, reject with a mandatory remark, or send back.)*
- **A rejection ends the request.** The requester may submit a new one; the old one stays in history [AP-02]. Rejected marks are entered again as a new submission.
- **Bulk approval.** Approvers can select many requests and approve them together with one optional comment; each item is logged separately [AP-25]. **Changed in 3.3 [A28, C12, answer 3]:** Changed in 3.3: the Quality Assurance, Legal and Compliance Officers and the Research Coordinator can also bulk-approve. Data Protection Officer approvals (full-tenant exports, deletions, retention changes) are never bulk-approved; each is reviewed on its own [C12].
- **No automatic movement.** If an approver does not act, the system sends reminders only. A request never moves on by itself [AP-03].
- **No self-approval.** Nobody approves their own request or acts at two steps of the same request. The system skips them to the next approver and logs why [AP-04]. If the approver at a step is the requester, that step is skipped [AP-05]. Added in 3.1: this holds even when a user has several roles or assignments [PQ-18]. Added in 3.2: there is no exception, including the Principal's own leave (Section 7.1) [D-002].
- **Simultaneous action.** If two approvers act at the same moment, the first one wins; the second sees “already actioned by <name>” [TE-09].
- **Deactivated approvers.** When a user is deactivated, their pending approvals move to whoever now holds that role, and the Admin is warned [WF-26].
- **Every decision is logged** with the approver, active role, time, remark and the request's before / after state. Added in 3.1: institutions may configure chain steps, approvers and escalation only within these fixed security and approval rules; no configuration can allow self-approval or widen anyone's scope [PQ-04, PQ-16].

**Delegation** [AP-06 to AP-10]

- Any approver can hand over approvals to a same-or-higher role for set dates. Added in 3.2: the one exception is the designated deputy – a Principal (College) may delegate to the Vice-Principal (College), and a School Principal to the Vice-Principal (School). The Principal chooses all approvals or chosen processes; AP-07 to AP-10 still apply; the deputy never acts on a request they raised, are the subject of or already acted on [AP-04]; Management is notified when a delegation starts and ends; without a Vice-Principal, same-or-higher applies. No other lower-role pairs exist, for example HOD → Professor [D-001]. **Changed in 3.3 [A29, C12, answer 3]:** Changed in 3.3: the governance approvers (Quality Assurance, Legal and Compliance Officers), the Research Coordinator and the Data Protection Officer can delegate; the Data Protection Officer only to another Data Protection Officer. Merit-list approval can never be delegated [C12, answer 3, WF-37].
- The delegate gets the approval right for those dates only, and it is logged [AP-07].
- A delegate cannot delegate again [AP-08].
- When the delegation ends, pending items go back to the original approver.
- The approver can cancel a delegation at any time; this is logged.
- The Vice-Principal can approve on the Principal's behalf when the Principal delegates (for a date range or a process), and the audit log records the delegation. (Confirmed in 3.2 as the designated-deputy exception above [D-001].)

### 7.1 Approval chains

&#91;embedded content: Main approval chains · leave, results, fees, payroll]

In words (added in 3.2): college student leave goes from the student or parent to the mentor (final up to 2 days; from 3.2 the mentor only forwards longer leave), the HOD (final for 3–7 days) and the Principal (final over 7 days). School student leave goes from the parent to the Class Teacher (final up to 3 days) and the School Principal (final over 3 days). College results: faculty enter and submit → HOD approves or rejects → Principal approves or rejects → Controller publishes. School results: Subject Teacher enters → Class Teacher reviews → School Principal approves or rejects → Principal or Admin publishes. Fee structure: Finance Director sets the fee policy → Accountant builds within its ranges → Principal approves → the structure goes live and locks at session start. Payroll (Phase 2): Payroll Officer generates → HR Manager verifies → Principal approves totals only → payslips released. Every step is approve or reject only; a rejection ends the request; nobody approves their own request.

Highlighted boxes are where a decision becomes final; for leave, the request stops at the first highlighted approver its length allows. The tables below list every chain.

**Leave**

| Process | Chain | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Student leave (college) | Student or parent applies → mentor / class coordinator → HOD → Principal. The request stops at the final approver for its length: **up to 2 days – mentor final; 3–7 days – HOD final; more than 7 days – Principal final** | Day limits configurable. College Admin monitors only [AP-11, AP-13]. Added in 3.2: for leave over 2 days the mentor only forwards the request, with an optional remark the HOD sees, and cannot reject it [F-11]. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 routed every request Faculty recommends → HOD approves → Principal final.)* |
| Student leave (school) | Parent applies → Class Teacher → School Principal. **Up to 3 days – Class Teacher final; longer – School Principal final** | Configurable. School Admin monitors only [AP-12] |
| Faculty leave (college) | Faculty applies → HOD recommends → Principal approves | HOD or Principal assigns a substitute [LV-11] |
| HOD's own leave | HOD applies → Principal approves | [AP-21] |
| Admin and Accountant leave (college) | Staff applies → HR verifies → Principal approves | [AP-21] |
| Other non-teaching staff leave (college) | Staff applies → HR Manager verifies → Principal approves | Same in a standalone tenant |
| Teacher leave (school) | Teacher applies → School Principal approves | Leave balance checked; loss of pay warned [AP-22, R2-09] |
| School Admin, School Accountant and school support staff leave *(v2.1)* | Staff applies → School Principal approves | No HR step in schools; leave balance checked and loss of pay warned |
| University staff leave | Staff applies → University HR Manager verifies → Registrar approves | [RL-09] |
| Principal's own leave | Principal applies → Management, Registrar or Vice-Chancellor (set per institution) | Self-approval only when nobody is above the Principal; logged and visible to Management [R2-04] (Changed in 3.2: no self-approval. The approver must be set before go-live and be a different person from the Principal; a missing approver blocks the request – never skipped or auto-approved – and the Admin and Management are warned; with nobody above the Principal, the institution names a person such as a trustee as a Management-type user [D-002, OI-A].) <br>**Changed in 3.3 [A30, C6, C7, C13]:** (Changed in 3.3: the approver is Management where it exists, otherwise the Governing Body Approver; a college or school under a university may instead set the Registrar or Vice-Chancellor. The approver is set by the Admin, or by the University Admin for institutions under a university (PRINCIPAL_LEAVE_APPROVER_SET), and must be set before every institution goes live – INSTITUTION_ACTIVATE refuses activation without it. The trustee becomes the Governing Body Approver [C6, C7, C13, answer 6].) |
| Vice-Principal's own leave (3.2) | Vice-Principal applies → Principal approves | College and school [F-11] |
| University staff leave, including the Finance Director and the Controller of Examinations (3.2) | Staff applies → University HR Manager verifies → Registrar approves | Same chain as university staff leave [RL-09, F-11] |
| Registrar's own leave (3.2) | Registrar applies → University HR Manager verifies → Vice-Chancellor approves (SENIOR_LEAVE_APPROVE) | [F-11] |
| Vice-Chancellor's own leave (3.2) | Vice-Chancellor applies → Management approves (SENIOR_LEAVE_APPROVE); where there is no Management, a designated approver must be set | Never self-approved; blocked if no approver [F-11, OI-A] <br>**Changed in 3.3 [A31, C6, C7]:** (Changed in 3.3: where there is no Management, the Governing Body Approver approves. The University Admin sets the approver (VC_LEAVE_APPROVER_SET); tenant go-live checks it [C6, C7, answer 6].) |

| Management (3.2) | No leave workflow | Management is a governing body, not staff [F-11] |
