### 7.2 Leave rules

- **Who applies:** a college student or their parent can apply. A school student's leave is always applied by the parent.
- **Leave types** are configurable per institution by the College or School Admin (letter C) [Q8]. Defaults – students: Sick, Personal, On-duty; staff: Casual, Sick, Earned, Maternity / Paternity, Duty, Loss of pay [LV-01].
- **Units:** full day, half day or per period [LV-02].
- **Late application:** leave can be applied up to 3 days after the absence (configurable) [LV-03].
- **Documents:** a medical note or other document can be uploaded on any leave; never required in v1 [R2-10]. **Changed in 3.3 [A37, Letter gaps]:** (Changed in 3.3: leave actions that can carry a medical attachment are marked sensitive in the Action List; every view is logged [PQ-66].)
- **Overlaps:** a request that overlaps an existing one is blocked, and the existing request is shown [LV-05].
- **Parents of college students** are notified of every request and every decision [LV-06].
- **Cancelling:** before the start date the requester can cancel; after it, cancelling needs the final approver [LV-07].
- **Counting days:** weekends and holidays inside a leave are not counted, using the calendar. Institutions can switch on a “sandwich” rule [LV-08].
- **Staff balances:** HR (in schools, the School Admin) credits a yearly number per leave type. No carry-forward or encashment. The system checks the balance and warns; loss of pay is flagged and HR (in schools, the School Admin) confirms it before payroll [R2-09, LV-10]. The leave year is the calendar year by default (configurable) [WF-32].
- **Substitutes:** when approving staff leave, the HOD or Principal assigns a substitute, who can mark attendance for those dates [LV-11].
- **On duty** (sports, placement drives) is treated as approved leave [LV-12].
- **Effect on attendance:** approved leave does not count against attendance %; making this configurable is a later phase [LV-13].
- **States:** Draft → Pending (current approver named) → Approved or Rejected; Cancelled. A requester can cancel while it is pending.
- **On final approval** attendance adjusts automatically: the days are marked “On approved leave” instead of “Absent”.
- **Absence without approved leave** is flagged “Unapproved absence” and the parent is alerted.
- **Approved staff leave** updates the HR record and feeds payroll *(Phase 2)*: loss of pay when the leave balance is exhausted.

### 7.3 Attendance rules

- **View only:** students and parents have view-only access to attendance.
- **Who marks:** only the faculty or teacher assigned to that subject, class and section, or a substitute assigned by the HOD or Admin for that date [AT-03].
- **How often:** college – once per subject period. School – twice a day by the teacher; per period is optional [AT-01].
- **Window:** attendance can be marked until midnight the same day; after that only through a correction request (Section 7.1) [AT-02]. Any change after submission goes through a correction request.
- **Statuses:** Present, Absent, On approved leave, Not held. “Late” is removed everywhere, including reports; old “Late” marks import as Present [R2-23, open item 13 of the Version 2.0 list, Section 19.3]. A teacher or HOD marks a cancelled period “Not held”; it is left out of the percentage [AT-12].
- **Percentage:** configurable per institution, starting from the default formula in Section 20 [AT-05, R2-37].
- **Minimum attendance:** configurable per subject and overall, set by the College Admin or School Admin in attendance rules [AT-06].
- **Alerts:** an in-app alert per subject, sent immediately and only when the student is absent, plus one SMS summary per day [AT-07, R2-36].
- **Term lock:** the Principal locks the term; then no attendance or marks can change. Unlocking needs the Principal and a reason, is logged, lasts at most 3 days and relocks automatically; the HOD and Admin are notified [R2-08, AT-09].
- **Bulk upload:** allowed for the assigned teacher, or for the Admin with Principal approval [AT-11].
- **Not supported:** attendance shortage condonation [AT-08].
- Every change keeps the original value, the new value and both users in the audit log.

### 7.4 Exam and result rules

- **Who owns what (university):** the Registrar owns programs and exam rules. The Controller of Examinations runs exam schedules, the marks process and result publishing [R2-06].
- **Exam schedules:** the Controller schedules university exams. The College Admin or Examination Clerk schedules internal exams within the calendar; either can do it [WF-18].
- **Exam patterns and grading:** the Admin configures patterns (internal / external split, grading system) within the Registrar's rules (university) or the Principal's (standalone). *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 named the Controller of Examinations as owner of the rules [R2-06].)* Grading is absolute, with configurable grade bands [EX-16]; GPA / CGPA use the configurable grading scheme (Section 20). **Changed in 3.3 [A38, C5]:** (Changed in 3.3: in a standalone institution the Admin sets the exam patterns and grading scheme (EXAM_PATTERN_SET, GRADING_SCHEME_SET) with no approval step; the Principal is notified of every change, and every change is logged and versioned [C5].)
- **Marks states:** Draft (teacher can edit) → Submitted (locked for the teacher) → HOD Approved / Class Teacher Reviewed → Principal Approved → Published. Rejected → the teacher sees the remark and enters a new submission; faculty cannot edit marks after submitting [R2-01]. School: Draft → Submitted → Class Teacher Reviewed → Principal Approved → Published. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 locked marks for faculty only at HOD Approved, and had no Class Teacher review in schools.)*
- **Special codes:** AB (absent), MP (malpractice), WH (withheld), medical-absent [EX-02].
- **Checks:** marks above the maximum or below zero are blocked; a big jump from the previous exam shows a warning [EX-17].
- **External marks:** the Examination Clerk uploads them; the HOD checks them; they follow the same approval chain [EX-01].
- **Publishing:** results can be published only after the final approval. The Publish button stays disabled until then. Publishing notifies students and parents.
- **Withdrawing a published result:** the Controller (college on an EDU 360 university), the College Admin with Principal approval (standalone or external-university college [Q4]) or the School Principal (school) can withdraw it with a reason; everyone is notified; it is logged [EX-07].
- **Re-evaluation is not in v1.** Students and parents can only view results [R2-07]. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 allowed published results to change through a re-evaluation request approved by the same chain, with the change logged. Re-evaluation is a later phase; a published result can now only be withdrawn with a reason.)*
- **Backlogs:** backlog tracking and supplementary exam registration are in v1 [EX-08].
- **Hall tickets:** generated by the Examination Clerk or Admin; withheld for low attendance or any overdue fee amount, each check switchable [R2-20]. The Principal can override for one student with a reason; logged [EX-09].

### 7.5 Fee rules

**Policy and structure**

- The **fee policy** (fee heads, allowed ranges, scholarship schemes, refund and penalty policy) is set by the University Finance Director for the colleges and schools under the university, or in a standalone institution by Management (else the Principal). The University Accountant maintains the data. Refunds are not in v1 [R2-21].
- The College or School Accountant builds the **fee structure**, installments, scholarships and late-fee penalties inside the policy; the structure goes live only after the Principal approves it. The Admin and Principal can view collections.
- **Outside the policy range:** blocked. The Accountant can raise an exception request (Section 7.1) [R2-03].
- **Fee edits are allowed only before the academic session starts.** After that, the structure is locked. Scholarships, fines and concessions still work, each with an approval and an audit entry. A mid-session change needs a new structure version approved by the Principal. A new fee version mid-session applies to new admissions and future installments only; amounts already billed stay [FE-02].
- **Students joining mid-year:** full fee or pro-rata, configurable per fee head [FE-03].
- **One student account:** hostel, mess and transport fees are fee heads in the same student ledger, with one receipt series [FE-22]. Admission application fees are paid through the gateway into the ledger and carried to the student account on admission [FE-23].
- **Scholarship vs concession:** a scholarship is a scheme with rules for many students; a concession is a one-off discount for one student, approved by the Principal [FE-17].

**Payments**

- **Methods:** online through the payment gateway (Razorpay by default, INR) – whatever the gateway supports: UPI, cards, net banking, wallets [FE-30]; offline cash or cheque entered by the Accountant. A receipt is generated for every payment. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 had GST configurable; there is no tax on fees in v1 [R2-22].)*
- **Part payments:** not allowed; only full installments [FE-04]. Overpayment is kept as credit for the next due [FE-05].
- **Gateway charges:** the institution chooses who pays them (institution or payer) [FE-06].
- **When a payment counts as paid:** only when the gateway confirms by verified webhook or server check. States: Started → Pending → Paid or Failed [FE-07]. A browser “success” page alone never marks it paid.
- **Manual marking:** the Accountant can mark an online payment paid by hand only by entering the gateway reference number; this also covers payments stuck in Pending [R2-33].
- **Duplicates:** a second confirmation with the same gateway payment ID is ignored; one receipt only [FE-09].
- **Cash control:** a daily collection report goes to the Principal [R2-33].

**Receipts, late fees and reports**

- **Receipts are never edited.** A wrong receipt is cancelled with a reason and Principal approval; its number stays as “void”; a new receipt is issued [FE-12]. Numbering is per institution, per financial year, with no gaps and a configurable prefix [FE-13].
- **Late fees:** configurable [FE-18]. A waiver needs Principal approval and is logged [FE-19].
- **Period lock:** the Accountant can lock a financial period; locked months cannot be edited.
- **Locked months:** unlocked only with Principal approval and a reason (the University Accountant's months: Finance Director approval [Q5]); logged [FE-20].
- **Reports:** by financial year (April–March) and by academic year [FE-21].
- **No-dues check:** dues must be cleared before a transfer certificate or other certificates; the Principal can override with a reason [FE-24].
- **Teachers** see only “dues pending: yes / no”, never amounts [FE-27].
- **Reminders:** automatic 7 days before the due date, on the due date, and 3 and 10 days after (configurable); manual reminders also allowed [FE-29].
- **Not in v1:** refunds [R2-21], tax on fees [R2-22], sibling discount [FE-25], paying for several children at once [FE-26], a direct connection to accounting software [FE-28] (the Tally-format export file is in v1 [PR-06]), cheque-bounce handling [FE-10].

### 7.6 Payroll rules *(Phase 2)*

- The Payroll Officer configures salary structures and deductions and generates payroll from approved leave. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 also used staff attendance, entered or uploaded by HR with no biometric devices; staff attendance is a later phase [OB-08], so loss of pay comes from leave.)*
- **Payroll is released only after approval:** the HR Manager verifies, then the Principal approves (the Finance Director for university staff). Payslips are then released to staff.
- Schools have no HR Manager or Payroll Officer: the School Accountant generates school payroll and the School Principal approves totals only *(v2.1)*.
- The Principal approves **totals only** (by department and staff type) and does not see individual salaries. The Finance Director also sees totals only [R2-05, open item 7].
- The Payroll Officer and HR Manager see individual salaries (in schools, the School Accountant who generates payroll); the Accountant has view access to payroll summaries (totals only) for reconciliation [PY-04]. **Changed in 3.3 [A39, C11, answer 2]:** (Changed in 3.3: individual salaries are seen only by – University: University Accountant and University HR Manager; College: Payroll Officer and HR Manager; School: School Accountant. Everyone else, including the Finance Director, Registrar, Principals and the College Accountant, sees totals only. Every individual view is logged as a sensitive-data view [C11, answer 2].)
- Both the Payroll Officer and the HR Manager can change salary structures [PY-08]. The Payroll Officer's own salary changes need the HR Manager; in schools, the School Accountant's own salary changes need the School Principal [PY-05, Q6].
- Back-dated increments: arrears are calculated automatically [PY-02].
- EDU 360 produces payslips only; salaries are paid outside the system [OB-10].
- Not supported: hourly pay for guest faculty [PY-03], loans and advances [PY-07]. Later: corrections after approval [PY-01], Form 16 and tax declarations [PY-06].

### 7.7 Risk flags and alerts

All thresholds are configurable per institution. Defaults (proposed in Version 1.0, confirmed as defaults):

| Flag | Default rule |
| --- | --- |
| Attendance risk: Normal | Attendance at or above 75% |
| Attendance risk: Warning | 65% up to 75% |
| Attendance risk: Critical | Below 65% |
| Continuous absence | Absent 3 or more working days in a row |
| Low marks | Below the subject pass mark |
| Academic risk | Any of: low marks, attendance Warning or Critical, continuous absence, 2 or more missed assignments in a month |

- The College or School Admin can change the thresholds (letter C) [RK-01, Q8].
- Flags are recalculated right after every attendance or marks change [RK-02].
- A flag clears automatically when the student no longer meets the rule; teacher remarks are kept [RK-03].
- Parents are alerted only when the level changes (for example Normal → Warning) [RK-04].
- A flagged student shows on the parent dashboard as an Academic Risk Warning, with teacher notes, and appears on the risk lists of the teacher, HOD and Principal.

### 7.8 Placement rules *(Phase 2)*

- The Placement Officer sets eligibility per job (for example CGPA, active backlogs, department, year). The system filters eligible students automatically; only eligible students can apply.
- Students track their application status. Parents of college students can view job posts and their child's application status.
- Eligibility is re-checked at shortlisting; the Placement Officer sees a warning and decides [PL-01].
- After placement, a student can apply only for jobs above a package threshold (configurable) [PL-02].
- Students keep a placement profile with resume upload [PL-05].
- Job packages are visible on posts; individual offers are visible to the student, parent and placement team only; reports show totals [PL-07].
- Interview results: Selected, Rejected, Waitlisted. The student accepts or declines offers in the system; the Placement Officer marks the student Placed.
- Not in v1: off-campus offers [PL-03], recruiter logins [PL-04], internships [PL-06].

### 7.9 Library rules *(Phase 2)*

- One copy can be issued to only one user at a time. Only the Librarian can update inventory. Issue limits per role are set by the College Admin or School Admin in library settings.
- Fines follow the institution's library policy.
- Barcode labels are printed by the system and used with a USB scanner; manual entry also allowed [LB-03].
- Fines are configurable per role [LB-04]. The Library Assistant collects fines; only the Librarian waives them, with no limit [LB-05, LB-06].
- Later: fines into the student ledger [LB-01], lost-book charges [LB-02].

### 7.10 Communication rules

- Teachers message students (college) and parents; parents message the class teacher and the school or college office; students message their teachers. Added in 3.2: Vice-Principals message staff, students (college) and parents of their own institution; the Placement Officer messages students about placement (Phase 2); the Alumni Coordinator sends alumni communications by email or SMS (Phase 3) [F-8]. **Students cannot message other students** [CM-01].
- **Quiet hours:** (9 pm–7 am) nobody can send messages to teachers or parents, and automatic alerts created in this window are held and delivered at 7 am. Sent at once: emergency notices, and security messages the user triggers (one-time login codes, password reset, new-phone alert) [CM-02, CM-18].
- Parents contact the Principal through the office only [CM-03].
- Class messages are one-way broadcasts from the teacher; replies come as private messages [CM-05].
- Attachments: PDF, JPG, PNG up to 10 MB, virus-scanned [CM-06].
- Comments pass an automatic bad-language filter; Admin and Principal can also hide them (logged) [CM-10]. No “report abuse” button [CM-04].
- Community posts: like and comment only; no share in v1 [R2-30].
- Users cannot switch off notifications [CM-14]. Added in 3.1: any personal preference never suppresses mandatory institutional or security notifications, and the single quiet-hours rule above stays [PQ-57]. The College or School Admin ticks which extra notifications the institution wants [CM-16, Q8].
- SMS carries only the subject or heading; details are inside the app [CM-15].
- Failed SMS or email: the sender sees it; the Admin sees a list of parents with wrong numbers [CM-17].
- Each institution registers its own SMS sender ID and templates under India's DLT rules [CM-08].
- Every message and notice is stored and traceable. Added in 3.1: every message is held to its tenant, institution, role, class, section and recipient scope, so it never reaches anyone outside it by accident [PQ-56].
- Not in v1: WhatsApp (Phase 2) [CM-07], read acknowledgments [CM-12], photo consent [CM-09], other languages [CM-13].

### 7.11 Complaints, issues and escalations

- Students and parents raise complaints; the Principal or Admin assigns each to an owner, who resolves or escalates it. The HOD resolves department student issues or escalates them to the Principal. The Principal can escalate an issue to the College Admin. Platform support tickets are escalated by the Product Owner or Support Manager.
- No categories or time limits [CP-01]; no anonymous complaints [CP-02]; no reopening or rating [CP-04]; staff cannot raise complaints [CP-05]. Committees: later [CP-03].

### 7.12 Academic calendar

- The university sets the master academic calendar (semester dates and university holidays) for all its colleges and schools; institutions add local holidays and events. They cannot change semester dates. A standalone institution sets its own calendar.
- Local holidays on exam days are blocked with a warning [CL-01].
- When the university changes the calendar mid-year, institutions are notified and affected timetables and exams are flagged [CL-02]. Added in 3.1: a calendar change never silently alters attendance already submitted or historical calculations; calendars follow the university or standalone-institution model, and one calendar is never assumed to fit all institutions [PQ-11, PQ-35].
- The weekly-off pattern (for example alternate Saturdays) is configurable per institution [CL-03].

### 7.13 Tenant lifecycle

- **States:** Created → Trial → Active → Suspended (no access, data kept) → Archived (data kept, access removed) → Deleted [CL-06]. A tenant can be exported at any stage. Deletion needs an export first, the end of the retention period, and Data Protection Officer approval. Added in 3.1: institutions inside a tenant are likewise created, edited, archived and deactivated only by authorized administrators, and are archived or deactivated rather than hard-deleted where records exist [PQ-09].
- **Trial:** 30 days, sample data allowed [MK-05]. When the trial ends, the tenant becomes read-only until it pays [R2-24].
- **Suspension** is done by the Product Owner by hand [R2-24].
- **Retention** is set when the tenant is created [CL-08]. After it ends, the system creates a deletion request for the Data Protection Officer to approve [CL-07].
- **Deletion certificate:** after deletion, a small record (who, when, what) is kept by the platform [CL-10].
- **Export:** CSV / Excel per module plus a ZIP of documents, with a data dictionary [CL-09]. Download links expire after 24 hours.
- **User limit:** warning at 90%; new users blocked at 100%; the Admin can request an upgrade [WF-01].
- **Cancellation:** no refunds in v1; after cancelling, a full data export stays available for 90 days [MK-09, open item 4].

### 7.14 Audit and data rules

- Every create, edit, delete, approval, login, export and denied attempt is logged with the user, active role, time, old value and new value.
- Viewing sensitive records (ID numbers, salaries, health notes) is also logged [AU-01].
- Sensitive fields are masked in the log (ID numbers, bank details, health) [AU-04].
- Denied attempts are logged; repeated attempts alert the Admin [AU-05].
- Audit logs are immutable: kept in write-once storage, separate from the main database, with integrity checks. No role, including the Product Owner, can edit or delete them [AU-06]. Added in 3.1: audit entries keep the actor, active role, time and old and new values where applicable, for every material change; audit exports are scoped, retention is configurable and no secrets are written to the log [PQ-25, PQ-65].
- Audit log retention is set when the tenant is created [AU-02].
- Anyone who can view audit logs can export them; the export is logged [AU-03]. Each role sees logs only for its own scope. Added in 3.1: sensitive personal and financial data has separate, explicit rights to view, export, correct and delete it (marked per action in the Action List V3.1), with field and record controls where needed; approval, audit and retention rules still apply [PQ-66].
- Admin bulk corrections may touch any data, but changes to attendance, marks or fees go through the normal approval chain [R2-32].
- Only the last 4 digits of Aadhaar (or similar national ID) are stored [R2-34].
- Data protection rules (consent, retention, access requests) are configured per institution to match its own legal requirements [PV-01].

## 8. Functional modules

EDU 360 has 29 modules: 20 in Phase 1, 4 in Phase 2 and 5 in Phase 3. Version 1.0 had 27 modules in three groups: 12 core modules, 7 extended modules from Part 2, and 8 modules that the role workflows use but the sources never defined. Each module owns one institutional domain and shares data through the tenant's central database; each can be switched on or off per plan and per tenant. Every module from Version 1.0 is kept; the numbering now follows the phases (the old-to-new mapping is in Section 19.4). Each Phase 1 and Phase 2 module below explains what it does, who uses it, its main screens, its rules, what goes in and out, its notifications and its edge cases.

| Phase | Modules |
| --- | --- |
| Phase 1 | 8.1 Users, roles and access · 8.2 Institution setup and academic structure · 8.3 Timetable and online classes · 8.4 Attendance · 8.5 Examinations · 8.6 Results · 8.7 Assignments, homework and study material · 8.8 Fees · 8.9 Leave · 8.10 Communication · 8.11 Community feed and events · 8.12 Complaints and issues · 8.13 Student notes · 8.14 Policies and documents · 8.15 Staff records · 8.16 Risk monitoring · 8.17 Reports and dashboards · 8.18 Data import, search and IDs · 8.19 Governance and data protection · 8.20 Platform administration |
| Phase 2 | 8.21 Payroll · 8.22 Library · 8.23 Placement · 8.24 Admissions |
| Phase 3 | 8.25 Hostel · 8.26 Transport · 8.27 Alumni · 8.28 Research and publications · 8.29 API and integration governance |

### 8.1 Users, roles and access *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Gives every person exactly one account per identity, the right roles with the right scope, and a safe login.

**Users.** Admins (create users, roles), IT Administrator / School IT Support (resets, unlocks, non-sensitive roles), every user (login, profile, role switcher).

**What it does**

- **Accounts:** single creation and bulk upload; staff log in with email and password; students (college) with Student ID and password; parents with a mobile one-time code and an optional password; applicants with a mobile or email one-time code.
- **First login:** students receive a printed one-time password that must be changed at first login and expires in 7 days [R2-35]; parents activate the link from the admission form with a code sent to their mobile [WF-22].
- **Roles and scope:** standard roles from the template, plus fully custom roles built by the Admin [R2-02]. Each role is assigned with a scope (institution, department, class, subject, child). A user with several roles works in one at a time through the role switcher [HI-15].
- **Guardians:** up to 3 per child, each with their own login; one is “primary” for fees and leave [WF-24]. Parents are matched by mobile number to avoid duplicates [WF-21].
- **Security:** passwords of at least 8 characters, common passwords blocked, forced change every 120 days; two-step login for platform roles, Admins, Principal, Accountant, HR and Payroll [NF-08, NF-09, R2-12] (Changed in 3.2: also Management, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Director, Controller of Examinations, IT Administrator and School IT Support [F-14]); lockout for 15 minutes after 5 wrong passwords (Admin can unlock early) [NF-07].
- **Sessions:** idle timeout 15 minutes for Admin, finance and HR roles, 60 minutes for teachers, parents and students; “remember this device” for 60 days for parents and students; one phone and one computer at a time [WF-35, R2-11].
- **Role change:** the user is logged out at once and sees the new role's screens at next login; permission changes take effect within 1 minute [WF-27, TE-10].

**Key screens.** Users list; Create / bulk upload users; Roles and rights editor; Role switcher; Profile; Security settings.

**Rules.** Deactivating a user moves their pending approvals to the new role holder and warns the Admin [WF-26]. Changing or blocking a guardian needs Principal approval [WF-23, WF-25]. A new parent phone number is verified with a code and an alert goes to the old number [WF-30]. Every rights change is logged and notifies the Principal / Management. Added in 3.1: a user with several roles never has their rights combined in a way that broadens access – one active role at a time, with scope checked again on every switch; role, employment, assignment and entitlement changes take effect within one minute [PQ-17, PQ-20].

**Inputs / outputs.** In: user details, role, scope. Out: accounts, login credentials, role assignments, audit entries.

**Also covers (Version 1.0 “User Management” supporting module).** User creation (single and bulk upload); role assignment; parent linking; activation and deactivation.

**Edge cases.** A staff member who is also a parent has two accounts (Section 2.1). A parent with children in two tenants has two logins. Self-service roles (security, housekeeping, drivers) do not count against the user limit [RL-07].

**Changed in 3.3 [A40, C4, C6]:** “Changed in 3.3: the University Admin builds custom roles for university-office roles only [C4]. The Tenant Admin also creates the Governing Body Approver account (two-step login) [C6, answer 6].” *(Place in V3.2: §8.1 Users, roles and access – Rules)*


### 8.2 Institution setup and academic structure *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Builds the skeleton every other module uses: institutions, departments, programs, years, semesters, sections, classes, subjects, subject groups and the calendar.

**Users.** University Admin (institutions as Draft, calendar, departments and courses for any college), Vice-Chancellor (activates institutions), College / School Admin (own structure), Registrar (programs and exam rules), HOD (subject and faculty allocation), Principal (promotion approval).

**What it does**

- Creates institutions as Draft; the Vice-Chancellor activates them; the plan limits how many [WF-16, WF-14].
- Departments → Programs → Years → Semesters (configurable per year) → Sections for colleges; Classes → Sections for schools [HI-01, HI-02].
- Subjects and **subject groups** that mix students from several sections (electives) [HI-05].
- Subject allocation to faculty; mentor / class coordinator assignment; class teacher assignment.
- Academic calendar: semester dates and holidays from the university; local holidays and events from institutions; weekly-off pattern [CL-03].
- **Year-end promotion:** the Admin runs bulk promotion; the Principal approves; failed or detained students are left out with a reason; detained students stay with status “Detained” [HI-03].
- Grading scheme (grade points, credits, grade bands) set by the university or standalone institution [OB-06].

**Rules.** The HOD must be a faculty member of that department [WF-20]. Local holidays on exam days are blocked with a warning [CL-01]. A mid-year university calendar change notifies institutions and flags affected timetables and exams [CL-02]. Added in 3.1: renames, merges, splits and closures of institutions, departments or programs are controlled operations that keep historical records, relationships and audit history; academic structures are configurable within the hierarchy and institution type, and existing academic records are kept when the structure changes; custom fields, where permitted, have validated types, permissions and audit and never bypass authorization or validation [PQ-03, PQ-10, PQ-12]. Added in 3.2: every college and school must set who approves the Principal's own leave (Management, Registrar or Vice-Chancellor, a different person) before it goes live [D-002, OI-A].

**Outputs.** The structure tree, class lists, allocation lists, calendar.

**Also covers (Version 1.0 “Academic Configuration” supporting module).** Grading systems; exam patterns; attendance rules; academic calendar; courses, subjects, classes and sections.

**Changed in 3.3 [A41, C7]:** “Changed in 3.3: an institution cannot be activated until its Principal's-leave approver is set; a university tenant cannot go live until the Vice-Chancellor's-leave approver is set (VC_LEAVE_APPROVER_SET, University Admin) [C7, answer 6].” *(Place in V3.2: §8.2 Institution setup – Rules)*


### 8.3 Timetable and online classes *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Manages academic schedules: plans who teaches what, where and when, and runs online classes.

**Users.** Admin, HOD, Department Coordinator (build); faculty, students, parents (view).

**What it does**

- Builds the timetable by hand in v1; automatic generation comes later [MD-06].
- Allocates faculty and rooms; publishes timetables by class, faculty and room.
- Creates Zoom, Google Meet or Microsoft Teams meetings automatically for online periods, through a platform-built integration in Phase 1 [OB-07, open item 10].

**Rules.** Teacher or room double-booking shows a warning, not a block [MD-05]. Added in 3.1: a change to a published timetable keeps its history and notifies the people affected; historical timetable and attendance records are never rewritten silently [PQ-30, PQ-31].

**Inputs.** Course structure.

**Outputs.** Timetable views (by class, faculty, room); meeting links on the period.

**Changed in 3.3 [A42, Answer 7, letter gaps]:** “Changed in 3.3: the syllabus is maintained by the HOD and Department Coordinator (college, own department) and by the Vice-Principal (School) and School Admin (school) (SYLLABUS_MANAGE). It is seen by students and parents (SYLLABUS_VIEW), and by the Controller of Examinations and the Quality Assurance and Accreditation roles [answer 7, letter gaps].” *(Place in V3.2: §8.3 Timetable and online classes – What it does / Users)*


### 8.4 Attendance *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Records and monitors attendance accurately and alerts parents at once.

**Users.** Faculty / teachers and substitutes (mark), HOD (corrections in college), School Principal or Vice-Principal (corrections in school), Admin (rules, monitoring, bulk upload with approval), Principal (term lock), students and parents (view).

**What it does**

- Marking per subject period (college) or twice a day (school, per period optional), with statuses Present, Absent, On approved leave, Not held [AT-01, R2-23].
- Correction requests after midnight; bulk upload; substitutes for dates [AT-02, AT-03, AT-11].
- Attendance percentage per subject and overall (Section 20), minimum rules per subject and overall [AT-06].
- Daily attendance entry; subject-wise attendance; summaries, reports, analytics, defaulter lists, attendance risk list; automatic absence alerts.
- *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 had a “Late” status; it is removed everywhere [R2-23]. Version 1.0 had school corrections approved by the School Admin; now the School Principal or Vice-Principal [AP-14].)*

**Key screens.** Mark attendance; Correction requests; Attendance summary (class, department, institution); Defaulter list; Attendance rules.

**Inputs / outputs.** In: student presence status. Out: attendance percentage, defaulter lists, risk flags.

**Rules.** Section 7.3. Only assigned faculty can mark attendance; students and parents have view-only access.

**Notifications.** In-app absence alert per subject immediately; one daily SMS summary; risk-level change alerts.

**Edge cases.** A cancelled period is “Not held” and left out of the percentage [AT-12]. Approved leave and on-duty are not counted as absent. Edits after a term lock are refused. Added in 3.1: an approved correction keeps the original entry beside the change, with its audit trail; calendar changes never alter attendance already submitted; offline drafts are kept and never silently overwritten when they sync – the sync and conflict rules are set in detailed design (open item 20) [PQ-33, PQ-35, PQ-36].

### 8.5 Examinations *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Manages examination processes: exam setup, schedules, hall tickets and marks entry.

**Users.** Registrar (exam rules), Controller of Examinations (university schedules, marks process), Admin and Examination Clerk (internal schedules, hall tickets, external marks upload), faculty and teachers (marks), HOD, Class Teacher, Principal, Vice-Principal (approvals).

**What it does**

- Exam patterns (internal / external split) and grade bands.
- Exam schedules: university exams by the Controller; internal exams by the College Admin or Examination Clerk [WF-18].
- Hall tickets with automatic eligibility checks (attendance, overdue fees) and Principal override [EX-09].
- Marks entry with special codes AB, MP, WH and medical-absent, range checks and jump warnings [EX-02, EX-17].
- Backlog tracking and supplementary exam registration [EX-08].

**Rules.** Section 7.4. Admins set up and monitor exams but cannot enter marks [R2-18]. Added in 3.1: absent, withheld, incomplete and exempt statuses are always explicit and handled by the approved calculation rules, never assumed; imported or externally supplied marks are validated, their source is recorded and changes are audited [PQ-41, PQ-42].

**Inputs.** Exam details; student enrollment data.

**Outputs.** Schedules, hall tickets, marks lists, backlog lists.

Only authorized staff can modify exams. Hall ticket eligibility follows Section 7.4. Version 1.0 listed moderation workflows here; moderation is a later phase [OB-05].

**Changed in 3.3 [A43, C5]:** “Changed in 3.3: standalone exam rules are set by the Admin with no approval step; Principal notified; logged and versioned [C5].” *(Place in V3.2: §8.5 Examinations – Rules)*


### 8.6 Results *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Calculates, approves and publishes academic results.

**Users.** Faculty (marks), HOD, Class Teacher, Principal (approve), Controller / College Admin / School Principal / School Admin (publish), Admin, students and parents (view).

**What it does**

- Calculates grades, GPA and CGPA from approved marks (Section 20).
- Runs the approval chain and enables Publish only after final approval.
- Publishes grade sheets and notifies students and parents; keeps result history; supports withdrawal with a reason [EX-07].

**Inputs.** Approved marks data.

**Rules.** Results can be published only after approval (Section 7.4). Re-evaluation is not in v1; results are view-only for students and parents [R2-07]. Added in 3.1: the grading and formula configuration is versioned, so every result keeps the rules and version used when it was published; a published result is never silently overwritten – changes go through the controlled correction or withdrawal workflow with approval and audit [PQ-38, PQ-40, PQ-43]. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 listed re-evaluation requests as a feature.)*

**Outputs.** Grade sheets; pass percentage summaries and subject analysis; performance reports.

**Changed in 3.3 [A44, Letter gaps]:** “Changed in 3.3: the student's and parent's performance report (graph, class average, feedback) is part of their own results view (RESULT_VIEW_OWN); students and parents have no general Reports access [letter gaps #94, #95, #110].” *(Place in V3.2: §8.6 Results – What it does)*


### 8.7 Assignments, homework and study material *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Manages academic assignments and homework: gives and tracks coursework.

**Users.** Faculty and teachers (create, evaluate), college students (submit), parents (view and track for school children), Principal (homework compliance view).

**What it does**

- Assignment creation with subject, instructions and due date; study material upload.
- College students upload submissions. The teacher picks allowed file types per assignment from the safe types the system accepts [MD-02, TE-11].
- Late submissions are allowed until the teacher closes the assignment and are marked “Late” [MD-01].
- School homework: the teacher marks the status (Completed, Pending, Not submitted); parents see it [MD-04].
- Evaluation, marks and feedback; missed-assignment alerts.

**Inputs / outputs.** In: assignment files. Out: marks; feedback.

**Rules.** No plagiarism check [MD-03].

### 8.8 Fees *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Manages student financial transactions: everything a student owes and pays, with full control over cash and approvals.

**Users.** Finance Director and University Accountant, or Management (policy), Accountant (structures, collections, receipts), Principal (approvals, daily report), Admin (view), students and parents (pay), teachers (dues yes / no only).

**What it does**

- Fee policy, fee structures and versions, fee heads (including hostel, mess, transport in one ledger), installments, scholarships, concessions, late-fee rules.
- Online payments through the gateway (UPI, cards, net banking, wallets) and offline entry; receipts with gap-free numbering per institution and financial year.
- Student ledger with paid, pending, overdue and credit balance.
- Automatic and manual reminders; daily collection report to the Principal; monthly, scholarship and outstanding reports by financial and academic year; financial period lock.

**Key screens.** Fee policy; Fee structure; Exception requests; Student ledger; Payments; Manual payment entry; Receipts; Concessions; Scholarships; Reminders; Reports; Lock period.

**Inputs / outputs.** In: fee plans; payment records. Out: receipts; outstanding balance reports; daily, monthly and scholarship reports.

**Rules.** Sections 7.1 and 7.5. Fee edits allowed only before the academic session starts. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 listed refunds as a feature; refunds are not in v1 [R2-21].)*

**Notifications.** Fee due and overdue reminders; payment received; payment failed (if the institution ticks it).

**Edge cases.** Gateway success without confirmation stays Pending; duplicate confirmations give one receipt; overpayment becomes credit; mid-year joiners pay full or pro-rata. Added in 3.1: fee-category and fee-assignment changes are controlled and audited, and existing financial history is never rewritten silently; the link from each fee to its student, course, class and year stays traceable; mismatches found in reconciliation are escalated under role control, keeping evidence and audit; a future refund workflow (not in Phase 1) must never overwrite the original payment ledger [PQ-44, PQ-45, PQ-49, PQ-52].

### 8.9 Leave *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Manages student leave requests and approvals (Version 1.0 “Student Leave Management”) and staff leave, with the right approver and the right effect on attendance and payroll.

**Users.** Students, parents, staff (apply); faculty mentors, Class Teachers, HODs, HR, Principal, Registrar, Management (approve); College Admin and School Admin (monitor).

**What it does**

- Applications by full day, half day or period, with optional document, up to 3 days after the absence.
- Length-based routing to the final approver; staff balance checks and loss-of-pay warnings; substitute assignment.
- Student leave application; parent leave request submission; multi-level approval workflow; attendance adjustment rules (automatic adjustment after final approval); leave history tracking; stage-by-stage notifications.

**Inputs / outputs.** In: leave dates; leave reason; supporting document (optional). Out: leave approval status; leave history.

**Rules.** Sections 7.1 and 7.2.

**Notifications.** Every stage notifies the requester; college parents get every request and decision.

**Changed in 3.3 [A45, C6, letter gaps]:** “Changed in 3.3: the Governing Body Approver approves the Principal's, the Vice-Chancellor's or a dedicated Data Protection Contact's leave where there is no Management; leave with a medical attachment is sensitive [C6, letter gaps].” *(Place in V3.2: §8.9 Leave – Rules)*


### 8.10 Communication *(Phase 1; WhatsApp Phase 2)*

**Purpose.** Enables official, traceable institutional communication.

**Users.** Admin, Principal, HOD, teachers, Accountant, Placement Officer, students, parents.

**What it does**

- Notices at university, institution, department and class level, with approval where Section 7.1 requires it; emergency notices on all channels.
- Direct messages and class broadcasts; meeting notices; Principal instructions.
- Notification center with in-app, push, SMS and email delivery (email alerts, SMS alerts, in-app alerts) and delivery status; notice approval.

**Rules.** Section 7.10 (quiet hours, who can message whom, attachments, SMS content, DLT).

**Inputs / outputs.** In: message content; audience. Out: delivery status (sent, delivered; “read” needs read acknowledgments, a later phase [CM-12]); failed-delivery lists for the Admin.

Notice approval follows Section 7.1. All messages are traceable.

### 8.11 Community feed and events *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Shares institution life (events, achievements, cultural programs, sports, placement news, photos, videos, announcements) and runs events.

**Users.** Admin and Principal (post, approve), teachers, HOD, Placement Officer (post for approval), parents, college students and staff (view, like, comment).

**What it does**

- Posts with photos and videos; approval queue for posts that need it; a notification for every approved post.
- Like and comment only. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 allowed sharing inside the platform; share is removed in v1 [R2-30].)* Comments pass an automatic bad-language filter; Admin and Principal can hide comments (logged) [CM-10].
- Events (Version 1.0 “Events” module): Admin, HOD, Faculty and other organizers propose; Principal approves; published to everyone; RSVP / registration only [MD-23, AP-18].
- Every approved post notifies parents.

**Edge cases.** No “report abuse” button [CM-04]; photo consent is a later phase [CM-09].

**Changed in 3.3 [A46, Letter gaps]:** “Changed in 3.3: the University Admin posts directly, university scope (COMMUNITY_POST_DIRECT). The Vice-Principals and Department Coordinator like, comment and RSVP only (Community letter V) [letter gaps #111–#114].” *(Place in V3.2: §8.11 Community feed and events – Users)*


### 8.12 Complaints and issues *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Logs, assigns and resolves complaints from students and parents and student issues in departments.

**Users.** Students and parents (raise); Admin, Principal, HOD (assign, resolve, escalate); University Admin (review escalated complaints).

**Rules.** Section 7.11: no categories, time limits, anonymity, reopening or rating; staff cannot raise complaints.

### 8.13 Student notes: discipline and health *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Records behavior, discipline and health notes for a student.

**Users.** Class Teacher, Subject Teacher, faculty and Principal (add) [WF-38]; Principal (review, instruct); parents (view).

**Rules**

- Notes can be added, not deleted. A wrong note is fixed by adding a linked correction note; the original stays [MD-19].
- Health notes are visible only to the class teacher, Principal and parent (where switched on for parents). Added in 3.2: in a college, the section's mentor takes the class teacher's place; the author of any note always sees the notes they wrote; the HOD has no access by default [F-9].
- Health notes follow the same rule in college as in school [R2-29]. The College Admin or School Admin switches health notes on or off for parents [WF-34, Q10].
- Parents see discipline notes immediately [MD-21].
- Notes are deleted 1 year after the student leaves, unless on legal hold [MD-22].
- Notes are not “student records”; viewing health notes is logged [AU-01].

### 8.14 Policies and documents *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Holds university policies, department documents and accreditation documents (evidence).

**Users.** University Admin (policies), Registrar (drafts), HOD (department documents), Accreditation Coordinator (accreditation documents), Compliance Officer. **Changed in 3.3 [A47, C2, C3, answer 1]:** (Changed in 3.3: University Admin and Registrar draft university policies; the Vice-Chancellor approves; the University Admin publishes. In a standalone institution the Admin (or the Principal) drafts and the Principal approves – Management where the Principal drafted. Compliance Officer and the standalone Admin prepare compliance reports; Accreditation Coordinators and the School Admin prepare accreditation items [C2, C3, answer 1].)

**Rules.** A published university policy applies to all institutions under it. Staff must read and accept new policies; acceptance is tracked [MD-24]. Accreditation templates (such as NAAC criteria) are a later phase [OB-17]. **Changed in 3.3 [A48, C2, C9]:** (Changed in 3.3: a policy is published only after approval [C2]. Management is not staff and does not accept policies [C9, answer 9].)

### 8.15 Staff records *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Keeps staff profiles, service records and documents. Version 1.0 also listed workload, performance reviews and daily staff attendance (manual entry or upload) here; these are later phases.

**Users.** HR Manager, HR Executive, University HR Manager, Principal, HOD (workload, later phase), Admin.

**What it does.** Staff profiles; service records; staff documents (degrees, ID) uploaded and verified by HR [MD-25]; yearly leave credit per leave type. Staff attendance and workload / performance monitoring are later phases [OB-08, OB-03, OB-04].

### 8.16 Risk monitoring *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Flags attendance and academic risk automatically (rules in Section 7.7) so teachers and parents act early.

**Users.** Teachers, HOD, Principal, Admin (risk lists); parents and college students (own status).

**Rules.** Section 7.7: recalculated on every change, cleared automatically, parents alerted only on level change. Risk action plans are a later phase [RK-05].

### 8.17 Reports and dashboards *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Gives every role the numbers it needs within its scope. Added in 3.2: fixed reports are open only to roles whose Reports letter is not N, and audit logs only to roles whose Governance letter is not N [F-6]. **Changed in 3.3 [A49, C2, letter gaps]:** Changed in 3.3: reports need no approval; every generation is logged [C2]. Billing and Support Managers see platform reports for their own area only (PLATFORM_REPORTS_VIEW). Management sees every tenant area read-only (TENANT_OVERSIGHT_VIEW). Summary-only views through REPORTS_VIEW: Registrar and Vice-Chancellor – Admissions; Vice-Chancellor – Alumni and Research; Principal (College) – Library, Hostel, Transport, Alumni, Research; School Principal – Library, Hostel, Transport; each only when the module is switched on. Students and parents: see A44 [letter gaps].

**What it does**

- Fixed reports with filters and PDF / Excel export: attendance, defaulters, risk, exams, pass %, results, fees (daily, monthly, outstanding, scholarship), leave, communication delivery, audit. A custom report builder comes later [OB-15].
- **Buyer dashboard** for Management, Principal, Registrar and Vice-Chancellor: fees collected, attendance and results at a glance [MK-11].
- Statutory exports in Tally, UDISE+, AISHE and affiliating-university formats [PR-06].
- Reports by financial year and academic year for finance [FE-21]. Added in 3.1: reports, search, dashboards, exports, downloads and background jobs keep the same tenant and role limits as the records they come from; historical reports keep the grouping and meaning they had when a student later changes class or institution; users may save a few personal filters and dashboard preferences, which never change report definitions, calculations or permissions; statutory exports use the official templates and are checked for fields, identifiers, totals, rejected records and export rights (exact affiliating-university templates: open item 19) [PQ-60, PQ-61, PQ-62, PQ-63].
- Version 1.0 “Reporting” supporting module: academic reports; financial reports; activity logs; report export (PDF and Excel).

### 8.18 Data import, search and IDs *(Phase 1)*

- **Import templates** for students, staff, parents, fee dues and past results; the platform team helps with the first import only through tenant-granted 24-hour ticket access, or by guiding the tenant Admin [MD-26, Q7].
- **Bulk upload:** the whole file is checked first and errors are shown row by row. The user then imports only a clean file, or imports the good rows and keeps the bad rows (with reasons) in a list to fix and add later [MD-27]. Added in 3.1: likely duplicate records found on import or entry are flagged and routed for review, never merged automatically [PQ-24].
- **Global search** by name, ID or phone, for roles allowed to see students [MD-28].
- **Student ID** generated automatically; the pattern is configurable [MD-29].
- **Student status:** Applicant → Active → On hold → Withdrawn / Transferred / Dropped → Graduated → Alumni, plus Detained [MD-30, open item 6]. Admin “delete” only changes status to Withdrawn; there is no hard delete [MX-09]. Added in 3.1: status changes are controlled; inactive, transferred and graduated records keep their history, with access adjusted to the new status. A transfer is a controlled change of ownership and scope that keeps history and audit; nothing moves silently between tenants [PQ-14, PQ-26]. Added in 3.2: setting Graduated is a Phase 1 status change; the Phase 3 alumni module (GRADUATION_CONFIRM) later creates the alumni record from it [F-10]. **Changed in 3.3 [A50, Answer 8, letter gaps]:** Changed in 3.3: the College Admin, School Admin and Records Officer edit individual student records (STUDENT_RECORD_EDIT), never the student ID or status; changes to sensitive fields are logged as sensitive. Governance officers, the Controller of Examinations and the Registrar search students read-only with limited fields (STUDENT_SEARCH); every view logged [answer 8, letter gaps].
- **ID numbers:** only the last 4 digits of Aadhaar (or similar national ID) are stored [R2-34].
- **ID card data export** (photo + details) for a printing vendor [OB-12].

### 8.19 Governance and data protection *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Approval workflows, audit logs, compliance and personal-data requests.

**Users.** Governance officers, Data Protection Contact, Data Protection Officer, Admins.

**What it does**

- Audit logs (Section 7.14) with export.
- Personal-data requests (access, correction, deletion) from students, parents and staff, handled by the tenant's Data Protection Contact; no fixed time limit [R2-25, PV-06].
- Full-tenant export and deletion requests approved by the DPO. Added in 3.2: parent consent is recorded with its date – in the app at onboarding, or from paper by the Admin [PV-03, F-13]; a tenant can opt out of anonymous platform analytics through its tenant settings [PV-07, F-13]; the student's request to limit what college parents see waits for the lawyer check (open item 12) [PV-04].
- **RBAC mapping layer** (Version 1.0 module 8.19): keeps the permission matrix (Section 10 and the companion Excel) and the system's real permissions in step, including each institution's custom roles and rights [R2-02]. Users: Product Owner, Platform Admin, Data Protection Officer, Audit Officer. Features: role-to-permission mapping; module-level permission linking; audit reconciliation (matrix vs. live permissions); exportable RBAC reports; governance validation.
- Compliance reports and accreditation document storage. **Changed in 3.3 [A51, C3]:** (Changed in 3.3: preparers and approvers as in Section 7.1; nobody approves an item they prepared [C3, answer 1].)

### 8.20 Platform administration *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Runs EDU 360 as a SaaS product.

**Users.** Product Owner, Platform Admin, Billing Manager, Support Manager, Release Manager, Data Protection Officer.

**What it does**

- Tenants and lifecycle (Trial → Active → Suspended → Archived → Deleted).
- Plans built by ticking modules and features; several pricing types (per student per year by default, flat, per module); usage types such as SMS and storage [MK-03, MK-04, WF-07]. Added in 3.2: the Product Owner creates platform staff accounts and handles release rollout and rollback, support escalations and invoice review; the Platform Admin may edit plan modules, features and limits (never prices) and schedule releases [F-4, F-12].
- Billing with invoices; SMS charged per message; no tax and no refunds in v1 (open items 4 and 5).
- Subscription plans and limits; feature control; platform analytics; data protection approvals.
- Support tickets raised by any user; tenant-granted read-only access per ticket for 24 hours [WF-11]. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 listed SLAs; no support SLA in v1 [R2-27].)*
- Built-in usage counts on the Product Owner dashboard (logins, attendance marked, fees paid online); no outside analytics tool [R2-13].
- Security policy, backup and retention settings, platform audit logs.
- Releases: one version for all tenants; app-only rollback [R2-26].
- Allowed integration types list (platform roles never see a tenant's keys or webhooks) [MX-02].

**Changed in 3.3 [A52, Letter gaps]:** “Changed in 3.3: Billing and Support Managers see platform reports for their own area (PLATFORM_REPORTS_VIEW); they no longer hold V on Tenant, Analytics or Data Protect. Release Manager and Data Protection Officer: platform letters reduced to what their actions need [letter gaps #1–#17].” *(Place in V3.2: §8.20 Platform administration)*


### 8.21 Payroll *(Phase 2)*

**Purpose.** Manages staff salary processing: produces correct, approved payslips for every staff member. Salaries are paid outside EDU 360 [OB-10].

**Users.** Payroll Officer (structures, generation), HR Manager (verify, structures), Principal (approves totals), University Accountant and Finance Director (university staff), School Accountant and School Principal (school payroll, no HR step), Accountant (totals for reconciliation), staff (own payslips).

**What it does**

- Salary structures with components and deductions; changes by the Payroll Officer or HR Manager; the Payroll Officer's own salary changes need the HR Manager [PY-05, PY-08].
- Monthly payroll generation using approved leave and loss-of-pay confirmed by HR.
- Arrears for back-dated increments calculated automatically [PY-02].
- Approval by totals (department and staff type); payslip generation and release; salary history; deduction management; payroll reports.

**Inputs.** Leave data (approved leave and loss of pay). *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 also took staff attendance; staff attendance is a later phase [OB-08].)* Payroll is released only after approval (Section 7.6).

**Key screens.** Salary structures; Run payroll; Verification; Approval (totals); Payslips; History; Reports.

**Rules.** Sections 7.1 and 7.6. Individual salaries are visible only to the Payroll Officer and HR Manager; viewing them is logged.

**Outputs.** Payslips, payroll register, totals by department and staff type.

**Edge cases.** No hourly pay for guest faculty, loans or advances [PY-03, PY-07]; corrections after approval and Form 16 are later [PY-01, PY-06].

**Changed in 3.3 [A53, C11]:** “Changed in 3.3: individual salaries – see Section 7.6 [C11, answer 2].” *(Place in V3.2: §8.21 Payroll – Rules)*


### 8.22 Library *(Phase 2)*

**Purpose.** Manages all physical and digital library resources efficiently and transparently.

**Users.** Librarian, Library Assistant, students, faculty, parents (view), College Admin / School Admin (settings). **Changed in 3.3 [A54, Letter gaps]:** (Changed in 3.3: students and all staff use the library; Lab Assistant, Research Assistant and School Lab Assistant added to library self-service [letter gaps #77, #78, #109].) See Part E, item E3

**What it does**

- Catalog and ISBN management; digital library records; barcode labels printed by the system for a USB scanner, or manual entry [LB-03].
- Library cards for students and faculty; issue and return with automatic due dates; reservations with a queue; fines configurable per role [LB-04]. **Changed in 3.3 [A55, Letter gaps]:** (Changed in 3.3: students and staff.)
- Inventory audit; damaged and lost book tracking; issue, fine and inventory reports.
- Student and faculty self-service: search books, reserve books, view issued books and fine status (e-resource downloads later).

**Inputs / outputs.** In: book details; student and faculty IDs; issue and return dates. Out: issue history; fine reports; inventory reports.

**Rules.** Section 7.9: one copy to one user; only the Librarian updates inventory and waives fines; the Library Assistant collects fines.

**Edge cases.** E-resource downloads, fines into the student ledger and lost-book charges are later phases [OB-14, LB-01, LB-02].

### 8.23 Placement *(Phase 2)*

**Purpose.** Manages campus placement activities systematically, from company to placed student.

**Users.** Placement Officer, students, parents (view), College Admin (creates the officer), Principal (reports).

**What it does**

- Company profiles; job posts with role, package, eligibility and deadline; automatic eligibility mapping; job alerts to eligible students and their parents.
- Student placement profile with resume upload [PL-05]; applications; shortlisting with a re-check of eligibility [PL-01]; interview scheduling (online / offline); results (Selected, Rejected, Waitlisted).
- Offer letter upload; offer acceptance by the student; marking Placed; package threshold for placed students [PL-02].
- Reports by department, company and package; company feedback; placement history; placement notices and community posts.

**Inputs / outputs.** In: company details; job descriptions and eligibility criteria; student academic data. Out: placement statistics (department-wise, company-wise, package analysis); offer records; company feedback reports.

**Rules.** Section 7.8. Only eligible students can apply; students track their application status. Placement applies to colleges only. Individual offers are visible only to the student, parent and placement team [PL-07].

**Edge cases.** Off-campus offers, recruiter logins and internships are later phases.

### 8.24 Admissions *(Phase 2)*

**Purpose.** Manages the complete digital admission lifecycle up to a ready student account.

**Users.** Admission Officer, College / School / University Admin, Principal (approves merit lists), applicants (log in with a one-time code), parents (school applicants), Accountant (application fee view). **Changed in 3.3 [A56, Letter gaps]:** (Changed in 3.3: the University Admin creates admission forms (ADMISSION_FORM_CREATE). The Registrar and Vice-Chancellor see summaries only. Phase 2 note: the Records Officer will need a view of admitted applicants when this module is built; Office Staff and School Office Staff access to be revisited at MD-11 [letter gaps #29, #35, #84, #86, #108].)

**What it does**

- Application forms per session; online applications with document upload; application fee paid through the gateway into the ledger [FE-23].
- Merit list generation; Principal approval of the final list; seat allocation.
- On confirmation, student and parent accounts are created automatically and the parent link comes from the form [WF-22].
- Admission approval; admission reports.

**Inputs / outputs.** In: applicant details; documents; marks; seat matrix. Out: merit lists; allocation lists; new student records.

**Rules.** Role-based approval (Admission Officer prepares, Principal approves the final list); audit logs; data validation before account creation. Reserved-category seats, tie-breakers, waitlists, document re-upload and admission enquiries are later phases [MD-07 to MD-11]; delegating merit-list approval is later [WF-37]. **Changed in 3.3 [A57, C12]:** (Changed in 3.3: merit-list approval can never be delegated [WF-37, C12].)

### 8.25 Hostel *(Phase 3)*

**Purpose.** Manages student residential operations digitally (records only, no hardware).

**Users.** Hostel Warden, Hostel Staff, College / School Admin, Accountant (view mess fees), students and parents (view). **Changed in 3.3 [A58, Letter gaps]:** (Changed in 3.3: College / School Admin – settings only (HOSTEL_MANAGE). Accountants see mess fees as fee heads in the ledger (LEDGER_VIEW) and have no Hostel letter. Principals see a summary only [letter gaps #65, #68, #104, #106].)

**What it does.** Blocks and rooms; room allocation and student hostel assignment; vacancies; mess fees as fee heads in the student ledger; hostel attendance; hostel complaints; reports.

**Outputs.** Occupancy and vacancy reports; hostel attendance; mess fee dues.

**Rules.** The Warden manages hostel assignments only and cannot edit academic or general student records. Out-pass / gate pass is later [MD-14].

### 8.26 Transport *(Phase 3)*

**Purpose.** Manages institutional transport operations (records only, no GPS hardware).

**Users.** Transport Manager, Driver, Transport Staff, College / School Admin, students and parents. **Changed in 3.3 [A59, Letter gaps]:** (Changed in 3.3: College / School Admin – settings only (TRANSPORT_MANAGE); Accountants see transport fees in the ledger only; Principals see a summary only [letter gaps #66, #69, #105, #107].)

**What it does.** Routes; vehicle allocation; driver assignment; student route mapping and pickup points; transport fees as fee heads; transport reports. Parent view: bus route, driver contact, pickup point.

**Rules.** The Transport Manager manages route assignments only. Drivers see only name, photo and pickup point, never phone numbers or addresses [MD-15].

### 8.27 Alumni *(Phase 3)*

**Purpose.** Keeps lifelong engagement with graduates.

**Users.** Alumni Coordinator, College Admin, University Admin; Records Officer or Controller (confirm graduation). **Changed in 3.3 [A60, Letter gaps, wording]:** (Changed in 3.3: the College Admin and University Admin add or remove alumni records by hand only (ALUMNI_RECORD_MANAGE) [MD-12]; only the Records Officer and the Controller of Examinations confirm graduation (GRADUATION_CONFIRM).)

**What it does.** The Records Officer or Controller confirms graduation; the alumni record is created automatically and can also be added or removed by hand [MD-12]. Alumni profiles, academic history linking, placement history, employment tracking, alumni communications and event invitations, alumni reports.

**Inputs / outputs.** In: graduated student records; alumni updates. Out: alumni directory; engagement reports.

**Rules.** Alumni do not log in [R2-40]; the Alumni Coordinator manages the records. A student record converts to an alumni record on graduation. Contribution and donation tracking is later [MD-13]. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 let alumni log in and see their own record and alumni communications.)*

### 8.28 Research and publications *(Phase 3)*

**Purpose.** Supports academic research governance.

**Users.** Faculty, HOD, Research Assistant, Research Coordinator, University Admin. **Changed in 3.3 [A61, Letter gaps]:** (Changed in 3.3: the Department Coordinator adds research records (RESEARCH_RECORD_ADD); the University Admin has no Research task and its Research letter is N [letter gaps #44, #83].)

**What it does.** Research project records; faculty publications; journal submissions; conference participation; research grants; research reports.

**Rules.** Faculty enter their own records, the HOD verifies, the Research Coordinator approves grant records. Approval in standalone colleges is later [MD-16].

### 8.29 API and integration governance *(Phase 3)*

**Purpose.** Manages external system connections securely.

**Users.** Product Owner, Platform Admin, University / College / School Admin, IT Administrator.

**What it does.** API key management; webhook configuration; third-party system mapping (payment gateway, SMS, email, SSO, meeting tools); access permission control; integration audit logs; integration usage reports.

**Governance.** Product Owner approval for new integration types; tenant-level enable or disable; audit tracking; API usage limits from the subscription plan. Platform roles manage only the list of allowed integration types; they never see a tenant's keys or webhooks [MX-02]. Institutions creating their own API keys is later [MD-17]. The meeting-tool integration for online classes is built by the platform in Phase 1 and does not wait for this module.

## 10. Master role permission matrix (Version 3.3) <!-- A64: was (Version 3.0) -->

The matrix covers 70 roles across 28 feature areas. It replaces both the permission tables in the main document and the original Excel sheet: 43 roles and 20 feature areas come from the Excel; Version 1.0 added 24 roles and 8 feature areas (67 roles) and corrected 35 cells from the source Excel (the reason for each is in Section 19.3 and in the companion Excel's change log); Version 2.0 added Management, the University HR Manager and the Data Protection Contact and the Student (School) role, and removed the Alumni login (70 roles). **Bold** values changed in Version 3.0 (8 cells, from the action list questions); the earlier Version 2.0 and 2.1 changes are listed in Section 19.2 and the Excel change logs. Letters follow Section 6.2; **approval power comes only from the chains in Section 7**. The letters are a one-letter summary: the exact rights are the actions in Section 26. No matrix cell changed in Version 3.1. Version 3.2 changes 19 cells, marked “(3.2)”: A is added where a role holds an approval action, and the Controller of Examinations and the Records Officer get Alumni A for confirming graduation. Letters show authority over other people's records; self-service actions, approval tools (delegate, bulk approve) and checking steps appear only in the Action List. Where the two differ, the Action List governs access checks [D-003]. **Changed in 3.3 [A65, C6, letter gaps]:** Changed in 3.3: 71 roles – the Governing Body Approver was added [C6, C13]; 68 letters changed (6 decided, 3 derived, 59 from the letter-gap decisions) and 55 letters kept and now backed by an action (Section 19.14).

**Rules on top of the matrix**

- Scope always limits access: a College Admin with F on Users manages only their own college; a parent sees only their own children.
- Restrictions lines win over letters [R2-18]: an Admin with M+C on Exams sets up and monitors exams but cannot enter marks.
- Every staff user can always see their own profile, payslips and notices and request their own leave. **Changed in 3.3 [A66, C9]:** (Changed in 3.3: Management and the Governing Body Approver are not staff [C9].)
- Students and parents can pay their own fees from V on Finance, and like and comment from V on Community (sharing posts was removed in 2.0 [R2-30]).
- Every role can view the audit log entries for its own scope (Section 7.14); the Governance column covers the governance module itself.
- Platform roles have N on every tenant feature area, except the DPO's limited Governance view and Support's tenant-granted 24-hour ticket access [MX-01, R2-19, WF-11]. For platform roles, Reports and Analytics mean platform-level reports only (usage, revenue; no SLA in v1). Platform roles never see tenant academic, financial or personal data.
- Custom roles built by an institution start from these rows; their rights are picked from the actions in Section 26 and tracked by the RBAC mapping layer.
- **Changed in 3.3 [A67, R-1]:** Changed in 3.3: every non-N letter is backed by at least one action in Section 26; an action includes the reads it needs (R-1). The Action List governs access checks [D-003].

### 10.6 What scoped letters mean

| Role | Area | Letter | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Head of Department | Records | V | Own department only [MX-15] |
| Professors, Class Teacher, Subject Teacher | Records | V | Assigned students; photo, contact and parent details only [MX-16] |
| Principal (College), School Principal | Records | V | Plus approval of certificate / TC requests and record corrections [MX-12] |
| Parent (School) | Records | **V+R** | Views own child's record; requests certificates (bonafide, TC) and record corrections [MX-18] |
| Student (College) | Records | R | Views own record; requests certificates and corrections [MX-19] |
| College Admin, School Admin | Records | F | “Delete” only changes status to Withdrawn; no hard delete [MX-09] |
| Alumni Coordinator | Records | V | Graduated students only [MX-22] |
| Librarian, Hostel Warden, Transport Manager, Office Staff | Records | V | Limited fields: name, ID, class, photo, parent contact as needed [MX-23] |
| School Principal, School Admin | Exams | A / M+C | Both also hold RESULT_PUBLISH, used only after Principal approval [AP-16] |
| College Admin *(v2.1)* | Exams | M+C | Also holds RESULT_PUBLISH and RESULT_WITHDRAW for standalone and external-university colleges; publishing only after Principal approval, withdrawal only with Principal approval [HI-10, Q4] |
| Registrar *(v2.1)* | Exams | **M+C** | Owns exam rules: patterns and grading scheme; does not enter marks [R2-06] |
| School Accountant *(v2.1)* | HR / Payroll | **M** | Generates school payroll (Phase 2); School Principal approves totals |
| Student (College) | Exams | V | View only; re-evaluation not in v1 [R2-07] |
| Subject Teacher | Leave | V | Student leave for own classes [MX-17] |
| Class Teacher, Subject Teacher *(V3)* | Academic | **M** | Homework, study material, timetable for own classes [Q1] |
| College Accountant, School Accountant *(V3)* | Comm | **M** | Financial notices (Principal approval) and replies to fee queries [Q2] |
| Office Staff, School Office Staff *(V3)* | Comm | **M** | Messages only: office inbox; passes parent messages to the Principal [Q3, CM-03] |
| College Admin, School Admin *(V3)* | Leave | **V+C** | Configures leave types and the sandwich rule; monitors leave, never approves [Q8] |
| Parent (College) | Records | V | Cannot request certificates; college students request their own (confirmed) [Q11] |
| Management | Leave, Finance | A | Principal's own leave where assigned; in standalone institutions the fee policy and fee exceptions |
| Management *(v2.1)* | Integrations | **N** | Integrations means API keys and webhooks; Management does not need to see them |
| Data Protection Officer | Governance | V | Data-protection items only; not tenant audit logs [MX-01, R2-19] |
| Product Owner, Platform Admin, Release Manager, DPO | Integrations | F / M / V / V | Allowed integration types only [MX-02] |

### 10.7 Original permission tables from Source 1 (kept for reference)

These are the permission tables exactly as the main source document gave them, before they were merged with the Excel matrix. **The matrix above (10.2–10.5) replaces them**; the conflicts between the two were resolved in Version 1.0 (Section 19.11), and later decisions are in Section 19.2. They are kept so that nothing from the source is lost.

**Platform level**

| Role | Universities | Billing & Plans | Feature Control | Analytics | Support | Releases | Data Access |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Product Owner | Full Access | Full Access | Full Access | Full Access | Full Access | Full Access | Full Access |
| Platform Admin | Manage | Manage | Manage | Manage | Manage | Manage | Full Access |
| Billing Manager | View Only | Full Access | No Access | View Only | No Access | No Access | No Access |
| Support Manager | View Only | No Access | No Access | View Only | Full Access | No Access | No Access |
| Release Manager | View Only | No Access | No Access | View Only | No Access | Full Access | No Access |
| Data Protection Officer | View Only | No Access | No Access | View Only | No Access | No Access | Approve |

This level controls the entire EDU 360 platform, including tenant management, subscriptions, system configuration, releases, and global data protection enforcement.

## 11. Role workflows – all roles and Platform level

Sections 11–14 give the screen-level workflow of every role: the menu path, what the system does, and who feels the change. Workflows marked *(new)* were written from the role's permissions and the rules in Section 7. *(changed)* marks steps changed by a decision in Version 2.0 or later; the Version 1.0 wording is kept and the change is added. Steps added after Version 1.0 are marked *(added)*. Every workflow starts at login and ends at logout. Only the Product Owner's login step is shown in full; the other roles log in the same way to their own dashboard.

### 11.0 Rules for every role

- **Idle timeout:** Admin, finance and HR roles 15 minutes; teachers 60 minutes; parents and students 60 minutes, with “remember this device” for 60 days [WF-35, R2-11].
- **Devices:** each user can be logged in on one phone and one computer at a time; logging in on a new one logs out the old one [R2-11].
- **Passwords:** at least 8 characters, common passwords blocked, forced change every 120 days [NF-08, R2-12]. Lockout for 15 minutes after 5 wrong passwords; the Admin can unlock early [NF-07].
- **Two-step login** for platform roles, Admins, Principal, Accountant, HR and Payroll [NF-09]. Added in 3.2: also Management, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Director, Controller of Examinations, IT Administrator and School IT Support [F-14]. **Changed in 3.3 [A71, C6]:** Changed in 3.3: also the Governing Body Approver [C6, answer 6].
- **Role change:** an Admin adding, removing or re-scoping one of a user's role assignments (USER_ROLE_ASSIGN, Section 26.5) — the affected user is logged out immediately and sees the new role's screens at next login [WF-27].
- **Role switcher:** self-service control (ROLE_SWITCH, Section 26.4) distinct from the Admin-driven role change above — a user with several existing role assignments works in one at a time, selects among their own assignments without logging out, and the active role shows in the header and in every audit entry (full functional rules in Section 5.2.1) [HI-15].
- **Approvals:** approve or reject only, with bulk approval, reminders, no self-approval and delegation (Section 7.0).

### 11.1 Product Owner

**Role:** SaaS platform owner. **Scope:** the EDU 360 product: plans, tenants, features, billing, support, security, releases.

Platform overview | Dashboard shows total universities, active tenants, tenants by state (Trial / Active / Suspended), revenue, active users, system health; built-in usage counts: logins, attendance marked, fees paid online [R2-13] | Business and system status at a glance | Product planning decisions |

Now also: pricing type (per student per year default, flat, per module); modules and features ticked with checkboxes; SMS limit; usage types (SMS, storage) [MK-03, MK-04, WF-07] | New subscription option created | All future tenants choosing a plan |
| 5. Configure modules for plan | Inside plan → Module Settings → toggle modules (for example Library ON, Placement OFF, Payroll ON) → Save | Tenants on this plan get only the enabled modules | Tenant functionality |
| 6. Configure features inside a module | Library → Feature Control → toggle features (for example Digital Books ON, Inventory Audit OFF) | Controls sub-features | Librarians and students (module users) |

Create tenant *(changed)* | Choose type (University, College or School) → enter name, email, plan, start date, retention period, backup retention → Create | Tenant created with an isolated database (or in the shared database on small plans), in **Trial** (30 days, sample data allowed); first admin account invited [CL-06, MK-05, CL-08, TE-01] | That institution only |

### 12.12 Governing Body Approver *(Changed in 3.3)*

Used only in a tenant where there is no Management. The Tenant Admin creates the account (TENANT_TOP_USERS_CREATE) with two-step login. The role approves or rejects, and sees, only the leave requests for which it is the set approver, and sees no other data [C6, C7, C13, answer 6].

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | Tenant URL → credentials → two-step code | Approver dashboard: pending leave requests only | Own session |
| 2. Principal's leave | Leave → Pending → Approve / Reject (PRINCIPAL_LEAVE_APPROVE), for a standalone college or school, or a college or school under a university that set this role as approver | Principal's leave decided | Principal |
| 3. Vice-Chancellor's leave | Leave → Pending → Approve / Reject (SENIOR_LEAVE_APPROVE) | Vice-Chancellor's leave decided | Vice-Chancellor |
| 4. Data Protection Contact's leave | Leave → Pending → Approve / Reject, for a dedicated Data Protection Contact (SENIOR_LEAVE_APPROVE) | Leave decided | Data Protection Contact |
| 5. Approver changes | Notified whenever the Admin or University Admin changes the leave approver | Accountability | Admin |
| 6. Logout | Logout | Session ends | – |

**Restrictions:** No other tenant data. Remark required on reject. Never approves its own request. The fee fallbacks to the Principal where there is no Management (HI-11, R2-03) stay unchanged [C6].
