## 14. Role workflows – School level

In a school, **students do not log in**, unless the school switches on view-only login for chosen classes (Section 14.7). The parent is the primary digital user and represents the child. Students are protected from mobile exposure, teachers stay accountable, and communication goes through parents.

### 14.1 School Admin

**Purpose:** manage the school's academic structure, users, students, attendance governance, exams, fee coordination, communication and reporting.

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | School portal → email and password → two-step code → Login | School-level operational control | Only this school |
| 2. Dashboard | Classes, students, teachers; attendance, fee and exam status; notifications; usage analytics; failed SMS list | School health snapshot | – |
| 3. Create classes | Menu → Classes → Create → class name, academic year → Save | Class created | Teachers, students |
| 4. Create sections | Class → Add Section → name | Class grouping created | Teachers, students |
| 5. Create subjects | Menu → Subjects → Create → assign to class; subject groups where needed | Curriculum defined | Teachers |
| 6. Teacher accounts | Menu → Users → Create User → role Teacher → assign class and subject | Teacher gets login access | Academic delivery |
| 7. Student records *(changed)* | Menu → Students → import template / checked bulk upload / manual add (or from Admissions) → class and section; auto student ID [MD-29] | Students appear in class lists (records only, no login unless switched on) | Teachers |
| 8. Parent accounts *(changed)* | Student → Link Parent → parent contact; parents matched by mobile; up to 3 guardians, one primary; activation code to the parent's mobile | Parent monitoring access enabled | Parents |
| 9. Class teachers | Menu → Class Management → Assign Class Teacher | Class responsibility defined | Teachers |
| 10. Attendance rules (C) | Menu → Academic Settings → Attendance Rules → minimum % per subject and overall; twice a day by default, per period optional [AT-01] | Attendance policy enforced | Students, parents |
| 10a. Leave, risk and notification settings (C) *(V3)* | Leave types and sandwich rule; risk thresholds; optional notifications [Q8] | Institution rules set | Parents, staff |
| 11. Monitor attendance | Menu → Attendance → Summary → class-wise | Attendance discipline control | Teachers |
| 12. Attendance alerts | System sends absent, low-attendance and continuous-absence alerts to parents; Admin views flagged students and delivery failures | Parents informed | Parents |
| 13. Attendance corrections *(changed)* | Menu → Attendance → Correction Requests → Approve / Reject. **Moved in 2.0** to the School Principal or Vice-Principal [AP-14]; the School Admin now views only | Attendance updated | Students, parents |
| 14. Exam patterns (C) | Menu → Exam Settings → Patterns → internal and external marks; grade bands | Exam structure applied | Teachers |
| 15. Internal exams *(added)* | Schedule within the calendar | Exams set | Students |
| 16. Monitor marks | Menu → Results → Entry Status → pending teachers; Class Teacher review status | Delays chased | Teachers |
| 17. Results status *(changed)* | Menu → Results → Approval Status → wait for School Principal approval | Admin cannot approve results | Principal |
| 18. Publish results | Menu → Results → Publish (enabled only after School Principal approval) [AP-16] | Parents can view results; parents notified | Parents |

## 15. Notifications and alerts catalog

Every alert goes to the in-app notification center and as a push notification on the installable app [OB-13]. Email and SMS follow the institution's settings. *(Changed in 2.0: Version 1.0 said email and SMS follow each user's preferences, and that because the product was web-only there were no mobile push notifications, with browser notifications optional. The web app is now installable on phones with push notifications [OB-13], and users cannot switch notifications off [CM-14].)* SMS carries only the subject or heading; details are in the app [CM-15]. Between 9 pm and 7 am nobody can send messages to teachers or parents, and automatic alerts are held until 7 am. Emergency notices go out on all channels at once, and security messages the user triggers (login codes, password reset, new-phone alert) are sent immediately [CM-02, CM-18]. WhatsApp is Phase 2 [CM-07].

### 15.2 Optional notifications (each institution ticks what it wants) [CM-16]

Account created; password reset; new-device login; role changed; delegation started or ended; term locked; hall ticket withheld; payment failed; trial ending.

### 15.3 Delivery failures [CM-17]

A failed SMS or email shows to the sender; the Admin sees a list of parents with wrong numbers. Each institution registers its own SMS sender ID and templates under India's DLT rules [CM-08]. Attendance is always saved first; alerts are retried automatically and failures are visible to the Admin [TE-21]. Added in 3.1: every delivery attempt is recorded with its status and the provider's outcome where available, so retries and failures can be audited [PQ-55].

## 16. System architecture

EDU 360 is built with **React** (web front end), **Spring Boot** (services), **PostgreSQL** (relational database) and **RESTful APIs**. Version 1.0 described deployment on **AWS** with an equivalent **Azure** design; v1 now runs on AWS in India only, with the design kept portable to Azure [TE-05, TE-06]. It uses separate services from day one, Keycloak for login, RabbitMQ or Amazon SQS for messages, and OpenSearch for search. Each tenant gets its own isolated database by default; small tenants can use a shared database with row-level security.

&#91;embedded content: EDU 360 architecture · web, gateway, services, data, integrations]

In words (added in 3.2): every request goes from the installable React web app (push notifications, drafts kept offline, tenant subdomain) to the API gateway and load balancer (tenant taken from the token and subdomain, request keys, REST /v1), which checks identity with Keycloak (one-time codes, two-step login, SSO, roles). It then reaches separate Spring Boot services on EKS: Platform and Tenant, Access and RBAC, Users and Records, Academic, Attendance, Exams and Results, Finance, Leave, Communication, Reporting and Governance in Phase 1; Payroll, Library, Placement and Admissions in Phase 2. The services use PostgreSQL (a database per tenant plus a platform database), SQS / RabbitMQ for events and alerts, OpenSearch for global search, S3 for files, backups and the write-once audit, and external services for payments, SMS (DLT), email, push and meeting tools. Everything runs in AWS Mumbai / Hyderabad; Phase 3 services (hostel, transport, alumni, research, API) are added later.

The browser (the installable web app) talks only to the gateway; Keycloak and the access service check identity and rights (permissions), then each service reads and writes the tenant's own database in India, and calls external services through adapters.

### 16.0 Non-negotiable rules the architecture enforces

- Multi-tenant and hierarchical: System → Tenant → Institution (College / School) → Department → Program → Year → Semester → Section → User (Version 1.0: System → University → College / School → Department → Class / Section → User).
- Tenant data isolation: a new tenant is created with an isolated database (shared database with row-level security on small plans).
- RBAC: every user can access only the data their role and scope permit; academic, financial and governance functions are isolated; approval power comes only from approval chains.
- Business rules in Section 7 are enforced in the service layer, not only in the screens: only assigned faculty (or substitutes) mark attendance; results publish only after approval; only eligible students apply for jobs; fee structures lock at session start; every approval chain is a state machine; nobody approves their own request.

### 16.1 Final technical decisions

| Topic | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Front end | React, one responsive web app, installable on phones with push notifications; drafts saved when the connection drops [OB-13, PR-03] |
| Services | Separate Spring Boot services from day one [TE-02]. *(Version 1.0 allowed a modular monolith at first)* |
| Database | PostgreSQL; own database per tenant by default; shared database with row-level security for small plans [TE-01] |
| Message queue | RabbitMQ or Amazon SQS [TE-03] |
| Login system | Keycloak: passwords, one-time codes, two-step login, SSO [R2-17] |
| Cloud | AWS only in v1; design kept portable to Azure [TE-05] |
| Data location | India regions only (AWS Mumbai / Hyderabad) [TE-06] |
| Tenant detection | From the login token; must match the subdomain; the X-Tenant-ID header only for API keys and never trusted alone [TE-07] |
| Repeated clicks | Every payment and approval call carries a unique request key; repeats are ignored [TE-08] |
| Concurrent approvals | First action wins; the second sees “already actioned by <name>” [TE-09] |
| Permission changes | Take effect within 1 minute; a changed user is logged out at once [TE-10, WF-27] |
| Files | Virus scan; allowed types only; download links expire after 15 minutes; every download checked against permissions [TE-11] |
| Exports | Download links expire after 24 hours; downloads logged [TE-12] |
| Search | OpenSearch from day one [TE-13] |
| Domains | Subdomain for all; custom domain on higher plans [TE-14, R2-14] |
| Time zone | Per tenant, default India time [TE-15] |
| API versions | Old version supported for 12 months after a new one [TE-16] |
| Sensitive fields | Field-level encryption [TE-17]; Aadhaar last 4 digits only [R2-34] |
| Tenant setup failure | Retried safely; half-made tenants cleaned up; Platform Admin alerted [TE-19] |
| Attendance and alerts | Attendance saved first; alerts retried automatically; failures visible to the Admin [TE-21] |
| Audit logs | Write-once storage separate from the main database, with integrity checks [AU-06] |
| Environments | Development, Staging (like production, fake data) and Production [R2-15] |
| Security test | One outside security test before launch [R2-28] |
| Next document | A field-by-field data dictionary [TE-20] |

### 16.2 Services (modules as bounded contexts)

Each module is one or more Spring Boot services with a matching area in the React app.

| Service | Responsibilities |
| --- | --- |
| Platform and Tenant | Tenant onboarding and lifecycle (Trial / Active …), plans and limits, feature switches, billing, usage counts and platform analytics, releases |
| Identity (Keycloak) / IAM | Login, one-time codes (OTP), two-step login (MFA), SSO, session and password policy, devices |
| Access and RBAC | Roles, custom roles, action lists, scopes, delegation, RBAC mapping |
| Users and Records | Users, guardians and parent linking, bulk upload, students, student profiles, staff records, IDs, statuses, imports, search |
| Academic | Structure, courses, programs, semesters, subjects and subject groups, timetable, online-class meetings and links, assignments, study material, calendar, promotion |
| Attendance | Student attendance, rules, marking, corrections, Not held, substitutes, term lock, defaulter and risk lists, risk recalculation trigger |
| Exams and Results | Patterns, schedules, hall tickets, marks, approval chains, GPA / CGPA, publishing, withdrawal, backlogs (moderation: later phase) |
| Finance | Fee policy, structures and versions, exceptions, installments, scholarships, concessions, penalties, gateway payments, receipts, ledger, reminders, period lock (refunds: later phase) |
| Leave | Student and staff leave, length-based routing, balances, substitutes |
| Communication | Notices, messages, notifications, push, SMS (DLT), email, community feed, events, complaints, student notes, policies |
| Reporting and Analytics | Fixed cross-module reports, risk analytics, buyer dashboard, statutory exports, PDF / Excel |
| Governance and Compliance | Approval engine and workflows, audit logs, policies, accreditation, data-protection requests, exports, deletion, RBAC mapping |
| Phase 2 services | HR and Payroll (salary structures, payroll, payslips), Library (catalog, loans, reservations, fines, inventory), Placement (companies, jobs, eligibility, applications, interviews, offers), Admissions (Student Lifecycle), WhatsApp |
| Phase 3 services | Campus Services (Hostel, Transport), Alumni, Research (projects, publications, grants), API governance |
| Supporting | File storage with virus scan, OpenSearch, scheduler, notification delivery, integration adapters (payment, SMS, email, SSO, meeting tools) |

Version 1.0 listed 17 services: Platform and Tenant Management; Identity and Access (IAM); User Management; Academic; Attendance; Examinations and Results; Student Lifecycle (admissions, profiles, leave, records, alumni); Finance; HR and Payroll (including staff attendance, now a later phase); Placement; Library (including e-resources, now a later phase); Campus Services; Communication; Reporting and Analytics; Governance and Compliance; Research; Supporting services. All are kept in the table above.

### 16.3 Key data flows

**Tenant onboarding (Product Owner)**

1. The Product Owner (or Sales, from a demo request) creates a tenant: POST /platform/tenants (name, type, plan, branding, domain, retention).
2. The Platform service validates the plan and records the tenant (in Trial) in the central platform database.
3. The provisioning orchestrator creates the isolated database (or schema), runs migrations, and stores connection details in the tenant registry; failures are retried safely and half-made tenants cleaned up.
4. Initial configuration is applied: feature toggles, limits, the Keycloak realm, the first admin user, and an invitation email.
5. An audit entry is written.

**Mark attendance (faculty or teacher)**

1. The teacher logs in and receives a token with tenant, role and assignment claims.
2. The UI posts to /tenants/{tid}/attendance/mark with class, section, subject, date and the status list.
3. The Attendance service checks tenant context, role, assignment (or substitute) and the midnight window; an unassigned teacher gets 403.
4. Rows are stored first and an attendance.marked event is published.
5. The Notification service sends per-subject in-app absence alerts and queues the daily SMS summary; the Risk service recalculates risk flags.

**Publish results (approval chain)**

1. Faculty save marks as Draft, then Submit (locked for faculty).
2. The HOD approves (college) or the Class Teacher reviews (school).
3. The Principal approves.
4. Publish is enabled: the Controller of Examinations publishes (college under a university on EDU 360), the College Admin (standalone or external-university college), or the School Principal or School Admin (school).
5. Grade sheets are generated, students and parents are notified, and audit entries are written. A rejection closes the submission; the teacher creates a new one.

**Student leave**

1. A student or parent posts /tenants/{tid}/leave (dates, reason).
2. The Leave service computes working days (calendar, sandwich rule) and length, sets status Pending, and routes to the approver chain for that length (Section 7.1).
3. Each approver acts; on final approval the Attendance service marks the days as approved leave; every step notifies the requester (and the college parent).

**Fee payment**

1. The payment starts with a unique request key → gateway.
2. A verified webhook or server check marks it Paid; one receipt per gateway payment ID.
3. The ledger is updated; the payment appears in the daily collection report.

**Placement application** *(Phase 2)*

1. The Placement Officer posts a job with eligibility rules.
2. The student applies; the Placement service checks eligibility against academic data.
3. Shortlists, interviews and offers trigger notifications to the student and parent.

### 16.4 REST API design

- **Authentication:** OAuth2 / OpenID Connect through Keycloak; JWT access tokens carrying tenant_id, roles, active role, permissions and scope. Refresh tokens; session timeout set by policy (Section 11.0). A successful `POST /v1/tenants/{tenantId}/me/active-role` call (Section 5.2.1) replaces the active-assignment context for the session and issues an updated token reflecting the newly selected assignment, scope and permissions — it does not create a new login session or require re-authentication.
- **Tenant context:** resolved from the login token, which must match the subdomain (for example uni-x.edu360.example.com); the X-Tenant-ID header only for API keys and never trusted alone [TE-07]. Every call carries Authorization: Bearer token.
- **Endpoint groups:** /platform/tenants, /platform/plans, /platform/releases; /auth/login, /auth/refresh, /auth/logout, /auth/sso/callback; /tenants/{tid}/users (and /users/bulk-upload, /roles); /structure; /courses, /subjects, /timetable; /attendance; /exams, /results, /results/approve; /fees, /payments, /invoices; /payroll; /leave; /notices, /messages; /library/books, /library/loans; /placements/jobs, /placements/applications; /admissions; /hostel; /transport; /community; /reports/*; /governance.
- **Conventions:** versioned paths (/v1, /v2 for breaking changes; old versions supported for 12 months); standard HTTP status codes; structured error bodies with an error code and audit id; pagination, filters and sorting on lists; bulk endpoints accept CSV and XLSX with row-level validation; unique request keys on payment and approval calls; rate limits per plan (API usage limits).

| Identity | User (type, status), Role, CustomRole, Permission / Action, UserRole (scope, effective from / to), Delegation, Device, Guardian (primary flag) |
| Organization / Structure | Tenant, University, College, School (Institution, status Draft / Active / Blocked), Department, Program, Year, Semester, Class, Section (each linked to its parent), Subject, SubjectGroup, MentorAssignment, AcademicCalendar, WeeklyOff |
| People | StudentProfile (enrollment number, admission date, program / course, class, parents, status incl. Detained), ParentLink, FacultyProfile, StaffProfile, StaffDocument, Assignment (several per staff) |
| Academic | Course, CourseOffering, SubjectAllocation, Timetable, MeetingLink, Assignment, Submission (late flag), Feedback, StudyMaterial, Promotion |
| Attendance | Attendance (student, subject, date, status Present / Absent / On approved leave / Not held, recorded by), AttendanceCorrection, TermLock, RiskFlag |
| Exams | ExamRule, ExamPattern, GradeBand, Exam, HallTicket, Marks (Draft / Submitted / HOD Approved / Principal Approved / Rejected / Published, special codes), Result, ResultPublication, Backlog, SupplementaryRegistration; ReEvaluation (later phase) |
| Finance | FeePolicy, FeeStructure (version, status), FeeException, Installment, Scholarship, Concession, Payment (Started / Pending / Paid / Failed, gateway ID, request key), Receipt (void flag), Penalty, LateFeeWaiver, FinancialPeriodLock, Credit; Refund (later phase) |
| HR and Leave | LeaveType, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest (requester, for student, unit, dates, reason, days counted, route, current approval level, final approver, status), Substitute; StaffAttendance (later phase); SalaryStructure, Payroll (period, components, net pay, approved by), Payslip *(Phase 2)* |
| Services (Phase 2–3) | LibraryBook, Loan, Reservation, Fine; Company, PlacementJob, PlacementApplication, InterviewSchedule, OfferLetter; ApplicationForm, Admission, MeritList; Hostel, HostelRoom, HostelAllocation; Route, Vehicle, RouteAssignment; Alumni; ResearchProject, Publication, Grant |
| Communication | Notice, Message, Notification (audience, delivery status), Delivery, CommunityPost, Comment, Event, RSVP, Complaint, StudentNote (correction link), Policy, PolicyAcceptance |
| Governance | ApprovalRequest, ApprovalStep, AuditLog (user, active role, action, entity, old value, new value, time; write-once, immutable), DataRequest, ExportRequest, AccreditationDocument, ApiKey, Webhook |

Attendance and marks are high-volume tables: partition them by academic year inside each tenant database.

### 16.6 RBAC enforcement

- Role definitions and permissions come from the master matrix (Section 10) and the action list (Section 26). The RBAC Mapping Layer keeps the matrix, custom roles and the live policy tables in step.
- Each service checks permissions through central policy middleware with a Redis cache; permission changes take effect within 1 minute.
- Permissions carry entity-level conditions, for example ATTENDANCE_MARK also checks that the user is assigned to that subject and class (or is the substitute for that date); parent access is limited to linked children.

### 16.7 Integrations

- Payment gateway: Razorpay by default (Stripe or PayU possible), with verified webhooks for payments (refunds are a later phase); UPI, cards, net banking, wallets.
- SMS gateway: alerts and one-time login codes, under India's DLT rules with each institution's sender ID and templates.
- Email service (Amazon SES or SendGrid): notices, invoices, result alerts; push notifications for the installable app.
- SSO (SAML / OIDC) through Keycloak: optional for universities.
- Meeting tools (Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams): online class meetings created automatically, built by the platform in Phase 1.
- File exports in Tally, UDISE+, AISHE and affiliating-university formats; direct connections later.
- External LMS or MOOC: integration through LTI or API only; hosting is out of scope.
- Cloud storage (S3; Azure Blob in the portable design): study materials, documents, offer letters, exports, backups.

### 16.8 Deployment (AWS, India regions)

| Layer | AWS (v1) | Azure (portable alternative from Version 1.0; not used in v1) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web front end | CloudFront + S3 (installable web app; subdomain per tenant) | Azure CDN + Static Web Apps |
| Gateway | Amazon API Gateway + Application Load Balancer | Azure API Management |
| Compute | EKS (Kubernetes) running separate Spring Boot services and workers | AKS |
| Identity | Keycloak cluster *(Version 1.0: custom OAuth2 server or Cognito)* | Keycloak *(Version 1.0: custom OAuth2 server or Entra ID)* |
| Database | RDS PostgreSQL, one database per tenant (shared Multi-AZ cluster with row-level security for small plans) | Azure Database for PostgreSQL (flexible server per tenant or shared) |
| Messages / events | Amazon SQS or RabbitMQ *(Version 1.0: Amazon MSK (Kafka) or RabbitMQ)* | Azure Service Bus / Event Grid |
| Cache | ElastiCache (Redis) for sessions and permission cache | Azure Cache for Redis |
| Search | OpenSearch | Azure AI Search or Elasticsearch |
| Files and backups | S3 with virus scanning and lifecycle rules | Azure Blob Storage |
| Audit | Write-once storage (e.g. S3 Object Lock) | Immutable Blob Storage |
| Secrets | Secrets Manager | Key Vault |
| Monitoring | CloudWatch, Prometheus, Grafana | Azure Monitor + Application Insights |
| CI/CD | Pipeline (CodePipeline) → ECR → EKS; Development, Staging, Production; canary / blue-green deploys of the single version | Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions → ACR → AKS |

### 16.9 Multi-tenant database strategy

- **Default: database per tenant.** Strongest legal and logical isolation. Provisioned automatically when the tenant is created.
- **Shared mode for small tenants:** one database with tenant_id on every row and PostgreSQL row-level security. A tenant can be migrated from shared to isolated as it grows. The mode is set per tenant in Platform Administration [TE-01].

### 16.10 Security, observability and compliance

- Audit logs for every sensitive action, write-once and immutable, with integrity checks.
- Daily backups; backup retention set per tenant when it is created [WF-02] (Version 1.0 default: configurable per plan, 5 years).
- Encryption at rest and in transit (TLS); field-level encryption for sensitive fields.
- Secrets in a managed vault.
- Least-privilege access; platform administration separated from tenant administration.
- Vulnerability scanning, one outside security test before launch, and a hotfix and rollback process tied to Release Management.

### 16.11 Reporting and scaling

- Reports read from read replicas or a reporting store, so they do not slow daily work. Cross-tenant platform analytics use a data warehouse (Redshift; Synapse in the Azure design) with no tenant personal data, anonymous and combined.
- Exports run as background jobs that write CSV or XLSX to storage and notify the user.
- Services autoscale on Kubernetes; RBAC policies are cached; heavy tables are partitioned.

### 16.12 Implementation checklist

- [ ] Tenant provisioning automation (database per tenant + shared mode) with retry and clean-up; Keycloak realm per tenant
- [ ] OAuth2 / JWT with tenant, role, active role and assignment claims; one-time codes and two-step login
- [ ] Policy middleware loaded from the master matrix and the action lists per role; scopes, custom roles, role switcher, RBAC mapping
- [ ] Approval engine and state machines for leave, results, fee structure, fee exceptions, concessions, payroll, notices and community posts (Section 7): approve / reject only, no self-approval, skip logic, bulk approval, reminders, delegation, concurrency
- [ ] Rule checks: assigned-faculty attendance, publish-after-approval, fee lock, placement eligibility, hall ticket eligibility
- [ ] Length-based leave routing; working-day counting
- [ ] Attendance window, Not held, substitutes, term lock with timed unlock
- [ ] Marks states, special codes, range checks, publish-after-approval, withdrawal
- [ ] Fee policy ranges and exceptions; payment states; idempotent receipts; gap-free numbering
- [ ] Tenant schema migrations and templates
- [ ] Write-once audit writes for every sensitive operation, with masking and sensitive-view logging
- [ ] Backup, retention, export and DPO-approved deletion
- [ ] Notification service with templates for every row in Section 15: quiet hours, emergency override, daily SMS summary, DLT templates, failure lists
- [ ] Pass/fail checks in Section 21 automated before release

### 16.13 Source architecture details carried forward

The original architecture in Source 1 (written for React, Spring Boot, SQL and REST, cloud-ready for AWS or Azure) is kept here in full detail. Where a later decision changed a point, the change is marked.

**Component relationships (text diagram)**

```
[React web app per tenant / subdomain]
        ↕ REST (Auth: JWT / OAuth2)
[API Gateway / Load Balancer] → [Auth service (Keycloak; Version 1.0: Spring Boot auth service, stateless)]
                              → [Tenant Management service (with the Tenancy Orchestrator)]
                              → [User Management service]
                              → [Academic service]
                              → [Attendance service]
                              → [Exams & Results service]
                              → [Financial service]
                              → [Library service]          (Phase 2)
                              → [Placement service]        (Phase 2)
                              → [Reporting service]
                              → [Comm & Notification service]
                              → [Integration adapters (Payment, SMS, Email, meeting tools)]
All services → [Relational SQL database(s)] (per tenant or shared)
All services → [Redis cache] (sessions and policy cache)
Async tasks  → [Message broker] (RabbitMQ or Amazon SQS; Version 1.0: Kafka / RabbitMQ)
Async workers (scheduled and background jobs)
File storage → [S3] (Azure Blob in the portable design)
Search       → [OpenSearch / Elasticsearch]
Monitoring   → [Prometheus + Grafana, CloudWatch] (Azure Monitor in the portable design)
```

- The React front end calls the API gateway, which enforces tenant routing and rate limits, then routes to internal services (RESTful contract).
- The auth service issues JWT tokens with claims: role, tenant_id, scope, permissions. Every request carries the tenant context and the JWT.
- Services consult the central RBAC (or a local policy cache) to authorize actions (for example, only assigned faculty may mark attendance).

**Authentication detail.** OAuth2 Authorization Code flow for SSO; JWT for internal calls; token includes tenant_id, roles[], permissions[] and scope. *(Changed: tenant context now comes from the token and must match the subdomain; the X-Tenant-ID header is only for API keys and never trusted alone [TE-07].)*

**Additional API detail.** Marks: POST /tenants/{tid}/exams/{examId}/marks (stored as draft); the HOD reviews pending marks and approves with POST …/approve (HOD-approved state); later approvals follow the chain; when all approvals are complete the Examination service moves the result to PUBLISHED and triggers the publication job (grade sheets). Leave approvals: POST …/approve by each approver. Placement: POST /tenants/{tid}/placements/jobs; POST /tenants/{tid}/placements/applications (eligibility validated). Plans and tenants: POST /platform/plans (plan name, price, user limit, storage limit, API limit) → toggle module features → POST /platform/tenants (provisions the tenant and its isolated database, runs migrations, tenant.status = CREATED; now Trial) → PATCH /platform/tenants/{id}/status = ACTIVE → tenant users can log in. Attendance: /tenants/{tid}/attendance (mark, summary, corrections) with classId, sectionId, subjectId, date and the presence list. Platform endpoints are authenticated with a platform-level role; reports are role-limited.

**Entity detail from the source ER model** (primary keys pk; foreign keys fk)

1. Platform (pk platform_id).
2. Plan (pk plan_id): user_limit, storage_limit, api_limit, enabled_modules (now also pricing type, SMS limit, usage types).
3. Tenant (pk tenant_id, fk plan_id): name, domain, branding, status, db_connection_info (if isolated database).
4. User (pk user_id, tenant_id): username, email, password_hash, user_type (Student / Faculty / Staff / Parent / Admin / ProductOwner), status. Passwords are now held by Keycloak.
5. Role (pk role_id, tenant_id): name (Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, HOD, Teacher, Student, Parent, Product Owner, Platform Admin, etc.), plus custom roles.
6. Permission (pk permission_id): granular permission records (e.g. ATTENDANCE_MARK, RESULT_APPROVE, FEE_EDIT) – now the action codes in Section 26.
7. UserRole (user_id, role_id, effective_from, effective_to; now with scope).
8. Organization: University, College, School, Department, Class, Section – each with pk and fk to its parent (hierarchical); now also Program, Year, Semester.
9. StudentProfile (student_id, user_id, enrollment_no, admission_date, course_id, class_id, parent_ids[]).
10. FacultyProfile (faculty_id, user_id, department_id, designations).
11. Course, Subject, CourseOffering (course_offering_id, subject allocations).
12. Timetable (timetable_id, course_offering_id, room, faculty_id, slot).
13. Attendance (attendance_id, student_id, subject_id, date, status, recorded_by_user_id, approved flag). Only assigned faculty can create records; corrections create AttendanceCorrection records for approval.
14. Exam (exam_id, exam_type, start_date, end_date, pattern_id); Marks (marks_id, exam_id, student_id, subject_id, marks, status draft / hod_approved / principal_approved / published; now also submitted and rejected).
15. FeesStructure, Invoice, Payment, Scholarship – financial entities; invoice state machine (draft / approved / paid / adjusted). Fee edits only before the academic session starts.
16. Payroll (payroll_id, staff_id, period, salary_components, net_pay, approved_by) – requires approval *(Phase 2)*.
17. LeaveRequest (leave_id, requester_id, for_student_id, start_date, end_date, reason, current_approval_level, status) – multi-level approvals.
18. Assignment, Submission, Feedback.
19. LibraryBook, Loan, Fine.
20. PlacementJob, PlacementApplication, InterviewSchedule, OfferLetter – only eligible students may apply; status tracking and reports.
21. AuditLog (log_id, user_id, action, target_entity, old_value, new_value, timestamp) – required for compliance.
22. Notification (notification_id, tenant_id, audience, delivery_status).

Cardinalities: Tenant 1..* → University / College / School (hierarchy enforced); a student has many Attendance rows (by date and subject); Exam 1..* → Marks (one mark record per student per subject); PlacementJob 1..* → PlacementApplication. Attendance and marks tables are high-volume: partition by academic_year (and student cohort, or tenant in the shared database); with a database per tenant, partitioning by year is still advised.

**RBAC mapping from the source.** Product Owner: full platform access, tenant management, plan creation, feature toggles, release control. Platform Admin: manage tenants, releases, support, global admin panels (now Manage, with pricing and deletion kept by the Product Owner). University roles, College Admin, Principal, HOD, Teacher / Faculty, Student, Parent, Librarian, Placement Officer, Accountant, Payroll Officer and HR Manager: permissions per the Role Permission Matrix (Section 10), implemented as role definitions with claims enforced by the auth service. Policy evaluation runs in a central authorization service or policy middleware in each service, using cached role-permission mappings.

**Integration detail from the source.** Payment gateway (Razorpay / Stripe / PayU) for fee payments and invoices (Added in 3.2: Razorpay is the decided default [FE-30]; Stripe and PayU are alternatives only), using webhooks (refunds are a later phase); SMS gateway for urgent notifications and one-time codes (attendance alerts, exam and hall-ticket updates); email service (SES / SendGrid) for institutional emails, invoices and result notifications; SSO identity providers (SAML / OIDC), which universities often want; external LMS / MOOC through LTI or API (hosting content is out of scope); cloud storage for study materials and scanned documents; backup and export adapters for tenant export and data archival.

**Deployment detail from the source (AWS).** Users → CloudFront (React app per tenant subdomain) → API Gateway (regional) → ALB → EKS (Spring Boot services: auth service, tenancy orchestrator, module services for Academic, Attendance, Exams, Finance, Library, Placement, Reporting and Communication, and async workers for scheduled and background jobs) → Redis (ElastiCache) for session and policy cache → event bus → RDS PostgreSQL (isolated tenant databases, or a Multi-AZ cluster for the shared mode) → S3 (study materials, invoices, backups) → OpenSearch. Monitoring: CloudWatch + Prometheus + Grafana. CI/CD: CodePipeline → ECR → EKS (canary / blue-green), tied into Release Management. Secrets: AWS Secrets Manager. Backups: RDS snapshots + S3 with lifecycle rules for retention. *(Changed: Version 1.0 and the source mapped Release Management to selective deploy and rollback per tenant; v1 deploys one version to all tenants [R2-26]; the identity layer is Keycloak, not Cognito [R2-17].)* Azure alternative (portable design): Azure CDN + Static Web Apps, Azure API Management, AKS, Azure Database for PostgreSQL (flexible server per tenant or one server with schemas), Blob Storage, Service Bus / Event Grid, Azure Monitor / Application Insights, Key Vault, and Azure Functions for scheduled tasks – it maps 1:1 to the AWS design.

**Multi-tenant database detail.** Default database per tenant – safest for logical and legal data isolation – with automated RDS provisioning and migrations. Hybrid mode for small tenants: shared database with tenant_id columns and PostgreSQL row-level security plus strict policy, an on-demand migration path from shared to isolated as the tenant grows, and the mode marked per tenant in Platform Administration.

**Observability, reporting and scaling detail.** All actions (user creation, fee edits, approvals) are logged in AuditLog with old and new values, immutable. Encryption at rest (RDS encryption) and in transit (TLS). The Reporting service aggregates data from tenant databases, or reads the event stream for near-real-time dashboards; tenant-level and platform-level analytics (usage, revenue). Long-running analytical queries run against read replicas or dedicated reporting databases to avoid slowing daily work. Exports run as background jobs to storage and notify the user. Services autoscale (EKS; AKS in the portable design); databases per tenant use read replicas for reporting; RBAC policies and role mappings are cached in Redis to avoid repeated database lookups; reports and heavy joins for cross-tenant analytics go to a data warehouse (Redshift; Synapse in the portable design).

**Operational governance from the source.** Release Management: tenant-level targeted deploys (select tenants) with canary or blue/green – *changed to one version for all tenants in v1* [R2-26]. Billing: the platform holds plan definitions and a billing engine that generates invoices (approve invoice, apply discount flows) and connects to payment provider webhooks. Support: ticketing routes to the Support Manager – the source's SLA tracking fields are *not in v1* [R2-27].

**Source developer hand-off checklist (kept).** Finalize the tenant database strategy (database per tenant by default) and automate provisioning. Authentication and RBAC: an OAuth2 server (now Keycloak; the source named Cognito or Azure AD as options) with JWT claims for role- and tenant-based authorization. Authorization middleware enforcing: ATTENDANCE_MARK only by assigned faculty; RESULT_PUBLISH only after approvals; FEE_EDIT only before the academic session begins; multi-level approval for leave, results and payroll. Canonical data model SQL migrations and DDL templates (tenant schema template). AuditLog triggers or service-level audit writes for all sensitive operations. Backup policy and export feature (per the Product Owner workflow).

**What the source architecture was grounded in.** The EDU 360 introduction, role hierarchy and multi-tenant structure; the module definitions (Library, Placement, Attendance, Exams, Results, Fees, Payroll, Communication, Reporting); tenant creation with an isolated database in the Product Owner workflow; the role permission matrix and examples for Product Owner, University, College, HOD, Teacher and Student; the attendance and leave rules (“Only assigned faculty can mark attendance”, “Attendance adjusts automatically after approval”); feature control, billing, plan limits and release management steps.

### 16.14 Phase 1 engineering rules (added in 3.1)

These rules come from the Phase 1 decision register (Section 27). They add to Sections 16.0–16.13; nothing there changes.

- **Modules and entitlements:** modules are independently controllable entitlements and configuration; permissions and navigation are scoped to tenant, institution and plan where applicable, with authorization and dependency controls kept [PQ-01].
- **Feature flags and rollout:** configuration and feature flags control availability, with dependency and permission checks, activation audit, monitoring and safe disabling and recovery. They never mean different app versions for selected tenants in Phase 1 (one version for all [R2-26]); disabling a feature does not reverse data or schema changes automatically [PQ-05, PQ-82].
- **Configuration versioning and precedence:** platform defaults, tenant overrides and institution overrides apply in an explicit order of precedence, set per setting in detailed design (open item 20). Configuration changes are validated, versioned, audited and safely reversible; historical records keep the rules that applied when they were created; configuration can never weaken security, authorization or mandatory audit controls [PQ-06, PQ-74].
- **Configurable fields:** custom fields have validated types, permissions and audit, and never bypass authorization or validation [PQ-03].
- **Module dependencies:** required and optional dependencies are declared; unsafe disabling is blocked; records and audit are kept; dependency combinations are tested; optional dependencies fail gracefully [PQ-73].
- **Identifiers:** internal identifiers are globally unique; external identifiers (such as student IDs) are unique within their defined scope [PQ-23].
- **Isolation in both database modes:** isolation is enforced at the database, application and API layers. Business logic is independent of the isolation mode; provisioning, migration, backups, reporting and transfers work in both modes (Section 16.9). Automated cross-tenant and cross-institution tests cover reads, writes, search, reports, exports, files and jobs [PQ-64, PQ-70].
- **Internal API contracts:** Phase 1 has shared internal API contracts, validation and error conventions and compatibility rules, with consistent tenant isolation, authorization and auditing (Section 16.4). Documented APIs and extension boundaries are used for future integrations and modules; external API and integration governance stays Phase 3 (Section 8.29) [PQ-07, PQ-71].
- **Schema migrations:** backward-compatible or staged where needed; tenant data, relationships, audit and financial integrity kept; tested on representative data in both isolation modes; run consistently, with partial failures detected and retried and checks, backup, recovery and verification defined. Where rollback is unsafe, a tested forward fix or restoration plan is used [PQ-72].
- **Audit storage:** the immutable write-once audit store is separate from the main database, with integrity checks, scoped exports, configurable retention and no secret leakage (Section 7.14) [PQ-65].
- **Backups and recovery:** daily backups alone cannot meet the 15-minute recovery point, so transaction-log / point-in-time recovery is used, with encryption, restricted access, failure monitoring and regular restoration tests (Section 17) [PQ-68].
- **Observability:** structured logs, metrics, tracing and correlation IDs, actionable alerts, tenant-aware diagnostics, sensitive-data masking and controlled access. Operational logs are kept separate from the immutable audit. The monitoring tools named in Section 16.8 stay the baseline; alert thresholds, log retention and on-call arrangements are set before launch (open item 17) [PQ-75].

## 17. Non-functional requirements (final targets)

The source files set no measurable targets. Version 1.0 proposed starting points to confirm with the engineering team and the first customers. These targets are now final decisions; the Version 1.0 proposal is kept beside each one so nothing is lost. Added in 3.1: these targets stay the baseline; the Phase 1 decision register asks for them to be confirmed as launch thresholds, with the evidence needed for each, before launch (open item 15) [PQ-78].

| Area | Final target | Version 1.0 proposal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Availability | 99.5% monthly in the first year; 99.9% after [NF-01] | 99.9% monthly uptime for the web app and APIs, excluding announced maintenance windows |
| Performance | 95% of pages under 2 s; 95% of API calls under 500 ms; attendance for 60 students saved under 1 s [NF-02] | Same: 95% of page loads under 2 seconds; 95% of API calls under 500 ms; attendance submission for a 60-student class under 1 second |
| Peak load | 10× normal for 1 hour on results day and fee deadlines, load-tested on Staging [NF-03, QA-05] | Result publishing and fee deadlines: designed for 10× normal traffic for 1 hour |
| Scale | No fixed v1 target; later phase [NF-04] | Up to 1,000 tenants and 1 million users on one platform deployment, scaling horizontally |
| Devices | Current Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox, plus Android Chrome up to 2 versions old; 360 px phones [NF-05] | Responsive web on current Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox; usable on 360 px-wide phone screens |
| Accessibility | WCAG 2.1 AA on parent, student and teacher screens [NF-06] | WCAG 2.1 AA |
| Language | English only in v1 [CM-13] | English first; text kept in resource files so other languages can be added (still applies) |
| Security | Lockout for 15 minutes after 5 wrong passwords; Admin can unlock early [NF-07]. Passwords and two-step login as in Section 11.0 [R2-12, NF-09]. TLS 1.2+; encryption at rest; field-level encryption for sensitive fields; one outside security test before launch | TLS 1.2+; encryption at rest; two-factor login for admin and platform roles; account lockout after 5 failed attempts; password and session policy set by the Product Owner |
| Backup and recovery | At most 15 minutes of data lost; back online within 4 hours [NF-10]. Daily backups; backup retention set per tenant [WF-02]. Added in 3.1: transaction-log / point-in-time recovery, because daily backups alone cannot meet the 15-minute point; encryption, restricted access, failure monitoring and restoration tests [PQ-68] | Daily backups; point-in-time recovery 7 days; recovery point under 24 hours; recovery time under 4 hours |
| Retention | Set per tenant when it is created [CL-08, AU-02]. Added in 3.1: hybrid retention with controlled archival and deletion and legal-hold checks; exact durations need policy confirmation (open item 20) [PQ-29] | Default 5 years after a record closes, configurable per tenant |
| Audit | 100% of create, edit, delete, approval, login, export and denied actions logged; logs write-once and immutable (Section 7.14) | 100% of create, edit, delete, approval, login and export actions logged; logs immutable |
| Data protection | Configurable per institution: consent records, access and correction requests (Data Protection Contact), retention, export, deletion with DPO approval (Section 22) | Configurable per institution: consent records, access and correction requests, retention, export, deletion with DPO approval |
| Data location | India only (AWS Mumbai / Hyderabad) [TE-06] | – |
| Notifications | In-app within 1 minute; SMS and email handed to the provider within 5 minutes [NF-13] | Same |
| Permission changes | Effective within 1 minute [TE-10]. Added in 3.1: covers role, employment, assignment and entitlement changes [PQ-20] | – |
| Maintenance window, support SLA | Not in v1 [NF-11, R2-27] | SLA tiers per plan (for example critical issues answered within 1 hour) |

## 18. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Tenant | The paying customer: a university (or group) with everything under it, a standalone college or a standalone school; has its own database by default (small plans share one) |
| Institution | A college or school inside a tenant |
| Management | Owner / trust role above the Principal in private institutions <br>**Changed in 3.3 [A123, C9]:** (Changed in 3.3: a governing body, not staff [C9].) |
| Product Owner | The company that owns and runs EDU 360 as a SaaS product |
| Plan | Subscription package: pricing type, price, ticked modules and features (enabled modules), user, storage, SMS and API limits |
| Trial | 30-day tenant state before Active; read-only after it ends until payment |
| Data Protection Officer (DPO) | Platform role that approves full-tenant exports and deletions |
| Data Protection Contact | The tenant's person who handles personal-data requests |
| RBAC | Role-based access control: what a user can do depends on their role and scope |
| Scope | The part of the hierarchy a user's role applies to (platform, tenant, university, college, school, department, class, own child) |
| F / M / C / A / V / R / N | Full / Manage / Configure / Approve / View / Request / No access (Section 6.2). Version 1.0 had F / M / A / V / R / N (Full Access / Manage / Approve / View Only / Request / No Access) |
| C (Configure) | Permission letter for setting up rules and settings |
| Action list | Detailed per-role permissions (e.g. MARKS_ENTER, RESULT_PUBLISH) that developers build from |
| Action code | Unique name of one thing a user can do (e.g. RESULT_WITHDRAW); used for access checks, tests and custom roles (Section 26) |
| Custom role | A role an institution Admin creates with any rights |
| Role switcher | Control for a user with several roles to choose the active one |
| Approval chain | Ordered approvers for a request (Section 7.1) |
| Delegation | Temporary hand-over of approvals to a same-or-higher role (Version 1.0: a Principal's hand-over to the Vice-Principal). Added in 3.2: or to the designated deputy – Principal → Vice-Principal, college and school [D-001] |
| Exception request | Request to save a fee outside the policy range |
| Concession | One-off discount for one student, approved by the Principal |
| Scholarship | Scheme with rules for many students |
| Daily collection report | The day's payments, sent to the Principal |
| Fee policy | University-level (or standalone Management / Principal) fee rules – heads, ranges, schemes – within which colleges and schools set fee structures |
| Fee structure | The fee components, amounts and due dates for a course or class |
| Program | A course of study in a department (e.g. B.Sc. Physics), with years and semesters |
| Subject group | Students from several sections taking one subject |
| Mentor / class coordinator | Faculty member assigned to a section; final approver for short student leave |
| Not held | Attendance mark for a cancelled period; left out of the percentage |
| Term lock / lock period | Principal's lock on attendance and marks edits (unlock lasts at most 3 days) / Accountant's lock on a closed financial month |
| Attendance risk | Normal / Warning / Critical status from the attendance percentage (Section 7.7) |
| Academic risk | Flag raised by low marks, low attendance, continuous absence or missed assignments (Section 7.7) |
| Defaulter list | Students below the minimum attendance |
| Community feed | Institution social feed for events, achievements and announcements |
| Hall ticket | Admit card for an examination |
| Backlog | A failed subject to be cleared in a supplementary exam |
| Detained | Student status for a student not promoted at year end |
| No-dues check | Dues must be cleared before certificates or TC |
| Deletion certificate | Record of who deleted a tenant, when and what |
| Staging | Copy of production with fake data, used for testing |
| DLT | India's registration system for SMS sender IDs and templates |
| SSO | Single sign-on with the institution's own identity system |
| MFA | Multi-factor authentication (two-step / two-factor login) |
| SLA | Service level agreement for support response and resolution (not in v1) |
| HOD | Head of Department |
| Tenant Admin (3.2) | The top Admin of a tenant: the University Admin in a university tenant; the College Admin or School Admin in a standalone tenant. Creates the Management, Data Protection Contact and Vice-Chancellor accounts [F-12] <br>**Changed in 3.3 [A124, Answer 6]:** (Changed in 3.3: and the Governing Body Approver account [answer 6].) |
| Governing Body Approver (Changed in 3.3) | Tenant role used where there is no Management; approves or rejects only the Principal's (standalone), the Vice-Chancellor's or a dedicated Data Protection Contact's own leave, and sees nothing else [C6, C13] <!-- A122 --> |

## 19. Change log and decisions

Version 2.0 applies 447 decisions from two rounds of questions (EDU 360 – Final Decisions v1.1) and 10 open-item answers. Version 2.1 applies the 10 fixes and 4 wording clean-ups from the Version 2.0 review. Version 3.0 is the master copy of everything: it restores all Version 1.0 and source wording that Version 2.0 had shortened, adds the action list per role and applies its 11 answered questions. From now on, every edit gets a change-log row and a new version number [R2-42]. **Changed in 3.3 [A125]:** Changed in 3.3: Version 3.3 applies the Product Owner decisions of 27 October 2026 (Section 19.14).

## 20. Default formulas

Every institution starts with these formulas and can change them [R2-37, AT-05, OB-16].

| Measure | Default formula |
| --- | --- |
| Attendance % (per subject) | Present ÷ (periods held − periods on approved leave) × 100. “Not held” periods and holidays are not counted as held |
| Attendance % (overall) | Same formula, adding up all subjects |
| Attendance risk | Normal ≥ 75%; Warning 65–75%; Critical < 65% [RK-01] |
| Pass % | Students who passed ÷ students who appeared (AB not counted) × 100 |
| GPA (one semester) | Sum of (grade point × credits) ÷ sum of credits |
| CGPA | Same formula across all completed semesters |
| Outstanding fees | Amount billed + late fees − scholarships − concessions − amount paid − credit balance |
| Fees paid online % | Amount paid online ÷ total amount paid × 100 |
| Placement % *(Phase 2)* | Students placed ÷ eligible students who registered × 100 |
| Weekly active teachers % | Teachers who logged in at least once in the last 7 days ÷ active teacher accounts × 100 |
| Parent login % | Parents who logged in during the last 30 days ÷ parent accounts × 100 |
| Trial-to-paid % | Trials that became paid ÷ trials that ended × 100 |
| Renewal rate | Tenants that renewed ÷ tenants due for renewal × 100 |

Worked example: a student with 40 periods held in a subject, 2 of them on approved leave, and 30 present has 30 ÷ (40 − 2) × 100 = 78.9%, which is Normal.

## 21. Pass/fail checks for high-risk rules

These checks cover permissions, approvals, money and marks only [R2-41]. QA writes all other test cases [DC-04]. Every one must pass before release.

| # | Situation | Must happen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A user from one tenant asks for a record of another tenant (changes the ID in the address or API) | Refused; nothing shown; attempt logged; Admin alerted on repeats [AU-05] |
| 2 | A parent changes the student ID to another child's | Refused; nothing shown |
| 3 | A platform role (Support, Billing, Platform Admin) tries to read tenant academic or fee data through screens, API or export | Refused, unless the tenant Admin has granted Support read-only access for that ticket (24 hours); every view is logged [WF-11] |
| 4 | A user with two roles submits a request and is also the next approver | Their step is skipped; the reason is logged [AP-04] |
| 5 | Someone calls “publish results” before the final approval | Refused; no result published; no notification sent |
| 6 | A teacher not assigned to a class marks its attendance | Refused, unless assigned as substitute for that date [AT-03] |
| 7 | A teacher edits attendance after midnight | Refused; only a correction request is allowed [AT-02] |
| 8 | Attendance or marks are edited after the term is locked | Refused; an unlock needs a reason and relocks after 3 days [AT-09] |
| 9 | Marks are rejected | The old submission stays locked; the teacher must make a new submission [R2-01] |
| 10 | A fee value outside the policy range is saved | Refused unless an exception was approved by the Finance Director (or Management) and the Principal, or by the Principal alone where there is no Management [R2-03] |
| 11 | The browser shows “payment success” but the gateway has not confirmed | Payment stays Pending; no receipt [FE-07] |
| 12 | The gateway sends the same confirmation twice | One payment, one receipt [FE-09] |
| 13 | The Accountant marks an online payment paid by hand | Allowed only with a gateway reference number; logged [R2-33] |
| 14 | A receipt is cancelled | Needs Principal approval; its number stays as “void” [FE-12] |
| 15 | An Admin bulk-corrects marks, attendance or fees | Changes go into the approval chain, not straight into the records [R2-32] |
| 16 | Two approvers act on the same request at once | First wins; the second sees “already actioned by <name>” [TE-09] |
| 17 | A user's role is changed while they are logged in | Logged out at once; new rights at next login [WF-27] |
| 18 | A delegate approves after the delegation dates | Refused; pending items are back with the original approver [AP-09] |
| 19 (3.2) | The Vice-Principal, acting as the Principal's delegate, approves their own leave or a request they already acted on | Refused; the item waits for the Principal or goes to Management [D-001, AP-04] |
| 20 (3.2) | An HOD delegates approvals to a Professor | Refused; only same-or-higher roles or the Principal → Vice-Principal pair are allowed [D-001] |
| 21 (3.2) | A Principal approves their own leave | Refused; there is no self-approval [D-002] |
| 22 (3.2) | An institution tries to go live without a Principal's-leave approver, or the approver is missing when the Principal applies | Go-live refused; a pending request is blocked (never skipped or auto-approved) and the Admin and Management are warned [D-002, OI-A] <br>**Changed in 3.3 [A128, C7]:** (Changed in 3.3: also when the tenant tries to go live without the Vice-Chancellor's-leave approver (university tenant), or that approver is missing when the Vice-Chancellor applies. Applies to every institution, including those under a university. The warning goes to the Admin and to Management, or the Governing Body Approver where there is no Management [C7].) |
| 23 (3.2) | A Driver or Security Supervisor opens reports or audit logs | Refused; only roles with Reports or Governance letter not N [F-6] |
| 24 (3.2) | A mentor tries to reject student leave of more than 2 days | Not possible; the mentor can only forward it with a remark [F-11] |

## 22. Privacy and legal

- Data protection rules are generic and configurable per institution [PV-01].
- The institution owns its data; EDU 360 processes it on the institution's behalf under a data processing agreement signed with each customer [PV-02].
- Parents give consent during admission or onboarding; it is recorded with the date [PV-03].
- College parents see attendance, results and fees by default. The student is told and can ask the institution to limit this (legal check needed) [PV-04].
- After a data breach, the platform tells the institution within 24 hours; the institution informs the authorities and people as the law requires [PV-05]. Added in 3.1: incident response covers detection, an owner and escalation, containment, internal escalation, legally required external notification, evidence preservation, recovery checks and closure records; severity levels and external notification deadlines need legal and business confirmation (open item 18) [PQ-69].
- Personal-data requests are handled by the tenant's Data Protection Contact; no fixed time limit [PV-06, R2-25]. Added in 3.1: each request is tracked with an ID, status, owner and history; the requester's identity is verified, retention and legal holds are checked and the outcome is recorded; the DPO approves full-tenant exports and deletions. Response deadlines need legal and business confirmation (open item 18) [PQ-67].
- Platform analytics use only anonymous, combined numbers; customers can opt out [PV-07].
- No AI features in v1 [PV-08]. Only the last 4 digits of Aadhaar are stored [R2-34].
- All data stays in India (AWS Mumbai / Hyderabad) [TE-06].
- Terms of service, privacy policy and the data processing agreement are written by the internal team [PV-09].
- Lawyer checks before launch: PV-04, college health notes visible to parents (R2-29), and no time limit for data requests (PV-06).

## 23. Testing and release

- Every rule and workflow step gets an ID [DC-03]. Each rule ID has at least one positive, one negative and one permission test [QA-06].
- Environments: Development, Staging (like production, generated fake data) and Production [R2-15]. Only generated fake data is used for testing [QA-03].
- Load tests on Staging for results day and fee deadlines (10× normal for 1 hour) [QA-05].
- One outside security test before launch [R2-28]; security claims are used in marketing only after it.
- The QA lead signs off acceptance testing [QA-01]. The Product Owner decides each time whether a release can go out with known bugs [QA-04]. Added in 3.1: both stay; institution UAT is also part of acceptance, and its named approvers, release-blocking severity levels and the named final go / no-go authority are open items 14 and 16 [PQ-76, PQ-78].
- Pilot with 3–5 institutions for one term before public launch [QA-07]; KPI targets are set after the pilot. Added in 3.1: 3–5 institutions for one term stays the starting plan; the exact pilot workflows and modules, number of institutions, duration, success targets and defect thresholds are confirmed in pilot planning (open item 13). Before public launch the pilot must show workflow acceptance, security and isolation verification, data integrity, operational stability, institution UAT, a known-issue review and a formal go / no-go [PQ-79].
- Releases go to all tenants as one version; rollback is app-only [R2-26]. Added in 3.1: feature flags may control availability but never mean different versions for selected tenants (Section 16.14) [PQ-05, PQ-82].
- Added in 3.1 – test types: requirement-traceable acceptance tests; unit, integration and end-to-end tests; tenant-isolation and permission tests; migration and financial-integrity tests; regression testing; documented evidence and UAT. Coverage targets and release-blocking severity are open item 14 [PQ-76].
- Added in 3.1 – scope register: a register of the Phase 1 modules, workflows, roles, dependencies, exclusions, defects and approvals is kept. Incomplete functionality is hidden, and a module is never switched on while a dependency is missing [PQ-77].
- Added in 3.1 – launch readiness: public launch needs evidence for critical workflows, RBAC and isolation, data integrity, performance, security and privacy, UAT, defect review, monitoring, backup and recovery, and support readiness, followed by a formal evidence-based go / no-go decision (Section 27.14) [PQ-78].
- Added in 3.1 – support: support ownership, hours, severity levels, response and resolution targets, escalation, incident tracking, communications and security escalation are defined before the pilot. No contractual SLA is offered in v1 [R2-27]; hours, staffing, targets and any contractual commitment are agreed before they are promised (open item 17) [PQ-80].
- Added in 3.1 – change approval: every material change needs a formal change request with the business reason, an impact and risk assessment, and explicit approval before it is built; it is traced to requirements, design, tasks, tests and releases and recorded in the version-controlled change log. Emergency changes get controlled handling and a review afterwards. The approvers and the final conflict decision-maker are open item 16 [PQ-81].

### 25.2 Risks accepted

| Decision | Risk | Safeguard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fully custom roles [R2-02] | An Admin could give themselves any right, such as entering marks | Every rights change is logged and the Principal / Management is notified (built in) |
| Cheque bounce not handled [FE-10] | A bounced cheque stays “paid” until the receipt is cancelled | Accountant cancels the receipt with Principal approval |
| Cash checked only by the daily report [R2-33] | One person still takes and records cash | Principal reviews the daily report every day |
| No time limit for data requests [PV-06]; generic privacy law [PV-01] | India's data protection law may set deadlines | Lawyer check before launch |
| College health notes visible to parents [R2-29] | College students are adults | Lawyer check together with PV-04 |
| Audit logs exportable by anyone who can view them [AU-03] | Logs can still reveal sensitive activity | Exports are logged; sensitive fields masked |
| Separate services from day one [TE-02] | More cost and time for the first release | None needed if the team is ready |
| Release with known bugs decided case by case [QA-04] | Serious bugs may ship | Product Owner decision each time |
| No platform tax in v1 (open item 5) | Invoices may need GST under Indian tax law | Confirm with a tax adviser before the first invoice |

## 26. Action list per role (new in Version 3.0)

Section 26 lists all 262 actions (219 in Phase 1, 32 in Phase 2, 11 in Phase 3); from Version 3.2, 270 actions (226, 32 and 12): every action, who may do it, what it is limited to and what is never allowed. Because of its size it is in its own tab of this document: 26 · Action list per role. The same list, with the full rules and a role-by-action grid, is in the companion Excel (EDU 360 Action List V3.2). **Changed in 3.3 [A130]:** Changed in 3.3: 278 actions (234, 32 and 12); 8 new Phase 1 actions. Replace label: EDU 360 Action List V3.3.


**Changed in 3.3 [A130]:** the separate Section 26 tab is replaced by the V3.3 tab, reproduced in full below.


This tab is Section 26 of the EDU 360 Final Master Product Document, Version 3.3. It sits in its own tab because of its size; the rest of the document is in the main tab.

EDU 360 has 262 actions: 219 in Phase 1, 32 in Phase 2 and 11 in Phase 3. Version 3.2 adds 8 actions: 270 in all (226 in Phase 1, 32 in Phase 2, 12 in Phase 3) [D-002, F-7, F-11, F-12, F-13]. Changed in 3.3: Version 3.3 adds 8 actions, all Phase 1: 278 in all (234 in Phase 1, 32 in Phase 2, 12 in Phase 3) [C2, C6, C7, answers 6–8, letter gaps]. Each action is one thing a user can do; developers build every access check from it, testers test every line, and institution Admins pick from it when they build custom roles [R2-02, RL-05]. The companion Excel (EDU 360 Action List V3.3) also gives, for every action, the full rules the system checks, what is never allowed and the source, plus a role-by-action grid.

### 26.1 Rules for every action

1. Approval actions act only at the chain step the role holds (Section 7.1); nobody approves their own request or acts at two steps of one request – the step is skipped and logged [AP-04]. Added in 3.2: there is no self-approval anywhere, including the Principal's own leave [D-002].
2. Every action is checked on the server against role, scope and state – never only in the screen. Added in 3.1: rights are scope-bound and never inherit broader access by accident; a user with several roles acts in one active role at a time [PQ-16, PQ-17].
3. Every create, edit, delete, approval, export, login, denied attempt and view of sensitive data is logged [7.14, AU-01, AU-05]. Added in 3.1: actions that view, export, correct or delete sensitive personal or financial data are marked in the Sensitive data column of the Action List V3.1; their rights are given explicitly, never by default [PQ-66].
4. Platform roles never reach tenant data, except Support under tenant-granted 24-hour ticket access [WF-11].
5. A delegate can use approval actions only for the delegated dates [AP-07]. Added in 3.2: delegation goes to a same-or-higher role, or to the one designated deputy – Principal → Vice-Principal (college and school); the deputy never acts on a request they raised, are the subject of or already acted on [D-001].
6. A role can also get any action through a custom role; “Never allowed” items stay blocked whatever the custom role says.

# Appendix C — Historical decision records (text extraction of the two decision PDFs)

Carried unchanged from the C1 master (its Appendix H). Text extracted from *EDU 360 Final Decisions v1.1* (40 pages) and *EDU360 Phase 1 Requirements Decision Register* (14 pages); the PDFs stay in the source archive. Layout follows the PDF text layer.

## C.1 Final Decisions v1.1 (40-page PDF text extraction)


EDU 360 — Final Decisions v1.1




  EDU 360 — Final Decisions v1.1
    Oct 22, 2026         · ​@Pratheesh S


  How to use this document
  This document holds every decision from both rounds of questions (447 answers), ready
  to copy into the EDU 360 Final Master Product Document. Where Round 2 changed a
  Round 1 answer, only the final decision appears here.

        Order: sections follow the main document, from Introduction to the change log. Each
        change names the main-document section it belongs to.
        Replace / Add / Remove: each change says whether to replace existing text, add new
        text, or delete text.
        Decision IDs in brackets (for example [AP-11], [R2-01]) point back to the question you
        answered. They are kept so anyone can trace why a rule exists.
        "Later phase" means the feature is not built in v1. All of these are collected in the last
        section [R2-31].
        "Configurable" means each institution sets its own value; the default shown is what a
        new institution starts with.
        New version: after you paste these changes, set the main document to Version 1.1 and
        add one change-log row per edit [R2-42].


  Summary and release phases
  EDU 360 v1 launches in India for universities, colleges and schools together, built in three
  phases, with approvals only through approval chains and nobody ever approving their
  own request.

  The ten decisions that change the main document most

   1. Launch market is India only; the design must allow other countries later [PR-01]. All
      three customer types launch together [PR-02].
   2. Modules are built in three phases (table below) [OB-02].
   3. A tenant is the paying customer. Colleges and schools inside it are "institutions". Only
        tenants are billed and suspended [RL-01].




                                                                                              Page 1 of 40
EDU 360 — Final Decisions v1.1




   4. Approval power comes only from approval chains. The letters F and M never include
      approving [RL-03].
   5. Nobody approves their own request or acts twice in one chain; the system skips them
      to the next approver and logs why [AP-04].
   6. There is no "send back". Approvers approve or reject only; rejected marks are entered
      again as a new submission [R2-01].
   7. Institution Admins can create fully custom roles and give any right to any role [R2-02].
   8. New roles: Management, University HR Manager, Data Protection Contact, Student
      (School). Removed: Alumni login [PR-07, RL-09, RL-08, R2-39, R2-40].
   9. Login runs on Keycloak, data stays in India (AWS Mumbai / Hyderabad), each tenant
      gets its own database by default [R2-17, TE-06, TE-01].
 10. One outside security test runs before launch; security claims are used in marketing
        only after it [R2-28].

  Release phases [OB-02]


     Phase                       Modules

     Phase 1 (v1)                Users and roles, institution setup, academic
                                 structure and timetable, attendance, exams and
                                 results, fees, leave, communication (notices,
                                 messages, notifications, community feed), reports

     Phase 2                     Payroll, library, placement, admissions

     Phase 3                     Hostel, transport, alumni, research and
                                 publications, API and integration governance

     Later phases                Everything marked "not applicable in v1" or "out of
                                 v1" (full list in the last section)


  Rules written in this document for Phase 2 and 3 modules are final decisions, built when
  that phase starts.


  Sections 1–5: Introduction, hierarchy, objectives, scope, overview
  The product shape is now fixed: India, all three customer types, web app installable on
  phones, and a clearer college structure.




                                                                                          Page 2 of 40
EDU 360 — Final Decisions v1.1




  Section 1 – Introduction: replace the "Product shape" bullets
        Market: India only in v1; prices in INR. The design must allow other countries to be
        added later [PR-01].
        Customers (tenants): a university with its colleges and schools, a standalone college,
        or a standalone school. All three launch together [PR-02].
        Access: one responsive web app, installable on phones, with push notifications [OB-
        13]. It needs internet; forms save drafts so nothing is lost when the connection drops
        [PR-03]. No native Android or iOS apps in v1.
        School model: school students do not log in, except that a school may switch on login
        for chosen classes (for example 9–12). Those students see only timetable, homework,
        study material, attendance and results; no messaging, fees or leave [PR-04, R2-39].
        College model: college students and their parents both log in. All college students
        follow the same rules, whatever their age [PR-05].
        Outside systems: v1 exports files in the formats of Tally, UDISE+, AISHE and affiliating-
        university portals. Direct connections come later [PR-06].
        Management: private institutions get a Management role above the Principal (Section
        6) [PR-07].


  Section 2 – Hierarchy
        Replace the college academic structure with: Department → Program → Year →
        Semester → Section → Students → Parents. The number of semesters per year is
        configurable [HI-01, HI-02].
        Add: subjects can be taught to "subject groups" that mix students from several
        sections (electives) [HI-05].
        Add: one staff member can hold several assignments (departments, institutions), each
        with its own scope [HI-06].
        Add – year-end promotion: the Admin runs bulk promotion; the Principal approves;
        failed or detained students are left out with a reason [HI-03]. Repeating a year is not
        supported in v1 [HI-04].
        Add – parents: one parent login shows all their children inside the same tenant; a child
        in another tenant needs a separate login [HI-07].
        Add – staff who are also parents: two separate accounts. The staff account logs in
        with email and password; the parent account with a mobile one-time code. The same
        mobile number may be on both [HI-08, R2-16].
        Keep colleges and schools under a university, as written [HI-09].


                                                                                               Page 3 of 40
EDU 360 — Final Decisions v1.1




        Add – external university mode: a college whose university is not on EDU 360 enters
        or imports external marks itself and publishes after Principal approval [HI-10].
        Replace the standalone-tenant sentence about fee policy with: in a standalone
        college or school, Management (or the Principal if there is no Management role) sets
        the fee policy; the Accountant builds the fee structure; the Principal approves it [HI-11].
        Keep: schools have no departments in v1 [HI-12].
        Replace "External users" with: Applicants log in with a mobile or email one-time code.
        Alumni do not log in; their records are kept by the institution and managed by the
        Alumni Coordinator [HI-13, R2-40].


  Section 3 – Objectives
        Add product KPIs [OB-01]: weekly active teachers (%), parents who log in (%), fees
        paid online (%), trial-to-paid conversion (%), renewal rate (%), customer satisfaction
        score (NPS). Targets are still to be set (see open items).
        Remove from v1 "workload monitoring" and "performance monitoring" in 3.6 [OB-03,
        OB-04].


  Section 4 – Scope
  Change "In scope" for v1:

        GPA / CGPA uses a configurable grading scheme (grade points, credits) set by the
        university or standalone institution [OB-06].
        Online classes: EDU 360 creates Zoom, Google Meet or Microsoft Teams meetings
        automatically [OB-07].
        Reports are fixed reports with filters and PDF / Excel export; a custom report builder
        comes later [OB-15].
        ID card data (photo + details) can be exported for a printing vendor [OB-12].

  Move out of v1 (to Later phases):

        Staff attendance [OB-08]; payroll (Phase 2) [OB-09]; workload and performance
        monitoring [OB-03, OB-04].
        Exam moderation [OB-05]; certificate and transcript generation [OB-11]; e-resource
        downloads [OB-14]; accreditation templates such as NAAC criteria [OB-17].
        Fee refunds [R2-21]; tax on student fees [R2-22].

  Add to scope boundaries: when payroll is built, EDU 360 produces payslips only; salaries
  are paid outside the system [OB-10].

  Section 5 – System overview
        Replace the multiple-roles sentence in 5.2 with: a user may hold several roles. Each
        role keeps its own scope; the user gets each (role + scope) pair and never a wider mix
        [HI-14]. The user works in one role at a time using a role switcher; the active role shows
        in the header and in every audit log entry [HI-15].


  Section 6: Tenants, roles and permission letters
  Four roles are added, one is removed, and institutions may now build fully custom roles.


  Tenant and institution (replace the tenant definition)
        A tenant is the paying customer: a university (or group) with everything under it, a
        standalone college, or a standalone school. Colleges and schools inside a tenant are
        institutions [RL-01].
        Only tenants are billed and suspended by the platform. A University Admin can only
        block an institution's access, and only with Vice-Chancellor approval [RL-01, WF-15].
        A standalone college can later join a university tenant; the platform team moves its
        data on request [RL-02].

     F – Full                    Create, view, edit, delete within scope. No
                                 approving.

     M – Manage                  Create, view, edit day-to-day records. No setup, no
                                 approving.

     C – Configure (new)         Set up rules and settings for the area (for example
                                 attendance rules, exam patterns).

     A – Approve                 View, and approve or reject what others submit.

     V – View                    Read within scope.

     R – Request                 Submit requests for yourself or your child and
                                 track them.

     N – No access               Area hidden.


        Approval power comes only from the approval chains in Section 7. F and M never
        include approving [RL-03]. C is new [RL-04].
        The letter table stays as a summary. Developers build from a detailed action list per

        05].
        Where a letter and a role's "Restrictions" line disagree, the action list follows the
        Restrictions line. Example: Admin with M on Exams can set up and monitor exams but
        cannot enter marks [R2-18].
