  Section 7: Business rules
  Approvals become approve-or-reject only, leave approval depends on leave length, and
  attendance and exams get clearer rules.


  Section 7 – replace the opening paragraph
        Each approval step can approve or reject. There is no "send back" [R2-01].
        A remark is required on reject and optional on approve [AP-24]. A rejection ends the
        request; the requester may submit a new one and the old one stays in history [AP-02].
        Approvers can select many requests and approve them together with one optional
        comment; each item is logged separately [AP-25].
        If an approver does not act, the system sends reminders only. The request never
        moves on its own [AP-03].
        Nobody approves their own request or acts at two steps of the same request. The
        system skips them to the next approver and logs why [AP-04]. If the approver at a step
        is the requester, that step is skipped [AP-05].
        If two approvers act at the same moment, the first one wins; the second sees "already
        actioned by <name>" [TE-09].
        When a user is deactivated, their pending approvals move to whoever now holds that
        role, and the Admin is warned [WF-26].

  Replace the delegation sentence with: any approver can hand over approvals to a same-
  or-higher role for set dates [AP-06]. The delegate gets the approval right for those dates
  only, and it is logged [AP-07]. A delegate cannot delegate again [AP-08]. When the
  delegation ends, pending items go back to the original approver [AP-09]. The approver
  can cancel a delegation at any time; this is logged [AP-10].


  7.2 Leave rules – add
        Leave types are configurable per institution. Defaults – students: Sick, Personal, On-
        duty; staff: Casual, Sick, Earned, Maternity / Paternity, Duty, Loss of pay [LV-01].
        Leave can be taken as a full day, half day or per period [LV-02].
        Leave can be applied up to 3 days after the absence (configurable) [LV-03].
        A document (for example a medical note) can be uploaded on any leave. It is never
        required in v1 [R2-10].
        A request that overlaps an existing one is blocked, and the existing request is shown
        [LV-05].
        For college students, the parent is notified of every request and every decision [LV-
        06].




                                                                                               Page 10 of 40
EDU 360 — Final Decisions v1.1




        Before the start date the requester can cancel. After the start date, cancelling needs
        the final approver [LV-07].
        Weekends and holidays inside a leave are not counted, using the calendar. Institutions
        can switch on a "sandwich" rule [LV-08].
        Staff leave balances (simple): HR credits a yearly number per leave type. No carry-
        forward or encashment. The system checks the balance and warns; loss of pay is
        flagged and HR confirms it before payroll [R2-09, LV-10].
        When approving staff leave, the approver (HOD or Principal) assigns a substitute; the
        substitute can mark attendance for those dates [LV-11].
        "On duty" (sports, placement drives) is treated as approved leave [LV-12].
        Approved leave does not count against attendance %, as written. Making this
        configurable is a later phase [LV-13, R2-31].


  7.3 Attendance rules – add or replace
        How often: college – once per subject period. School – twice a day by the teacher; per
        period is optional [AT-01].
        Window: attendance can be marked until midnight the same day; after that only
        through a correction request [AT-02].
        Substitutes: a teacher assigned as substitute by the HOD or Admin can mark
        attendance for that date [AT-03].
        Replace the status list with: Present, Absent, On approved leave, Not held. "Late" is
        removed [R2-23]. A teacher or HOD marks a cancelled period "Not held"; it is left out of
        the percentage [AT-12].
        Percentage formula: configurable per institution, starting from the default formula in
        this document [AT-05, R2-37].
        Minimum attendance: configurable both per subject and overall [AT-06].
        Absence alerts: an in-app alert per subject, sent immediately and only when the
        student is absent; plus one SMS summary per day [AT-07, R2-36].
        Term lock stays in v1: the Principal locks the term. Unlocking needs a reason, lasts at
        most 3 days and then relocks automatically; the HOD and Admin are notified [R2-08,
        AT-09].
        Bulk upload: allowed for the assigned teacher, or for the Admin with Principal approval
        [AT-11].
        Not supported: attendance shortage condonation [AT-08].

EDU 360 — Final Decisions v1.1




  7.4 Exam and result rules – add or replace
        Who owns what (university): the Registrar owns programs and exam rules. The
        Controller of Examinations runs exam schedules, the marks process and result
        publishing [R2-06].
        Exam schedules: the Controller schedules university exams. The College Admin or
        Examination Clerk schedules internal exams within the calendar; both can do it [WF-
        18].
        External marks: the Examination Clerk uploads them; the HOD checks them; they
        follow the same approval chain [EX-01].
        Special codes: AB (absent), MP (malpractice), WH (withheld) and medical-absent [EX-
        02].
        Checks: marks above the maximum or below zero are blocked; a big jump from the
        previous exam shows a warning [EX-17].
        Grading: absolute, with configurable grade bands [EX-16].
        Rejected marks: when the HOD or Principal rejects marks, the teacher sees the
        remark and enters the marks again as a new submission. Faculty cannot edit marks
        after submitting [R2-01].
        Withdraw a published result: the Controller (college) or Principal (school) can
        withdraw it with a reason; everyone is notified; it is logged [EX-07].
        Replace the re-evaluation sentence with: re-evaluation is not in v1. Students and
        parents can only view results [R2-07].
        Backlogs: backlog tracking and supplementary exam registration are in v1 [EX-08].
        Hall tickets: keep as written – withheld for any overdue fee amount, and each check
        can be switched on or off [R2-20]. The Principal can override for one student with a
        reason; it is logged [EX-09].


  7.5 Fee rules – add or replace
        Outside the policy range: blocked; exception request → Finance Director → Principal
        (see 7.1) [R2-03].
        New fee version mid-session: applies to new admissions and future installments only;
        amounts already billed stay [FE-02].
        Students joining mid-year: full fee or pro-rata, configurable per fee head [FE-03].
        Part payments: not allowed; only full installments [FE-04]. Overpayment is kept as
        credit for the next due [FE-05].




                                                                                              Page 12 of 40
EDU 360 — Final Decisions v1.1




        Gateway charges: the institution chooses who pays (institution or payer) [FE-06].
        When a payment counts as paid: only when the gateway confirms by verified
        webhook or server check. States: Started, Pending, Paid, Failed [FE-07]. The
        Accountant can mark an online payment paid by hand only by entering the gateway
        reference number; this also covers payments stuck in Pending [R2-33].
        Duplicates: a second confirmation with the same gateway payment ID is ignored; one
        receipt only [FE-09].
        Cash control: a daily collection report goes to the Principal [R2-33].
        Receipts: never edited. A wrong receipt is cancelled with a reason and Principal
        approval; its number stays as "void"; a new receipt is issued [FE-12]. Numbering is per
        institution, per financial year, with no gaps and a configurable prefix [FE-13].
        Scholarship vs concession: a scholarship is a scheme with rules for many students; a
        concession is a one-off discount for one student, approved by the Principal [FE-17].
        Late fees: configurable [FE-18]. A waiver needs Principal approval and is logged [FE-
        19].
        Locked months: can be unlocked only with Principal approval and a reason; logged [FE-
        20].
        Reports: by both financial year (April–March) and academic year [FE-21].
        One student account: hostel, mess and transport fees are fee heads in the same
        student ledger, with one receipt series [FE-22]. Admission application fees are paid
        through the gateway into the ledger and carried to the student account on admission
        [FE-23].
        No dues check: dues must be cleared before a transfer certificate or other
        certificates; the Principal can override with a reason [FE-24].
        Teachers: see only "dues pending: yes / no", never amounts [FE-27].
        Reminders: automatic 7 days before the due date, on the due date, and 3 and 10 days
        after (configurable); manual reminders also allowed [FE-29].
        Payment methods: whatever the gateway supports – UPI, cards, net banking, wallets
        [FE-30].
        Not in v1: refunds [R2-21], tax on fees [R2-22], sibling discount [FE-25], paying for
        several children at once [FE-26], accounting export [FE-28], cheque-bounce handling
        [FE-10].


  7.6 Payroll rules (Phase 2) – add
        The Principal approves totals only and does not see individual salaries [R2-05].



                                                                                           Page 13 of 40

        The Payroll Officer and HR Manager see individual salaries; the Accountant sees totals
        only [PY-04].
        Both the Payroll Officer and the HR Manager can change salary structures [PY-08]. The
        Payroll Officer's own salary changes need the HR Manager [PY-05].
        Back-dated increments: arrears are calculated automatically [PY-02].
        Not supported: hourly pay for guest faculty [PY-03], loans and advances [PY-07]. Later:

  7.7 Risk flags – add
        Keep the default thresholds; each institution can change them [RK-01].
        Flags are recalculated right after every attendance or marks change [RK-02].
        A flag clears automatically when the student no longer meets the rule; teacher
        remarks are kept [RK-03].
        Parents are alerted only when the level changes (for example Normal → Warning) [RK-
        04].


  7.8 Placement rules (Phase 2) – add
        Eligibility is re-checked at shortlisting; the Placement Officer sees a warning and
        decides [PL-01].
        After placement, a student can apply only for jobs above a package threshold
        (configurable) [PL-02].
        Students have a placement profile with resume upload [PL-05].
        Job packages are visible on posts; individual offers are visible to the student, parent
        and placement team only; reports show totals [PL-07].
        Not in v1: off-campus offers [PL-03], recruiter logins [PL-04], internships [PL-06].


  7.9 Library rules (Phase 2) – add
        Barcode labels printed by the system, used with a USB scanner; manual entry also
        allowed [LB-03].
        Fines configurable per role [LB-04]. The Library Assistant collects fines; only the
        Librarian waives them, with no limit [LB-05, LB-06].
        Later: fines into the student ledger [LB-01], lost-book charges [LB-02].




                                                                                               Page 14 of 40
EDU 360 — Final Decisions v1.1




  7.10 Communication rules – add
        Students cannot message other students [CM-01].
        Nobody can message teachers or parents between 9 pm and 7 am, except emergency
        notices [CM-02].
        Parents contact the Principal through the office only [CM-03].
        Class messages are one-way broadcasts from the teacher; replies come as private
        messages [CM-05].
        Attachments: PDF, JPG, PNG up to 10 MB, virus-scanned [CM-06].
        Comments pass an automatic bad-language filter; Admin and Principal can also hide
        them [CM-10]. No "report abuse" button [CM-04].
        Community posts: like and comment only; remove "share" in v1 [R2-30].
        Users cannot switch off notifications [CM-14].
        SMS carries only the subject or heading; details are inside the app [CM-15].
        Each institution ticks which extra notifications it wants [CM-16].
        Failed SMS or email: the sender sees it; the Admin sees a list of parents with wrong
        numbers [CM-17].
        Each institution registers its own SMS sender ID and templates (India DLT rules) [CM-
        08].
        Not in v1: WhatsApp (Phase 2) [CM-07], read acknowledgments [CM-12], photo
        consent [CM-09], other languages [CM-13].


  7.11 Complaints – add
        No categories or time limits [CP-01]; no anonymous complaints [CP-02]; no reopening
        or rating [CP-04]; staff cannot raise complaints [CP-05]. Committees: later [CP-03].


  7.12 Academic calendar – add
        Local holidays on exam days are blocked with a warning [CL-01].
        When the university changes the calendar mid-year, institutions are notified and
        affected timetables and exams are flagged [CL-02].
        Weekly-off pattern (for example alternate Saturdays) is configurable per institution
        [CL-03].




                                                                                           Page 15 of 40
EDU 360 — Final Decisions v1.1




  7.13 Tenant lifecycle – replace
        States: Created → Trial → Active → Suspended → Archived → Deleted [CL-06].
        Trial: 30 days, sample data allowed [MK-05]. When the trial ends, the tenant becomes
        read-only until it pays [R2-24].
        Suspension is done by the Product Owner by hand [R2-24].
        Retention period is set when the tenant is created [CL-08]. After it ends, the system
        creates a deletion request for the Data Protection Officer to approve [CL-07].
        After deletion, a small "deletion certificate" (who, when, what) is kept by the platform
        [CL-10].
        Export: CSV / Excel per module plus a ZIP of documents, with a data dictionary [CL-09].
        User limit: warning at 90%; new users blocked at 100%; the Admin can request an
        upgrade [WF-01].


  7.14 Audit and data rules – add
        Viewing sensitive records (ID numbers, salaries, health notes) is also logged [AU-01].
        Audit log retention is set when the tenant is created [AU-02].
        Anyone who can view audit logs can export them; the export is logged [AU-03].
        Sensitive fields are masked in the log (ID numbers, bank details, health) [AU-04].
        Denied attempts are logged; repeated attempts alert the Admin [AU-05].
        Logs are kept in write-once storage, separate from the main database, with integrity
        checks [AU-06].
        Admin bulk corrections may touch any data, but changes to attendance, marks or fees
        go through the normal approval chain; everything is logged [R2-32].

  20. Default formulas (new)
  Each institution starts with these and can change them [R2-37, AT-05, OB-16].


     Measure                      Default formula

     Attendance % (per subject)   Present ÷ (periods held − periods on approved
                                  leave) × 100. "Not held" periods and holidays are
                                  not counted as held

     Attendance % (overall)       Same formula, adding up all subjects

     Attendance risk              Normal ≥ 75%; Warning 65–75%; Critical < 65%
                                  [RK-01]

     Pass %                       Students who passed ÷ students who appeared
                                  (AB not counted) × 100

     GPA (one semester)           Sum of (grade point × credits) ÷ sum of credits

     CGPA                         Same formula across all completed semesters

     Outstanding fees             Amount billed + late fees − scholarships −
                                  concessions − amount paid − credit balance

     Fees paid online %           Amount paid online ÷ total amount paid × 100

     Placement % (Phase 2)        Students placed ÷ eligible students who registered
                                  × 100

     Weekly active teachers %     Teachers who logged in at least once in the last 7
                                  days ÷ active teacher accounts × 100

     Parent login %               Parents who logged in during the last 30 days ÷
                                  parent accounts × 100

     Trial-to-paid %              Trials that became paid ÷ trials that ended × 100

     Renewal rate                 Tenants that renewed ÷ tenants due for renewal ×
                                  100

  22. Privacy and legal (new)
         Data protection rules are generic and configurable per institution [PV-01].
         The institution owns its data; EDU 360 processes it on the institution's behalf under a
         data processing agreement signed with each customer [PV-02].
         Parents give consent during admission or onboarding; it is recorded with the date [PV-
         03].
         College parents see attendance, results and fees by default. The student is told and
         can ask the institution to limit this (legal check needed) [PV-04].
         After a data breach, the platform tells the institution within 24 hours; the institution
         informs the authorities and people as the law requires [PV-05].
         Personal-data requests are handled by the institution's Data Protection Contact; no
         fixed time limit [PV-06, R2-25].
         Platform analytics use only anonymous, combined numbers; customers can opt out
         [PV-07].
         No AI features in v1 [PV-08]. Only the last 4 digits of Aadhaar are stored [R2-34].
         Terms of service, privacy policy and the data processing agreement are written by the
         internal team [PV-09].


  23. Testing and release (new)
         Every rule and workflow step gets an ID [DC-03]. Each rule ID has at least one positive,
         one negative and one permission test [QA-06].

## C.2 Phase 1 Requirements Decision Register (14-page PDF text extraction)


                                                                                                    EDU 360
                                                   Phase 1 Requirements Clarification
                                              Structured Requirements & Decision Register
                                        82-question clarification record • Approved directions, open decisions, deferred scope and implementation status



 Purpose. Consolidate the decisions approved in the clarification conversation into a working register for product, engineering, QA and operations.

 Baseline. EDU 360 Final Master Product Document V3.0, its permission matrix and Action List, plus the original 82-question clarification questionnaire.

 Decision integrity. This register summarizes decisions recorded in the conversation. It does not amend the V3.0 master documents and does not claim that any requirement has been implemented,
 tested or accepted in software.




 Status key
 Approved direction = the user accepted the recommendation in the clarification conversation. Details open = the direction is accepted, but specified values, authorities or implementation rules remain
 unresolved. Needs detailed design = a rule requires further specification before implementation.



                                                                                                 Prepared: 23 October 2026




EDU 360 Phase 1 Requirements Decision Register — working document, not implementation evidence                                                                                                             Page 1
 1. Executive summary
 All 82 numbered questions in the supplied questionnaire were addressed in the clarification sequence. The user's short responses such as “ok” and “yes” were treated as approval of the recommendation
 presented immediately before them. This is a decision register, not proof of implementation.

 Baseline constraints to preserve
 • Phase 1 modules per V3.0: users and roles; institution setup; academic structure and timetable; attendance; exams and results; fees; leave; communication (notices, messages, notifications and
 community feed); reports.
 • Phase 2: payroll, library, placement and admissions.
 • Phase 3: hostel, transport, alumni, research and publications, and API/integration governance.
 • One application version across all tenants in Phase 1; feature flags may control availability but do not authorize selective tenant deployments.
 • Approval chains apply; nobody approves their own request.
 • Refunds and partial payments are not Phase 1 features; WhatsApp is Phase 2; custom report builder is later-phase scope.

 V3.0 source references
 The source master document identifies V3.0 as the final master specification and sets a change-control rule: every edit requires a change-log row and new version number; only the sentence affected by a
 decision should change, with other wording preserved. The source document's release phases and change-control statements should govern any future master-document update.

 5. Unresolved decisions and implementation detail
 The following are deliberately not assigned invented values. They require confirmation during detailed design, pilot planning, legal review or operational planning.

 Pilot scope and readiness
 Confirm exact pilot workflows/modules, number of pilot institutions, pilot duration, quantitative success targets and defect thresholds.

 Testing
 Set minimum coverage expectations, release-blocking severity levels and named UAT approvers.

 Performance
 Agree measurable performance/availability thresholds and evidence requirements.

 Governance
 Name approvers for scope/architecture/security/data changes and final go/no-go authority.

 Operations
 Set monitoring/alert thresholds, operational log retention, support hours, staffing/on-call arrangements and response/resolution targets.

 Legal/privacy
 Confirm legal/business deadlines for data requests and external incident notification obligations.

 External reporting
 Confirm pilot institution(s), exact official Tally/UDISE+/AISHE/affiliating-university templates and acceptance criteria.

 Detailed implementation design
 Specify offline attendance synchronization/conflict handling; exact authentication configuration; retention durations; payment method details within V3.0; and precise configuration precedence per setting.

## F.1 Version 1.0

### EDU 360 – Education Management Platform: Final Master Product Document

Oct 22, 2026 · @Pratheesh S

#### Document control

This is the single, final master specification of EDU 360. It merges and replaces three source files, resolves every contradiction between them, and adds the workflows, rules and roles that were missing.

| Item | Detail |

| Product | EDU 360 – Education Management Platform (multi-tenant SaaS) |

**How to read this document**

- Sections 1–5 explain what EDU 360 is, why it exists and what it covers.
- Sections 6–7 define who the users are and the rules every approval follows. Where a workflow and a rule seem to differ, Section 7 wins.
- Sections 8–10 define the modules, what each role gets, and the full permission matrix.
- Sections 11–14 give the screen-level, step-by-step workflow of every role, grouped by Platform, University, College and School.
- Sections 15–18 cover notifications, architecture, non-functional requirements and terms.
- Section 19 lists every decision taken while merging the sources, so nothing is changed silently.

**Conventions used**

- Each workflow step lists **Action** (what the user clicks), **Impact** (what changes in the system) and **Affects** (which roles or records feel the change).
- “Admin” on its own means the administrator of the current level: University Admin, College Admin or School Admin.
- Values marked *proposed* are defaults chosen during merging. Each institution can change them in configuration.

#### 1. Introduction

**EDU 360** is a comprehensive education management platform that centralizes the academic, administrative, financial and human resource operations of universities, colleges and schools in one unified system.

The platform lets institutions manage students, faculty, staff, courses, attendance, examinations, results, fees, payroll, leave and institutional communication through secure, role-based dashboards. EDU 360 supports structured institutional hierarchies, so a university can oversee many colleges and schools while keeping full operational control and data integrity.

EDU 360 provides complete lifecycle management for students and employees: admissions, academic tracking, attendance, examinations, performance evaluation, salary management, leave management and service records. Faculty and staff payroll, leave approvals, workload monitoring and compliance reporting are handled in the same ecosystem.

The platform brings academic administration, HR management, finance, communication and reporting into one system. This reduces operational complexity and removes dependence on many disconnected tools. Built for enterprise-grade security, audit readiness and scalability, EDU 360 gives educational institutions reliable, compliant and future-ready digital governance.

EDU 360 acts as the **single source of truth** for each institution, enabling transparent operations, efficient management and better academic outcomes for every stakeholder.

**Product shape (decided for this version)**

- **Delivery:** a multi-tenant SaaS product run by the Product Owner, sold on subscription plans.
- **Customers (tenants):** a university together with its colleges and schools, or a standalone college, or a standalone school.
- **Access:** one responsive web application used on desktop, tablet and phone browsers. There are no separate native mobile apps in this version.
- **School model:** school students do not log in. Their parent or guardian is their digital representative.
- **College model:** college students and their parents both log in, each with their own access.

#### 2. Institutional and role hierarchy

EDU 360 runs on six levels: **System → University → College / School → Department / Class → Section → User**. Authority, responsibility and data visibility follow this tree. A role sees only its own branch and what sits below it, unless the permission matrix (Section 10) says otherwise.

The Product Owner's team sits outside every tenant; inside a tenant, colleges and schools branch from the university and end at students and parents.

#### 3. Objectives

The primary objective of EDU 360 is to provide a unified, secure and scalable education management platform that centralizes the academic, administrative, financial and human resource operations of educational institutions in one integrated system. The objectives are grouped below for clarity and implementation alignment.

**3.1 Centralization of institutional operations.** Centralize all institutional activities (academic management, staff administration, finance, library services, placement activities and communication) in one digital platform. This removes dependence on disconnected systems and creates a single source of truth for all institutional data.

**3.2 Support for a structured institutional hierarchy.** Implement a hierarchical model that represents real educational institutions, supporting:

- System-level governance
- University-level control
- College- and school-level management
- Department-level administration
- Class- and section-level academic operations
- Student- and parent-level access

This ensures that authority, responsibility and data visibility follow institutional boundaries.

**3.3 Role-based access control and data security.** Enforce strict role-based access control (RBAC) where:

- Every user can access only the data their role permits.
- Academic, financial, administrative and governance functions are logically isolated.
- Conflicts of authority are prevented through permission boundaries.
- Audit readiness and accountability are maintained across all actions.

**3.4 Academic management automation.** Automate and manage academic processes:

- Attendance tracking
- Examination scheduling
- Marks entry and result publishing
- Academic performance monitoring
- Timetable and syllabus access
- Assignment and study material management

This ensures accuracy, efficiency and transparency in academic operations.

**3.5 Student lifecycle management.** Provide complete lifecycle management for students:

- Admission *(added from the Admissions module)*
- Academic tracking
- Attendance history
- Examination records
- Result history
- Fee payments and receipts
- Leave application and approval tracking
- Assignment submissions and learning materials
- Graduation and alumni record *(added from the Alumni module)*

This ensures continuous academic visibility from admission to completion and beyond.

**3.6 Faculty and staff management.** Manage faculty and staff records:

- Staff profiles and service records
- Workload monitoring
- Leave management and approvals
- Payroll and salary processing
- Performance monitoring

This ensures effective human resource administration within the institution.

**3.7 Financial management and transparency.** Manage institutional financial activities:

- Fee structure management
- Scholarship handling
- Installment tracking
- Payment and receipt generation
- Payroll processing
- Financial reporting

This ensures transparency, accountability and audit readiness.

**3.8 Placement and career support management.** Support placement operations:

- Company profile management
- Job posting management
- Student eligibility mapping
- Application tracking
- Interview scheduling
- Offer letter management
- Placement reporting

This ensures structured career support for students.

**3.9 Library resource management.** Manage library operations:

- Book catalog management
- Issue and return tracking
- Reservation handling
- Fine calculation
- Digital library records
- Inventory auditing
- Damaged and lost book tracking

This ensures efficient use of, and accountability for, learning resources.

**3.10 Institutional communication.** Provide official communication channels:

- Notices
- Notifications
- Email and SMS alerts
- Student and parent messaging
- Community feed *(added from the workflows)*

This ensures reliable and traceable institutional communication.

**3.11 Governance, compliance and audit readiness.** Support governance and compliance through:

- Audit logs
- Compliance reporting
- Accreditation documentation
- Approval workflows
- Data protection enforcement

This keeps the institution legally compliant and accreditation-ready.

**3.12 Monitoring and reporting.** Provide reporting and monitoring:

- Academic performance reports
- Attendance summaries
- Examination overviews
- Financial reports
- Institutional performance reports
- Activity logs

This enables informed decisions at every management level.

**3.13 Scalability and future readiness.** Design EDU 360 as a scalable platform that supports:

- Multiple universities
- Multiple colleges and schools
- A growing user base
- Feature expansion
- Long-term digital governance

**3.14 Single source of truth.** Establish EDU 360 as the authoritative system for all institutional information, ensuring:

- Data consistency
- Data accuracy
- Controlled access
- Long-term data integrity

#### 5. System overview

EDU 360 is an enterprise-grade digital system that manages and governs the complete operational lifecycle of educational institutions. It combines academic administration, human resource management, financial operations, library services, placement management, institutional communication and governance in one ecosystem, and acts as the **single source of truth**: data stays consistent, secure and transparent at every level.

**5.1 Platform structure.** The system is hierarchical and multi-tenant. It gives centralized governance while each institution operates independently. The hierarchy is: System → University → College / School → Department → Class / Section → User. Each level works within defined authority boundaries, which control data access and operational responsibility.

**5.2 User-centric role architecture.** Every user is assigned a predefined role. The role decides:

- Functional access
- Data visibility
- Approval authority
- Reporting scope

Roles are grouped into Platform roles, Governance roles, Academic roles, Administrative roles, Support roles, and Student and Parent roles (full catalog in Section 6). A user may hold more than one role (for example a Professor who is also HOD); their access is the union of those roles, within their own branch.

**5.3 Modular design.** The system is divided into independent but integrated modules:

- Academic Management
- Student Lifecycle Management
- Faculty and Staff Management
- Financial Management
- Placement Management
- Library Management
- Leave Management
- Communication
- Reporting and Analytics
- Governance and Compliance
- Extended modules: Admissions, Alumni, Hostel, Transport, Research and Publications, API and Integration Governance

Each module works independently while sharing data through the tenant's central database. The Product Owner can switch modules on or off per plan and per tenant.

**5.4 Data integration and consistency.** All modules use a common data model, which ensures:

- No data duplication
- Real-time data synchronization
- Cross-module reporting
- Historical record preservation

**5.5 Governance and control.** EDU 360 enforces governance through role-based access control, approval workflows, audit logs, compliance reporting and data protection enforcement. This ensures operational accountability and regulatory readiness.

**5.6 Institutional operational coverage.**

- University level: centralized governance
- College and school level: academic and administrative management
- Department level: academic delivery control
- Class level: teaching and learning activities
- Student and parent level: monitoring and participation

**5.7 Communication framework.** Official channels: institutional notices, system notifications, email and SMS alerts, direct messaging between authorized users, and the community feed. All communication is transparent and traceable.

**5.8 Reporting and decision support.** Structured reports cover academic performance, attendance, examination results, financial status, institutional performance and activity audits. Each report is limited to the user's role and authority level.

**5.9 Scalability and extensibility.** The system supports many institutions on one platform, a growing user base, new features, and long-term digital transformation.

**5.10 Operational philosophy.** EDU 360 is a governance platform, not only a management system. It is built for transparency, accountability, operational efficiency, academic quality improvement and institutional compliance.

#### 6. Tenancy model and role catalog

A **tenant** is one paying customer with its own isolated data: a university (with all its colleges and schools), a standalone college, or a standalone school. The Product Owner and platform staff sit outside every tenant and never see a tenant's academic, financial or personal data.

##### 6.1 Permission legend

| Code | Meaning | What the user can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F | Full Access | Create, view, edit, delete, configure and approve within their scope |
| M | Manage | Create, view and edit day-to-day records; no configuration of policy, no final approval |
| A | Approve | View, and approve or reject what others submit; cannot create or edit the records |
| V | View Only | Read within their scope |
| R | Request | Submit requests for themselves (or their child) and track them |
| N | No Access | The area is hidden |

##### 6.3 Role name standards

- “Library Admin” in the source is the **Librarian**.
- “Examination Controller” and “Controller of Exams” are the **Controller of Examinations**.
- “Teacher / Faculty” in college workflows means any of Professor, Associate Professor or Assistant Professor.
- “Class Coordinator” (assigned by the HOD) is an **assignment** given to a faculty member for one class or section, not a separate role.
- “Accountant” without a level means the College Accountant or School Accountant of that institution.

#### 7. Business rules and approval chains

These rules are binding. Every workflow in Sections 11–14 follows them. Each approval step can approve, reject (with a mandatory remark) or send back. A rejection ends the request, and every step notifies the requester (and the parent, where a student is involved).

##### 7.1 Approval chains at a glance

&#91;embedded content: Main approval chains · leave, results, fees, payroll\]

The highlighted box in each lane is where the decision becomes final; the table below adds staff leave, notices, community posts, events and tenant deletion.

| Process | College | School | Standalone tenant |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Student leave | Student or Parent applies → Faculty recommends → HOD approves → **Principal gives final approval**. College Admin monitors only. | Parent applies → Class Teacher approves → **School Principal gives final approval**. School Admin monitors only. | Same as college / school |
| Staff leave (teaching) | Faculty applies → HOD recommends → **Principal approves** | Teacher applies → **School Principal approves** | Same |
| Staff leave (non-teaching) | Staff applies → HR Manager verifies → **Principal approves** | Staff applies → **School Principal approves** | Same |
| University staff leave | Staff applies → HR verifies → **Registrar approves** | – | – |
| Attendance correction | Faculty requests → **HOD approves** | Teacher requests → **School Admin approves** | Same |
| Marks and results | Faculty enters → HOD approves → Principal approves → **Controller of Examinations publishes** | Teacher enters → **School Principal approves** → School Principal **or** School Admin publishes | College: College Admin publishes after Principal approval |
| Fee structure | University Finance Director sets fee policy → Accountant configures structure → **Principal approves** → live | Same as college | Accountant configures → **Principal approves** |
| Refund or concession | Accountant reviews → **Principal approves** | Same | Same |
| Payroll | Payroll Officer generates → HR Manager verifies → **Principal approves** → payslips released → Accountant reconciles | Same (School Principal) | University staff: **Finance Director approves** |
| Institution-wide notice | Admin or Principal: publish directly. Anyone else: **Principal approves** | Same (School Principal) | Same |
| Class or department notice | Teacher or HOD publishes directly | Teacher publishes directly | Same |
| Community post | Admin or Principal: publish directly. Teacher, HOD, Placement Officer: **Principal approves** | Admin or Principal: direct. Teacher: **School Principal approves** | Same |
| Events | Organizer proposes → **Principal approves** | Same | Same |
| University reports and policies | University Admin prepares → approves and publishes; colleges must follow | – | – |
| Tenant deletion | Product Owner requests → data exported → retention period met → **Data Protection Officer approves** → deleted | Same | Same |

The Vice-Principal can approve on the Principal's behalf when the Principal delegates (for a date range or a process), and the audit log records the delegation.

##### 7.2 Leave rules

- A college student or their parent can apply. A school student's leave is always applied by the parent.
- Leave states: Draft → Pending (current approver named) → Approved or Rejected. A requester can cancel while it is pending.
- On final approval, attendance adjusts automatically: the days are marked “On approved leave” instead of “Absent” and do not count against the attendance percentage, unless the institution's attendance rules say otherwise.
- Absence without approved leave is flagged “Unapproved absence” and the parent is alerted.
- Approved staff leave updates the HR record and feeds payroll (loss of pay when leave balance is exhausted).

##### 7.3 Attendance rules

- Only the faculty or teacher assigned to that subject, class and section can mark attendance (statuses: Present, Absent, Late, On approved leave).
- Students and parents have view-only access.
- Any change after submission goes through a correction request (7.1). The original value, the new value and both users are kept in the audit log.
- Minimum attendance percentage is set by the College Admin or School Admin in attendance rules.
- After the Principal locks the academic term, no attendance or marks can be edited. Unlocking needs the Principal and is logged.

##### 7.4 Examination and results rules

- Exam patterns (internal and external split, grading system) are configured by the Admin within the rules set by the Controller of Examinations (university) or the Principal (standalone).
- Marks states: Draft (faculty can edit) → Submitted → HOD Approved (locked for faculty) → Principal Approved → Published. School: Draft → Submitted → Principal Approved → Published.
- **Results can be published only after approval.** The Publish button stays disabled until the final approval is recorded.
- Publishing notifies students and parents. Published results can be changed only through a re-evaluation request approved by the same chain, and the change is logged.
- Hall tickets are generated by the Examination Clerk or Admin. A hall ticket is withheld when attendance is below the minimum or fees are overdue; each institution can switch either check on or off.

##### 7.5 Fee rules

- The University Finance Director sets the **fee policy** for the colleges and schools under the university: fee heads, allowed ranges, scholarship schemes, refund and penalty policy. The University Accountant maintains the data.
- The College or School Accountant configures the **fee structure**, installments, scholarships and late-fee penalties inside that policy. The structure goes live only after the Principal approves it. The Admin and Principal can view collections.
- **Fee edits are allowed only before the academic session starts.** After that, the structure is locked. Scholarships, fines, refunds and concessions still work, each with an approval and an audit entry. A mid-session change needs a new structure version approved by the Principal.
- Payments: online through the payment gateway (default Razorpay, INR, GST configurable) or offline (cash or cheque) entered by the Accountant. A receipt is generated for every payment.
- The Accountant can lock a financial period. Locked months cannot be edited.

##### 7.6 Payroll rules

- The Payroll Officer configures salary structures and deductions, then generates payroll from staff attendance and approved leave.
- **Payroll is released only after approval:** HR Manager verifies, then the Principal approves (the Finance Director for university staff). Payslips are then released to staff.
- The Accountant has view access to payroll summaries for reconciliation.
- Staff attendance is entered or uploaded by HR. Biometric devices are out of scope.

##### 7.7 Risk flags and alerts

All thresholds are configurable per institution. Defaults *(proposed)*:

| Flag | Default rule |
| --- | --- |
| Attendance risk: Normal | Attendance at or above 75% |
| Attendance risk: Warning | Attendance from 65% up to 75% |
| Attendance risk: Critical | Attendance below 65% |
| Continuous absence | Absent 3 or more working days in a row |
| Low marks | Score below the subject pass mark |
| Academic risk | Any of: low marks, attendance Warning or Critical, continuous absence, 2 or more missed assignments in a month |

A flagged student shows on the parent dashboard as an Academic Risk Warning, with teacher notes, and appears on the risk lists of the teacher, HOD and Principal.

##### 7.8 Placement rules

- The Placement Officer sets eligibility for each job (for example CGPA, active backlogs, department, year).
- The system filters eligible students automatically. **Only eligible students can apply.**
- Students track their application status. Parents of college students can view job posts and their child's application status.
- Interview results: Selected, Rejected or Waitlisted. The student accepts or declines an offer in the system. The Placement Officer marks the student Placed.

##### 7.9 Library rules

- One copy can be issued to only one user at a time.
- Fines follow the institution's library policy.
- Only the Librarian can update inventory.
- Issue limits per role are set by the College Admin or School Admin in library settings.

##### 7.10 Communication rules

- Teachers can message students (college) and parents; parents can message the class teacher and the school or college office; students can message their teachers.
- Every message and notice is stored and traceable.
- Community comments can be hidden by the Admin or Principal; hiding is logged.

##### 7.11 Complaints, issues and escalations

- Students and parents raise complaints. The Principal or Admin assigns each one to an owner, who resolves it or escalates it.
- The HOD resolves department student issues or escalates them to the Principal.
- The Principal can escalate an issue to the College Admin.
- Platform support tickets are escalated by the Product Owner or Support Manager.

##### 7.12 Academic calendar

- The University sets the master academic calendar (semester dates, university holidays) for all its colleges and schools.
- Colleges and schools can add local holidays and events. They cannot change semester dates.
- A standalone college or school sets its own calendar.

##### 7.13 Tenant lifecycle

Created → Active → Suspended (no access, data kept) → Archived (data kept, access removed) → Deleted. A tenant can be exported at any stage. Deletion needs an export first, the end of the retention period, and Data Protection Officer approval.

##### 7.14 Audit and data rules

- Every create, edit, delete, approval, login and export is written to an audit log with the user, time, old value and new value.
- Audit logs are immutable. No role, including the Product Owner, can edit or delete them.
- Each role sees audit logs only for its own scope.
- Data protection rules (consent, retention, access requests) are configured per institution to match its own legal requirements.

#### 8. Functional modules

EDU 360 has 27 modules in three groups: 12 core modules (8.1–8.12), 7 extended modules from Part 2 (8.13–8.19), and 8 modules that the role workflows use but the sources never defined (8.20–8.27). Each module owns one institutional domain and shares data through the tenant's central database. Each can be switched on or off per plan and per tenant.

##### 8.1 Library Management

- **Purpose:** Manage all physical and digital library resources efficiently and transparently.
- **Users:** Librarian, Library Assistant, Students, Faculty, Parents (view), College Admin / School Admin (settings).
- **Features:** Book catalog management; ISBN management; digital library records; issue and return tracking; reservation management; fine calculation; inventory auditing; damaged and lost book tracking; student and faculty library card management; e-resource access and downloads.
- **Student / faculty self-service:** search books, reserve books, view issued books, fine status, download e-resources.
- **Inputs:** Book details; student and faculty IDs; issue and return dates.
- **Outputs:** Issue history; fine reports; inventory reports.
- **Rules:** One copy can be issued to only one user at a time. Fine calculation follows institution policy. Only the Librarian can update inventory. Issue limits are set by the Admin in library settings.

##### 8.2 Placement Management

- **Purpose:** Manage campus placement activities systematically.
- **Users:** Placement Officer, Students, Parents (view), College Admin (creates the Placement Officer), Principal (reports).
- **Features:** Company profile management; job posting management; student eligibility mapping; student application tracking; shortlisting; interview scheduling; offer letter uploads; offer acceptance tracking; placement reports; company feedback records; placement history.
- **Inputs:** Company details; job descriptions and eligibility criteria; student academic data.
- **Outputs:** Placement statistics (department-wise, company-wise, package analysis); offer records; company feedback reports.
- **Rules:** Only eligible students can apply. Students can track their application status. Placement applies to colleges only.

##### 8.3 Student Leave Management

- **Purpose:** Manage student leave requests and approvals.
- **Users:** Students, Parents, Faculty / Class Teacher, HOD, Principal; College Admin and School Admin (monitor).
- **Features:** Student leave application; parent leave request submission; multi-level approval workflow; attendance adjustment rules; leave history tracking; stage-by-stage notifications.
- **Inputs:** Leave dates; leave reason; supporting document (optional).
- **Outputs:** Leave approval status; leave history.
- **Rules:** The approval chain in Section 7.1 must be followed. Attendance adjusts automatically after final approval.

##### 8.4 Attendance Management

- **Purpose:** Record and monitor attendance accurately.
- **Users:** Faculty / Teachers, HOD, Principal, Admin, Students, Parents.
- **Features:** Daily attendance entry; subject-wise attendance; Present / Absent / Late statuses; correction requests; attendance summaries; attendance reports; attendance analytics; defaulter lists; attendance risk list; automatic absence alerts.
- **Inputs:** Student presence status.
- **Outputs:** Attendance percentage; defaulter lists; risk flags.
- **Rules:** Only assigned faculty can mark attendance. Students and parents have view-only access. Corrections need approval (HOD in college, School Admin in school).

##### 8.5 Examination Management

- **Purpose:** Manage examination processes.
- **Users:** Controller of Examinations, Admin, Examination Clerk, Faculty, HOD, Principal, Vice-Principal.
- **Features:** Exam schedule creation; exam pattern configuration (internal and external marks); hall ticket generation; marks entry; moderation workflows.
- **Inputs:** Exam details; student enrollment data.
- **Outputs:** Exam schedules; hall tickets; marks lists.
- **Rules:** Only authorized staff can modify exams. Hall ticket eligibility follows Section 7.4.

##### 8.6 Results Management

- **Purpose:** Calculate, approve and publish academic results.
- **Users:** Faculty, HOD, Principal, Controller of Examinations, Admin, Students, Parents.
- **Features:** Result calculation (grades, GPA / CGPA); result approval workflows; result publishing; result history; re-evaluation requests.
- **Inputs:** Approved marks data.
- **Outputs:** Grade sheets; performance reports; pass percentage summaries.
- **Rules:** Results can be published only after approval (Section 7.4).

##### 8.7 Fees Management

- **Purpose:** Manage student financial transactions.
- **Users:** Finance Director and University Accountant (fee policy), College / School Accountant, Principal (approval), Admin (view), Students, Parents.
- **Features:** Fee policy; fee structure configuration; scholarship management; installment management; payment tracking (online and offline); receipt generation; refunds and concessions; late-fee penalties; fee reminders; student ledger; fee reports; financial period lock.
- **Inputs:** Fee plans; payment records.
- **Outputs:** Receipts; outstanding balance reports; daily, monthly and scholarship reports.
- **Rules:** Fee edits allowed only before the academic session starts (Section 7.5).

##### 8.8 Payroll Management

- **Purpose:** Manage staff salary processing.
- **Users:** Payroll Officer, HR Manager, Principal / Finance Director (approval), Accountant (view), Staff (own payslips).
- **Features:** Salary structure configuration; payroll generation; payslip generation; salary history; deduction management.
- **Inputs:** Staff attendance; leave data.
- **Outputs:** Payslips; payroll reports.
- **Rules:** Payroll is released only after approval (Section 7.6).

##### 8.9 Communication

- **Purpose:** Enable official institutional communication.
- **Users:** Admin, Principal, HOD, Faculty / Teachers, Accountant, Placement Officer, Students, Parents.
- **Features:** Notices (university, institution, department, class); notice approval; notifications; email alerts; SMS alerts; in-app alerts; direct messaging; meeting notices; principal instructions.
- **Inputs:** Message content; audience.
- **Outputs:** Delivery status (sent, delivered, read).
- **Rules:** Notice approval follows Section 7.1. All messages are traceable.

##### 8.10 Assignment Management

- **Purpose:** Manage academic assignments and homework.
- **Users:** Faculty / Teachers, Students (college), Parents (view and track for school children).
- **Features:** Assignment creation (subject, instructions, due date); assignment submission (college students upload files); submission status (Completed, Pending, Not submitted); evaluation; feedback; missed-assignment alerts; homework compliance view for the Principal.
- **Inputs:** Assignment files.
- **Outputs:** Marks; feedback.

##### 8.11 Timetable Management

- **Purpose:** Manage academic schedules.
- **Users:** Admin, HOD, Department Coordinator, Faculty, Students, Parents.
- **Features:** Timetable creation; faculty allocation; room allocation; timetable publishing; online class links.
- **Inputs:** Course structure.
- **Outputs:** Timetable views (by class, faculty, room).

##### 8.12 Supporting modules

- **Academic Configuration:** grading systems; exam patterns; attendance rules; academic calendar; courses, subjects, classes and sections.
- **User Management:** user creation (single and bulk upload); role assignment; parent linking; activation and deactivation.
- **Reporting:** academic reports; financial reports; activity logs; report export (PDF and Excel).

##### 8.13 Admissions Management *(extended)*

- **Purpose:** Manage the complete digital admission lifecycle.
- **Users:** Admission Officer, College Admin, School Admin, University Admin, Principal (approval), Applicants, Parents (school applicants).
- **Features:** Application form creation; online application submission; document upload; application fee payment; merit list generation; seat allocation; admission approval; student account auto-creation (and parent linking); admission reports.
- **Inputs:** Applicant details; documents; marks; seat matrix.
- **Outputs:** Merit lists; allocation lists; new student records.
- **Rules / governance:** Role-based approval (Admission Officer prepares, Principal approves the final list); audit logs; data validation before account creation.

##### 8.14 Alumni Management *(extended)*

- **Purpose:** Keep lifelong engagement with graduates.
- **Users:** Alumni, Alumni Coordinator, College Admin, University Admin.
- **Features:** Alumni profile management; academic history linking; placement history; employment tracking; alumni communication; event invitations; contribution and donation tracking; alumni reporting.
- **Inputs:** Graduated student records; alumni updates.
- **Outputs:** Alumni directory; engagement and donation reports.
- **Rules:** A student record converts to an alumni record on graduation; alumni see only their own record and alumni communications.

##### 8.15 Hostel Management *(extended)*

- **Purpose:** Manage student residential operations digitally (records only, no hardware).
- **Users:** Hostel Warden, Hostel Staff, College Admin, Accountant (mess fees), Students, Parents (view).
- **Features:** Hostel block management; room allocation; student hostel assignment; vacancy tracking; mess fee management; hostel attendance; complaint tracking; hostel reports.
- **Outputs:** Occupancy and vacancy reports; hostel attendance; mess fee dues.
- **Rules:** The Warden manages hostel assignments only and cannot edit academic or general student records.

##### 8.16 Transport Management *(extended)*

- **Purpose:** Manage institutional transport operations (records only, no GPS hardware).
- **Users:** Transport Manager, Driver, Transport Staff, College Admin, School Admin, Students, Parents.
- **Features:** Route management; vehicle allocation; driver assignment; student route mapping and pickup points; transport fee tracking; transport reports.
- **Parent view:** bus route, driver contact, pickup point.
- **Rules:** The Transport Manager manages route assignments only.

##### 8.17 Research and Publications *(extended)*

- **Purpose:** Support academic research governance.
- **Users:** Faculty, HOD, Research Assistant, Research Coordinator, University Admin.
- **Features:** Research project records; faculty publications; journal submissions; conference participation; research grants; research reports.
- **Rules:** Faculty enter their own records; the HOD verifies; the Research Coordinator approves grant records.

##### 8.18 API and Integration Governance *(extended)*

- **Purpose:** Manage external system connections securely.
- **Users:** Product Owner, Platform Admin, University / College / School Admin, IT Administrator.
- **Features:** API key management; webhook configuration; third-party system mapping (payment gateway, SMS, email, SSO, meeting tools); access permission control; integration audit logs; integration usage reports.
- **Governance:** Product Owner approval for new integration types; tenant-level enable or disable; audit tracking; API usage limits from the subscription plan.

##### 8.19 RBAC Mapping Layer *(extended)*

- **Purpose:** Keep the permission matrix (Section 10 and the companion Excel) and the system's real permissions in step.
- **Users:** Product Owner, Platform Admin, Data Protection Officer, Audit Officer.
- **Features:** Role-to-permission mapping; module-level permission linking; audit reconciliation (matrix vs. live permissions); exportable RBAC reports; governance validation.

##### 8.20 Community Feed *(from workflows)*

- **Purpose:** Share institution life: events, achievements, cultural programs, sports, placement news, photos and videos, announcements.
- **Users:** Admin, Principal (post and approve), Teachers, HOD, Placement Officer (post for approval), Parents and college students (view, like, comment, share inside the platform).
- **Rules:** Approval per Section 7.1. Every approved post notifies parents.

##### 8.21 Student Notes: Discipline and Health *(from workflows)*

- **Purpose:** Record behavior, discipline and health notes for a student.
- **Users:** Class Teacher, Subject Teacher, Faculty (add); Principal (review, instruct); Parents (view).
- **Rules:** Notes can be added, not deleted; health notes are visible only to the class teacher, Principal and parent.

##### 8.22 Complaints and Issues *(from workflows)*

- **Purpose:** Log, assign and resolve complaints from students and parents, and student issues raised in departments.
- **Users:** Students, Parents (raise); Admin, Principal, HOD (assign, resolve, escalate); University Admin (review).
- **Rules:** Section 7.11.

##### 8.23 Events *(from workflows)*

- **Purpose:** Propose, approve and publish institutional events.
- **Users:** Admin, HOD, Faculty (propose); Principal (approve); everyone (view).

##### 8.24 Policies and Documents *(from workflows)*

- **Purpose:** Hold university policies, department documents and accreditation documents.
- **Users:** University Admin (policies), HOD (department documents), Accreditation Coordinator (accreditation documents), Compliance Officer.
- **Rules:** A published university policy applies to all colleges and schools under it.

##### 8.25 Staff Records and Staff Attendance *(from workflows)*

- **Purpose:** Maintain staff profiles, service records, workload, performance reviews and daily staff attendance (manual entry or upload).
- **Users:** HR Manager, HR Executive, Principal, HOD (workload), Admin.

##### 8.26 Risk Monitoring *(from workflows)*

- **Purpose:** Flag attendance and academic risk automatically (rules in Section 7.7).
- **Users:** Teachers, HOD, Principal, Admin (lists); Parents and students (own status).

##### 8.27 Platform Administration *(from workflows)*

- **Purpose:** Run EDU 360 as a SaaS product.
- **Users:** Product Owner, Platform Admin, Billing Manager, Support Manager, Release Manager, Data Protection Officer.
- **Features:** Tenant management; subscription plans and limits; feature control; subscription billing; support tickets and SLAs; platform analytics; security policy; backup and retention; release management; data protection approvals.

#### 10. Master role permission matrix

The matrix covers 67 roles across 28 feature areas. It replaces both the permission tables in the main document and the original Excel sheet: 43 roles and 20 feature areas come from the Excel, and 24 roles and 8 feature areas are added. **Bold** values were corrected from the source Excel (35 cells; the reason for each is in Section 19.3 and in the companion Excel's change log). Codes follow the legend in Section 6.1.

**Rules that apply on top of the matrix**

- Scope always limits access: a College Admin with F on Users manages users of their own college only; a Parent sees only their own child.
- Every staff user can always see their own profile, payslips and notices, and request their own leave, whatever their Leave column says.
- Students and parents can pay their own fees from a V on Finance, and like, comment on or share posts from a V on Community.
- Every role can view the audit log entries for its own scope (Section 7.14); the Governance column covers the governance module itself.
- For platform roles, Reports and Analytics mean platform-level reports only (usage, revenue, SLA). Platform roles never see tenant academic, financial or personal data.

#### 11. Role workflows – Platform level

Sections 11–14 give the screen-level workflow of every role: the menu path, what the system does, and who feels the change. Workflows marked *(new)* were written for this document from the role's permissions and the rules in Section 7. Every workflow starts at login and ends at logout. Only the Product Owner's login step is shown in full; the other roles log in the same way to their own dashboard.

##### 11.1 Product Owner

**Role:** SaaS platform owner. **Scope:** the EDU 360 product: plans, tenants, features, billing, support, security, releases.

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | Open the EDU 360 platform URL → enter email and password → two-factor code → Login | Product Owner dashboard opens | Only the Product Owner session |
| 2. Platform overview | Dashboard shows total universities, active tenants, revenue, active users, system health | Business and system status at a glance | Product planning decisions |
| 3. Open subscription plans | Menu → Subscription Management → Plans → Create New Plan | Plan form opens | – |
| 4. Create plan | Enter plan name, price, user limit, storage limit, API limit → Save | New subscription option created | All future tenants choosing a plan |
| 5. Configure modules for plan | Inside plan → Module Settings → toggle modules (for example Library ON, Placement OFF, Payroll ON) → Save | Tenants on this plan get only the enabled modules | Tenant functionality |
| 6. Configure features inside a module | Library → Feature Control → toggle features (for example Digital Books ON, Inventory Audit OFF) | Controls sub-features | Librarians and students |
| 7. Open tenant management | Menu → Tenants → Create Tenant | Tenant form opens | – |
| 8. Create tenant | Choose type (University, College or School) → enter name, email, plan, start date → Create | Tenant created with an isolated database; first admin account invited | That institution only |
| 9. Activate tenant | Tenant → Status → Activate | The institution can log in | Its admins |
| 10. Branding and domain | Tenant Settings → Branding → upload logo, set colors and domain | The institution sees a branded system | All its users |
| 11. Tenant feature control | Tenant → Features → disable a module (for example Placement) | The module disappears for that tenant | Placement Officers and students |
| 12. User limits | Tenant → Limits → set maximum users (for example 500) | Tenant cannot exceed the user count | Its admins |
| 13. Billing review | Tenant → Billing → review the invoice prepared by the Billing Manager → approve exceptions | Invoice becomes official | The tenant's finance team |
| 14. Apply discount | Apply Discount → enter % → confirm | Invoice reduces; discount logged | The tenant's payment |
| 15. Support tickets | Menu → Support → open a ticket → read the complaint | Understands the platform issue | System quality |
| 16. Escalate ticket | Escalate | Support team must resolve faster (SLA tightened) | Support staff |
| 17. Tenant usage analytics | Menu → Analytics → Tenant Usage → module usage, user activity | Product improvement planning | Future roadmap |
| 18. Revenue analytics | Menu → Revenue → monthly revenue, churn | Business strategy | – |
| 19. Security settings | Menu → Security → set password policy and session timeout | Platform security improves | All users |
| 20. Backup policy | Menu → Backup → daily backup, retention 5 years | Disaster recovery assured | All tenants |
| 21. Audit logs | Menu → Audit Logs → review login logs and changes | Compliance verification | Legal audits |
| 22. Upload release | Menu → Releases → Upload Version | New version prepared | – |
| 23. Roll out release | Select tenants → Deploy | Selected tenants get the update | Their users |
| 24. Roll back | Rollback | System returns to the stable version | All affected tenants |
| 25. Suspend tenant | Tenant → Status → Suspend | The institution loses access; data kept | All its users |
| 26. Archive tenant | Tenant → Archive | Data preserved, access removed | All its users |
| 27. Export tenant data | Export | The institution gets a copy of its data | Tenant |
| 28. Delete tenant | Request delete → Data Protection Officer approves (after export and retention) → confirm | Tenant permanently removed | Tenant |
| 29. Logout | Logout | Session ends | – |

**Restrictions:** The Product Owner never touches attendance, exams, results, students, fees or payroll. They control platform governance only.

##### 11.2 Platform Admin *(new)*

**Scope:** runs daily platform operations for the Product Owner, with Manage rights on every platform area.

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | Platform URL → credentials → two-factor code | Platform Admin dashboard | Own session |
| 2. Dashboard | Tenants pending activation, open tickets, failed jobs, system health | Operational overview | – |
| 3. Onboard tenant | Tenants → Create Tenant → fill details → Create | Tenant provisioned (Product Owner sees it) | New institution |
| 4. Tenant settings | Tenant → Limits / Features / Branding → update within the plan | Tenant configured | Tenant admins |
| 5. Plans | Subscription Management → Plans → edit an existing plan | Plan details updated (pricing changes need the Product Owner) | Future subscribers |
| 6. Support oversight | Support → queue → reassign tickets | Faster resolution | Support staff |
| 7. Releases | Releases → schedule a deploy prepared by the Release Manager | Update window set | Selected tenants |
| 8. Integrations | Integrations → review tenant API key and webhook requests → enable | Integration live | Tenant IT |
| 9. Monitoring | Analytics → usage, errors, storage per tenant | Capacity planning | Product Owner |
| 10. Audit logs | Audit Logs → platform actions | Accountability | Compliance |
| 11. Logout | Logout | Session ends | – |

**Restrictions:** Cannot change pricing, delete tenants, or see tenant academic or financial data.

##### 11.3 Billing Manager *(new)*

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | Platform URL → credentials | Billing dashboard: invoices due, paid, overdue, revenue | Own session |
| 2. Generate invoices | Billing → Run Billing Cycle → review draft invoices per tenant | Invoices created from plan and usage | Tenants |
| 3. Tax configuration | Billing → Tax Settings → set tax rates (for example GST) | Correct tax on invoices | All invoices |
| 4. Send invoices | Select invoices → Send | Tenant finance team notified | Tenant finance |
| 5. Record payments | Payments → match gateway payments or enter offline payments | Invoice marked paid | Tenant account |
| 6. Overdue follow-up | Overdue → send reminder → flag for suspension review | Product Owner can suspend | Tenant |
| 7. Refunds | Refund Requests → review → approve or reject | Refund processed | Tenant |
| 8. Discount requests | Forward discount requests to the Product Owner | Product Owner decides | Tenant |
| 9. Reports | Reports → revenue, collections, outstanding | Financial visibility | Product Owner |
| 10. Logout | Logout | Session ends | – |

**Restrictions:** No access to any tenant's student fees, tenant data or feature settings.

##### 11.4 Support Manager *(new)*

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | Platform URL → credentials | Support dashboard: open tickets, SLA breaches, escalations | Own session |
| 2. Triage | Support → New Tickets → set priority and category | Tickets ordered by urgency | Requesting tenants |
| 3. Assign | Ticket → Assign to support agent | Ownership clear | Support staff |
| 4. SLA monitoring | Support → SLA → view tickets near breach | Breaches prevented | Tenants |
| 5. Escalate | Ticket → Escalate to engineering or Release Manager | Faster fix | Engineering |
| 6. Resolve and close | Ticket → add resolution → Close | Tenant notified | Tenant admin |
| 7. Reports | Reports → ticket volume, resolution time, SLA compliance | Service quality tracked | Product Owner |
| 8. Logout | Logout | Session ends | – |

**Restrictions:** Cannot open tenant data or tenant messages; works through the ticket only.

##### 11.5 Release Manager *(new)*

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | Platform URL → credentials | Release dashboard: versions, deployments by tenant | Own session |
| 2. Upload version | Releases → Upload Version → add release notes | Version ready for rollout | – |
| 3. Beta rollout | Select beta tenants → Deploy | Early feedback | Beta tenants |
| 4. Full rollout | Select tenants or all → Deploy (canary or blue-green) | Tenants updated | Their users |
| 5. Monitor | Releases → health after deploy | Problems caught early | – |
| 6. Rollback | Rollback for affected tenants | Stable version restored | Affected tenants |
| 7. Hotfix | Releases → Hotfix → deploy to affected tenants | Urgent issue fixed | Affected tenants |
| 8. Release notes | Publish release notes to tenant admins | Tenants informed | Tenant admins |
| 9. Logout | Logout | Session ends | – |

##### 11.6 Data Protection Officer *(new)*

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | Platform URL → credentials → two-factor code | Data protection dashboard: pending approvals | Own session |
| 2. Review export requests | Data Protection → Export Requests → approve or reject | Data leaves the platform only with approval | Tenant |
| 3. Review deletion requests | Data Protection → Deletion Requests → check export done and retention met → approve or reject | Tenant data deleted only when allowed | Tenant |
| 4. Retention policy | Data Protection → Retention → approve changes | Retention rules enforced | All tenants |
| 5. Data access requests | Data Protection → Requests from individuals (access, correction, deletion) → route to tenant admin | Individual rights handled | Tenant users |
| 6. Audit review | Audit Logs → data exports, deletions, permission changes | Compliance evidence | Legal audits |
| 7. RBAC check | RBAC Mapping → compare live permissions with the matrix | Drift detected | Product Owner |
| 8. Logout | Logout | Session ends | – |

#### 12. Role workflows – University level

University roles supervise; they do not run daily operations. They set structure, calendar, policy and fee policy, approve what reaches university level, and monitor every college and school under them.

##### 12.1 University Admin

**Scope:** controls all colleges, schools, users, academics, HR, exams and reporting under the university.

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | University URL → email and password → Login | Session with university-level authority | All colleges and schools under this university |
| 2. Dashboard | Total colleges, schools, students, staff; attendance summary; exam summary | High-level university visibility | Decision planning |
| 3. Create college | Menu → Colleges → Create College → name, address, Principal email → Save | New college created; Principal invited | That college's management |
| 4. Create school | Menu → Schools → Create School → name, address, Principal email → Save | New school created | That school's management |
| 5. Create university users | Menu → Users → Create User → role (Registrar, Finance Director, Controller of Examinations, governance officers) → Save | University roles activated | University governance team |
| 6. Assign roles | User → Edit → Assign Role | Authority boundaries defined | User access rights |
| 7. Academic calendar | Menu → Academic Settings → Calendar → semester dates, holidays → Save | All institutions follow this calendar | Colleges, schools, departments |
| 8. Create departments | Menu → Departments → Create → select college → name | Department structure created | Faculty assignment |
| 9. Create courses | Menu → Courses → Create → assign to department | Academic structure defined | Colleges |
| 10. Monitor attendance | Menu → Reports → Attendance → college-wise summary | Attendance oversight | Principals, HODs |
| 11. Monitor examinations | Menu → Examinations → Overview → exam schedules | Exam governance | Controller of Examinations |
| 12. Monitor results | Menu → Results → Summary → pass percentage | Academic quality control | Principals |
| 13. Monitor finance | Menu → Finance → Reports → fee collection, outstanding | Financial governance | Accountants |
| 14. Approve university reports | Menu → Reports → Approvals → Approve | Reports become official | Governance, accreditation |
| 15. University policies | Menu → Governance → Policies → Upload → Publish | Colleges and schools must follow the policy | All institutions |
| 16. Audit logs | Menu → Audit Logs → who changed what | Compliance tracking | Compliance |
| 17. Create College Admin | Menu → Users → Create User → role College Admin → assign college | College operational authority assigned | That college |
| 18. Suspend college | College → Status → Suspend | College access blocked | All its users |
| 19. Export data | Menu → Data Export → select data → Export | University gets records | – |
| 20. University notice | Menu → Communication → Notice → write → Publish | All colleges and schools receive it | Everyone in scope |
| 21. Complaints | Menu → Complaints → review escalated submissions | Issues handled at the top | Complainants |
| 22. Logout | Logout | Session ends | – |

**Restrictions:** Never enters marks, marks attendance, processes payroll or takes student fee payments. Supervises, does not operate.

In a school, **students do not log in**. The parent is the primary digital user and represents the child. Students are protected from mobile exposure, teachers stay accountable, and communication goes through parents.

#### 15. Notifications and alerts catalog

Every alert goes to the in-app notification center. Email and SMS follow each user's preferences and the institution's settings. Because the product is web-only, there are no mobile push notifications; browser notifications are optional.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Student marked absent | “Your child was absent today in Subject X.” | Parent | In-app, SMS |
| Absent without approved leave | “Unapproved absence detected.” | Parent | In-app, SMS |
| Continuous absence (default 3 days) | “Your child has continuous absence. Please contact the school / college.” | Parent; class teacher | In-app, SMS, email |
| Attendance risk changes (Warning / Critical) | Risk level with teacher remarks | Parent, student (college), teacher, HOD | In-app, email |
| Low marks | “Your child has scored low in Subject X.” | Parent, student (college) | In-app |
| Assignment or homework missed | “Your child missed an assignment submission.” / “Your child has not completed homework.” | Parent, student (college) | In-app |

| Exam schedule or hall ticket ready | Exam update | Students, parents | In-app, email |
| Leave stage changed | Approved / rejected at each stage | Requester, parent | In-app, SMS |

| Fee due or overdue | Fee reminder | Students, parents | In-app, SMS, email |
| Payment received | Receipt available | Payer | In-app, email |
| Refund decided | Refund status | Student, parent | In-app, email |

| Library due, reserved copy ready, fine | Library update | Borrower, parent | In-app |
| Payslip released | Payslip available | Staff | In-app, email |
