#### 16. System architecture

EDU 360 is built with **React** (web front end), **Spring Boot** (services), **PostgreSQL** (relational database) and **RESTful APIs**, deployed on **AWS** with an equivalent **Azure** design. Each tenant gets its own isolated database by default; small tenants can use a shared database with row-level security.

&#91;embedded content: EDU 360 architecture · web, gateway, services, data, integrations\]

The browser talks only to the gateway; services check identity and permissions, then read and write the tenant's own database, and call external services through adapters.

##### 16.1 Non-negotiable rules the architecture enforces

- Multi-tenant and hierarchical: System → University → College / School → Department → Class / Section → User.
- Tenant data isolation: a new tenant is created with an isolated database.
- RBAC: every user can access only the data their role and scope permit; academic, financial and governance functions are isolated.
- Business rules in Section 7 are enforced in the service layer, not only in the screens: only assigned faculty mark attendance; results publish only after approval; only eligible students apply for jobs; fee structures lock at session start; every approval chain is a state machine.

##### 16.2 Services (modules as bounded contexts)

Each module is one or more Spring Boot services (or a slice of a modular monolith at first) with a matching area in the React app.

| # | Service | Responsibilities |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Platform and Tenant Management | Tenant onboarding and lifecycle, plans and limits, feature toggles, billing, platform analytics, releases |
| 2 | Identity and Access (IAM) | Login, OTP, two-factor login (MFA) for admin roles, optional SSO, session and password policy, RBAC and delegation |
| 3 | User Management | Users, roles, bulk upload, parent linking |
| 4 | Academic | Courses, subjects, timetable, assignments, study material, online class links, calendar |
| 5 | Attendance | Student attendance, rules, corrections, defaulter and risk lists |
| 6 | Examinations and Results | Patterns, schedules, hall tickets, marks, moderation, approval chain, publishing |
| 7 | Student Lifecycle | Admissions, student profiles, leave, records, alumni |
| 8 | Finance | Fee policy, fee structure, scholarships, installments, payments, receipts, refunds, penalties, period lock |
| 9 | HR and Payroll | Staff records, staff attendance, staff leave, salary structures, payroll, payslips |
| 10 | Placement | Companies, jobs, eligibility, applications, interviews, offers |
| 11 | Library | Catalog, loans, reservations, fines, inventory, e-resources |
| 12 | Campus Services | Hostel, transport |
| 13 | Communication | Notices, notifications, email, SMS, messaging, community feed, events, complaints |
| 14 | Reporting and Analytics | Cross-module reports, risk analytics, exports |
| 15 | Governance and Compliance | Approval workflows, audit logs, policies, accreditation, data protection, RBAC mapping |
| 16 | Research | Projects, publications, grants |
| 17 | Supporting services | File storage, search, scheduler, notification delivery, integration adapters (payment, SMS, email, SSO, meeting tools) |

##### 16.3 Key data flows

**Tenant onboarding (Product Owner)**

1. The Product Owner creates a tenant: POST /platform/tenants (name, type, plan, branding, domain).
2. The Platform service validates the plan and records the tenant in the central platform database.
3. The provisioning orchestrator creates the isolated database (or schema), runs migrations, and stores connection details in the tenant registry.
4. Initial configuration is applied: feature toggles, limits, the first admin user, and an invitation email.
5. An audit entry is written.

**Mark attendance (faculty or teacher)**

1. The teacher logs in and receives a token with role, tenant and assignment claims.
2. The UI posts to /tenants/{tid}/attendance/mark with class, section, subject, date and the status list.
3. The Attendance service checks tenant context, role and assignment; an unassigned teacher gets 403.
4. Rows are stored and an attendance.marked event is published.
5. The Notification service sends absence alerts; the Risk service recalculates risk flags.

**Publish results (approval chain)**

1. Faculty save marks as Draft, then Submit.
2. The HOD approves (college) → marks locked for faculty.
3. The Principal approves.
4. Publish is enabled: the Controller of Examinations publishes (college under a university), the College Admin (standalone college), or the School Principal or School Admin (school).
5. Grade sheets are generated, students and parents are notified, and audit entries are written.

**Student leave**

1. A student or parent posts /tenants/{tid}/leave (dates, reason).
2. The Leave service sets status Pending and the first approver from the institution's chain (Section 7.1).
3. Each approver acts; on final approval the Attendance service marks the days as approved leave.

**Placement application**

1. The Placement Officer posts a job with eligibility rules.
2. The student applies; the Placement service checks eligibility against academic data.
3. Shortlists, interviews and offers trigger notifications to the student and parent.

##### 16.4 REST API design

- **Authentication:** OAuth2 / OpenID Connect; JWT access tokens carrying tenant\_id, roles, permissions and scope. Refresh tokens; short session timeout set by policy.
- **Tenant context:** resolved from the subdomain (for example uni-x.edu360.example.com), or the X-Tenant-ID header for API clients. Every call carries Authorization: Bearer token.
- **Endpoint groups:** /platform/tenants, /platform/plans, /platform/releases; /auth/login, /auth/refresh, /auth/logout, /auth/sso/callback; /tenants/{tid}/users (and /users/bulk-upload, /roles); /courses, /subjects, /timetable; /attendance; /exams, /results, /results/approve; /fees, /payments, /invoices; /payroll; /leave; /library/books, /library/loans; /placements/jobs, /placements/applications; /admissions; /hostel; /transport; /community; /reports/\*.
- **Conventions:** versioned paths (/v1, /v2 for breaking changes); standard HTTP status codes; structured error bodies with an error code and audit id; pagination, filters and sorting on lists; bulk endpoints accept CSV and XLSX; rate limits per plan (API usage limits).

##### 16.5 Data model (main entities)

| Area | Entities |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | Platform, Plan (user, storage and API limits, enabled modules), Tenant (type, plan, domain, branding, status, connection info), Invoice, SupportTicket, Release |
| Identity | User (type, status), Role, Permission, UserRole (effective from / to), Delegation |
| Organization | University, College, School, Department, Class, Section (each linked to its parent) |
| People | StudentProfile (enrollment number, admission date, course, class, parents), ParentLink, FacultyProfile, StaffProfile |
| Academic | Course, Subject, CourseOffering, SubjectAllocation, Timetable, AcademicCalendar, Assignment, Submission, Feedback, StudyMaterial |
| Attendance | Attendance (student, subject, date, status, recorded by), AttendanceCorrection, RiskFlag |
| Exams | ExamPattern, Exam, HallTicket, Marks (status Draft / Submitted / HOD Approved / Principal Approved / Published), ResultPublication, ReEvaluation |
| Finance | FeePolicy, FeeStructure (version, status), Installment, Scholarship, Payment, Receipt, Refund, Penalty, FinancialPeriodLock |
| HR | StaffAttendance, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest (requester, for student, dates, reason, current approval level, status), SalaryStructure, Payroll (period, components, net pay, approved by), Payslip |
| Services | LibraryBook, Loan, Reservation, Fine; PlacementJob, PlacementApplication, InterviewSchedule, OfferLetter; Admission, MeritList; HostelRoom, HostelAllocation; Route, Vehicle, RouteAssignment; Alumni; ResearchProject, Publication, Grant |
| Communication | Notice, Notification (audience, delivery status), Message, CommunityPost, Comment, Event, Complaint, StudentNote |
| Governance | AuditLog (user, action, entity, old value, new value, time; immutable), Policy, AccreditationDocument, ApiKey, Webhook |

Attendance and marks are high-volume tables: partition them by academic year inside each tenant database.

##### 16.6 RBAC enforcement

- Role definitions and permissions come from the master matrix (Section 10). The RBAC Mapping Layer keeps the matrix and the live policy tables in step.
- Each service checks permissions through central policy middleware with a Redis cache.
- Permissions carry entity-level conditions, for example ATTENDANCE\_MARK also checks that the user is assigned to that subject and class; parent access is limited to linked children.

##### 16.7 Integrations

- Payment gateway: Razorpay by default (Stripe or PayU possible), with webhooks for payments and refunds.
- SMS gateway: alerts and OTP login.
- Email service (Amazon SES or SendGrid): notices, invoices, result alerts.
- SSO (SAML / OIDC): optional for universities.
- Meeting tools (Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams): online class links.
- External LMS or MOOC: integration through LTI or API only; hosting is out of scope.
- Cloud storage (S3 or Azure Blob): study materials, documents, offer letters, exports, backups.

##### 16.8 Deployment

| Layer | AWS (primary) | Azure (alternative) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web front end | CloudFront + S3 (React app per tenant subdomain) | Azure CDN + Static Web Apps |
| API gateway | Amazon API Gateway + Application Load Balancer | Azure API Management |
| Compute | EKS (Kubernetes) running Spring Boot services and workers | AKS |
| Database | RDS PostgreSQL: one per tenant, or a shared Multi-AZ cluster with schemas / row-level security | Azure Database for PostgreSQL (flexible server per tenant or shared) |
| Cache | ElastiCache (Redis) | Azure Cache for Redis |
| Events | Amazon MSK (Kafka) or RabbitMQ | Azure Service Bus / Event Grid |
| Files and backups | S3 with lifecycle rules | Azure Blob Storage |
| Search | OpenSearch | Azure AI Search or Elasticsearch |
| Identity | Custom OAuth2 server or Cognito | Custom OAuth2 server or Entra ID |
| Secrets | Secrets Manager | Key Vault |
| Monitoring | CloudWatch + Prometheus + Grafana | Azure Monitor + Application Insights |
| CI/CD | CodePipeline → ECR → EKS (canary / blue-green) | Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions → ACR → AKS |

##### 16.9 Multi-tenant database strategy

- **Default: database per tenant.** Strongest legal and logical isolation. Provisioned automatically when the tenant is created.
- **Shared mode for small tenants:** one database with tenant\_id on every row and PostgreSQL row-level security. A tenant can be migrated from shared to isolated as it grows. The mode is set per tenant in Platform Administration.

##### 16.10 Security, observability and compliance

- Audit logs for every sensitive action, immutable.
- Daily backups, retention configurable per plan (default 5 years).
- Encryption at rest and in transit (TLS).
- Secrets in a managed vault.
- Least-privilege access; platform administration separated from tenant administration.
- Vulnerability scanning and a hotfix and rollback process tied to Release Management.

##### 16.11 Reporting and scaling

- Reports read from read replicas or a reporting store, so they do not slow daily work. Cross-tenant platform analytics use a data warehouse (Redshift or Synapse) with no tenant personal data.
- Exports run as background jobs that write CSV or XLSX to storage and notify the user.
- Services autoscale on Kubernetes; RBAC policies are cached; heavy tables are partitioned.

##### 16.12 Implementation checklist

- [ ] Tenant provisioning automation (database per tenant + shared mode)
- [ ] OAuth2 / JWT with tenant, role and assignment claims; OTP and two-factor login
- [ ] Policy middleware loaded from the master matrix
- [ ] State machines for leave, results, fee structure, refunds, payroll, notices and community posts (Section 7)
- [ ] Rule checks: assigned-faculty attendance, publish-after-approval, fee lock, placement eligibility, hall ticket eligibility
- [ ] Tenant schema migrations and templates
- [ ] Audit writes for every sensitive operation
- [ ] Backup, retention, export and DPO-approved deletion
- [ ] Notification service with templates for every row in Section 15

#### 17. Non-functional requirements *(proposed)*

The source files set no measurable targets. The values below are proposed starting points to confirm with the engineering team and the first customers.

| Area | Requirement (proposed) |
| --- | --- |
| Availability | 99.9% monthly uptime for the web app and APIs, excluding announced maintenance windows |
| Performance | 95% of page loads under 2 seconds; 95% of API calls under 500 ms; attendance submission for a 60-student class under 1 second |
| Peak load | Result publishing and fee deadlines: designed for 10× normal traffic for 1 hour |
| Scalability | Up to 1,000 tenants and 1 million users on one platform deployment, scaling horizontally |
| Devices | Responsive web on current Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox; usable on 360 px-wide phone screens |
| Accessibility | WCAG 2.1 AA |
| Language | English first; text kept in resource files so other languages can be added |
| Security | TLS 1.2+; encryption at rest; two-factor login for admin and platform roles; account lockout after 5 failed attempts; password and session policy set by the Product Owner |
| Backup and recovery | Daily backups; point-in-time recovery 7 days; recovery point under 24 hours; recovery time under 4 hours |
| Retention | Default 5 years after a record closes, configurable per tenant |
| Audit | 100% of create, edit, delete, approval, login and export actions logged; logs immutable |
| Data protection | Configurable per institution: consent records, access and correction requests, retention, export, deletion with DPO approval |
| Notifications | In-app within 1 minute of the event; SMS and email handed to the provider within 5 minutes |
| Support | SLA tiers per plan (for example critical issues answered within 1 hour) |

#### 18. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Tenant | One paying customer with isolated data: a university (with its colleges and schools), a standalone college or a standalone school |
| Product Owner | The company that owns and runs EDU 360 as a SaaS product |
| Plan | A subscription package that sets price, user, storage and API limits, and enabled modules |
| RBAC | Role-based access control: what a user can do depends on their role and scope |
| Scope | The part of the hierarchy a user's role applies to (platform, university, college, school, department, class, own child) |
| F / M / A / V / R / N | Full Access / Manage / Approve / View Only / Request / No Access (Section 6.1) |
| HOD | Head of Department |
| Approval chain | The ordered list of approvers for a request (Section 7.1) |
| Delegation | A Principal's temporary hand-over of approvals to the Vice-Principal |
| Attendance risk | Normal / Warning / Critical status from the attendance percentage |

| SSO | Single sign-on with the institution's own identity system |

## F.2 Version 2.1

### EDU 360 – Education Management Platform: Final Master Product Document (Version 2.1)

Oct 22, 2026 · @Pratheesh S

#### Document control

Version 2.1 is the final master specification of EDU 360. It applies all 447 decisions in *EDU 360 – Final Decisions v1.1* plus the answers to its open items and the Version 2.1 change sheet (10 fixes, 4 wording clean-ups), on top of Version 1.0. EDU 360 v1 launches in India for universities, colleges and schools together. It is built in three phases. Approvals happen only through approval chains, and nobody ever approves their own request.

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Product | EDU 360 – Education Management Platform (multi-tenant SaaS) |
| Version | 2.1 (Final Master). Version 1.0 is kept as a separate document; Version 2.0 is in this document's version history |
| Built from | Version 1.0 master document; EDU 360 – Final Decisions v1.1 (447 decisions, two rounds); answers to the open items (Section 19.3); Version 2.1 change sheet (Section 19.1) |
| Companion file | EDU 360 Master Permission Matrix, Version 2.1 (Excel) |
| Change rule | From now on, every edit gets a change-log row and a new version number \[R2-42\] |

**Release phases \[OB-02\]**

| Phase | Modules |
| --- | --- |
| Phase 1 (v1) | Users and roles, institution setup, academic structure and timetable, attendance, exams and results, fees, leave, communication (notices, messages, notifications, community feed), reports |
| Phase 2 | Payroll, library, placement, admissions |
| Phase 3 | Hostel, transport, alumni, research and publications, API and integration governance |
| Later phases | Everything listed in Section 25 |

Rules written here for Phase 2 and 3 modules are final decisions, built when that phase starts.

**How to read this document**

- Sections 1–5: what EDU 360 is, for whom, and what it covers.
- Sections 6–7: roles, permission letters and the binding business rules. Where a workflow and a rule differ, Section 7 wins.
- Sections 8–10: modules, features by role and the master permission matrix.
- Sections 11–14: screen-level workflows for every role.
- Sections 15–18: notifications, architecture, final targets and glossary.
- Section 19: change log and every decision.
- Sections 20–25 (new): default formulas, pass/fail checks, privacy, testing, commercial decisions, and later phases with open items.

**Conventions**

- Decision IDs in brackets (for example \[AP-11\], \[R2-01\]) trace each rule back to the decision behind it.
- “Configurable” means each institution sets its own value; the default shown is what a new institution starts with.
- *(Phase 2)* and *(Phase 3)* mark rules built in that phase; “Later phase” means not in v1 (Section 25).
- Workflow steps list **Action**, **Impact** and **Affects**. “Admin” alone means the Admin of the current level.

#### 1. Introduction

**EDU 360** is a comprehensive education management platform that centralizes the academic, administrative, financial and human resource operations of universities, colleges and schools in one unified system.

Institutions manage students, faculty, staff, courses, attendance, examinations, results, fees, payroll, leave and communication through secure, role-based dashboards. EDU 360 supports structured hierarchies, so a university can oversee many colleges and schools while keeping full operational control and data integrity.

EDU 360 provides lifecycle management for students and employees: admissions, academic tracking, attendance, examinations, leave and service records, with payroll in Phase 2. It brings academic administration, HR, finance, communication and reporting into one system, removing dependence on disconnected tools. It is built for audit readiness and scalability, with security controls tested before launch (Section 23).

EDU 360 is the **single source of truth** for each institution: transparent operations, efficient management and better academic outcomes for every stakeholder.

**Product shape (final)**

- **Market:** India only in v1; prices in INR. The design must allow other countries to be added later \[PR-01\].
- **Customers (tenants):** a university with its colleges and schools, a standalone college, or a standalone school. All three launch together \[PR-02\].
- **Access:** one responsive web app, installable on phones, with push notifications \[OB-13\]. It needs internet; forms save drafts so nothing is lost when the connection drops \[PR-03\]. No native Android or iOS apps in v1.
- **School model:** school students do not log in, except that a school may switch on login for chosen classes (for example 9–12). Those students see only timetable, homework, study material, attendance and results; no messaging, fees or leave \[PR-04, R2-39\].
- **College model:** college students and their parents both log in. All college students follow the same rules, whatever their age \[PR-05\].
- **Outside systems:** v1 exports files in the formats of Tally, UDISE+, AISHE and affiliating-university portals. Direct connections come later \[PR-06\].
- **Management:** private institutions get a Management role above the Principal (Section 6) \[PR-07\].
- **Language:** English only in v1 \[CM-13\].

#### 2. Institutional and role hierarchy

EDU 360 runs on these levels: **System → Tenant (University / standalone College / standalone School) → Institution (College / School) → Department → Program → Year → Semester → Section → User** (schools: Class → Section). Authority, responsibility and data visibility follow this tree.

&#91;embedded content: EDU 360 hierarchy, Version 2.0 · platform, tenant, college and school\]

The platform team sits outside every tenant; inside a tenant, Management and the Data Protection Contact sit beside the university, and colleges and schools branch down to students and parents.

**Platform level (outside every tenant)**

- System
  - Product Owner
    - Platform Admin
    - Billing Manager
    - Support Manager
    - Release Manager
    - Data Protection Officer

**Tenant level**

- Management *(private institutions; views everything in the tenant; final approval on items the institution assigns)* \[PR-07\]
- Data Protection Contact *(one per tenant; handles personal-data requests)* \[RL-08\]

**University level**

- University
  - Vice-Chancellor
  - Registrar
  - Finance Director
  - Controller of Examinations
  - University Admin
  - University Accountant
  - University HR Manager *(new)* \[RL-09\]
  - Research Coordinator
  - Governance: Audit Officer, Compliance Officer, Accreditation Coordinator, Quality Assurance Officer, Legal Officer
  - Colleges and Schools (below)

**College level** \[HI-01, HI-02\]

- College
  - Principal
  - Vice-Principal
  - College Admin
  - College Accountant
  - College Governance: College Audit Officer, Accreditation Coordinator
  - Departments
    - Department
      - HOD (must be a faculty member of that department) \[WF-20\]
      - Faculty: Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor
      - Academic Support Staff: Lab Assistant, Research Assistant, Department Coordinator
      - Programs
        - Program
          - Year 1 … Year N
            - Semester (number per year configurable)
              - Section A … N
                - Students
                  - Parents
  - College Non-Teaching Staff: Office Staff, Admission Officer, Examination Clerk, Records Officer, Librarian, Library Assistant, IT Administrator, System Operator, HR Manager, HR Executive, Payroll Officer, Placement Officer, Alumni Coordinator, Hostel Warden, Transport Manager, Driver, Security Supervisor, Housekeeping Supervisor

**School level** (no departments in v1) \[HI-12\]

- School
  - School Principal
  - Vice-Principal (School)
  - School Admin
  - School Accountant
  - Classes
    - Class
      - Class Teacher
      - Subject Teachers
      - Sections
        - Students (no login, unless the school switches on login for chosen classes) \[PR-04\]
          - Parents (digital representative of the child)
  - School Non-Teaching Staff: Office Staff, Librarian, Lab Assistant, IT Support, Transport Staff, Hostel Staff, Security Staff

**External users:** Applicants log in with a mobile or email one-time code. Alumni do not log in; their records stay with the institution and are managed by the Alumni Coordinator \[HI-13, R2-40\].

##### 2.1 Structure rules

- **Subject groups:** a subject can be taught to a group that mixes students from several sections (electives) \[HI-05\].
- **Several assignments:** one staff member can hold several assignments (departments, institutions), each with its own scope \[HI-06\].
- **Year-end promotion:** the Admin runs bulk promotion; the Principal approves; failed or detained students are left out with a reason \[HI-03\]. Repeating a year is not supported in v1 \[HI-04\]. A detained student stays in the same year and section with status “Detained” until repeating is supported (open item 6).
- **Parents:** one parent login shows all their children inside the same tenant; a child in another tenant needs a separate login \[HI-07\].
- **Staff who are also parents:** two separate accounts. The staff account logs in with email and password; the parent account with a mobile one-time code. The same mobile number may be on both \[HI-08, R2-16\].
- **Colleges and schools under a university** stay as written \[HI-09\].
- **External university mode:** a college whose university is not on EDU 360 enters or imports external marks itself and publishes after Principal approval \[HI-10\].
- **Standalone tenants:** a standalone college or school has no University level. Management (or the Principal if there is no Management role) sets the fee policy; the Accountant builds the fee structure; the Principal approves it \[HI-11\]. The College Admin or School Admin takes the other university-level duties (calendar, policies).
- A standalone college can later join a university tenant; the platform team moves its data on request \[RL-02\].

#### 3. Objectives

The primary objective of EDU 360 is a unified, secure and scalable education management platform that centralizes academic, administrative, financial and HR operations in one integrated system.

**3.1 Centralization of institutional operations.** All institutional activities (academics, staff administration, finance, library, placement, communication) in one platform, removing disconnected systems and creating one source of truth.

**3.2 Structured institutional hierarchy.** System-level governance; tenant, university, college and school management; department administration; program, class and section operations; student and parent access. Authority and data visibility follow institutional boundaries.

**3.3 Role-based access control and data security.** Every user accesses only what their role and scope permit; academic, financial, administrative and governance functions are isolated; approval power comes only from approval chains; every action is auditable.

**3.4 Academic management automation.** Attendance tracking; examination scheduling; marks entry and result publishing; academic performance monitoring; timetable and syllabus access; assignment and study material management.

**3.5 Student lifecycle management.** Admission; academic tracking; attendance history; examination and result history; fee payments and receipts; leave tracking; assignments and learning material; graduation and alumni record.

**3.6 Faculty and staff management.** Staff profiles and service records; leave management and approvals; payroll and salary processing *(Phase 2)*. Workload and performance monitoring are removed from v1 \[OB-03, OB-04\].

**3.7 Financial management and transparency.** Fee policy and structures; scholarships and concessions; installments; payments and receipts; payroll *(Phase 2)*; financial reporting.

**3.8 Placement and career support** *(Phase 2)*. Companies, job posts, eligibility, applications, interviews, offers, reports.

**3.9 Library resource management** *(Phase 2)*. Catalog, issue and return, reservations, fines, digital records, inventory, damaged and lost books.

**3.10 Institutional communication.** Notices, notifications, SMS and email, push notifications, messaging, community feed.

**3.11 Governance, compliance and audit readiness.** Audit logs, compliance reporting, accreditation documents, approval workflows, data protection.

**3.12 Monitoring and reporting.** Academic, attendance, examination, financial and institutional reports; activity logs.

**3.13 Scalability and future readiness.** Multiple universities, colleges and schools; growing user base; feature expansion; other countries later.

**3.14 Single source of truth.** Data consistency, accuracy, controlled access and long-term integrity.

##### 3.15 Product KPIs \[OB-01, MK-19\]

| KPI | Formula (Section 20) | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weekly active teachers % | Teachers who logged in in the last 7 days ÷ active teacher accounts × 100 | Set after the pilot term |
| Parents who log in % | Parents who logged in in the last 30 days ÷ parent accounts × 100 | Set after the pilot term |
| Fees paid online % | Amount paid online ÷ total amount paid × 100 | Set after the pilot term |
| Trial-to-paid % | Trials that became paid ÷ trials that ended × 100 | Set after the pilot term |
| Renewal rate % | Tenants that renewed ÷ tenants due for renewal × 100 | Set after the pilot term |
| Customer satisfaction (NPS) | In-app survey each term \[MK-20\] | Set after the pilot term |

#### 4. Scope

Scope is now split by release phase. Phase 1 is v1; Phase 2 and 3 are fully specified and built later; Section 25 lists everything deliberately left out.

##### 4.1 In scope – Phase 1 (v1)

**Users, roles and setup**

- Tenants and institutions; users, standard roles and fully custom roles \[R2-02\]
- Institution setup, academic calendar, weekly-off pattern
- Data import templates and checked bulk upload \[MD-26, MD-27\]; global search \[MD-28\]; auto student IDs \[MD-29\]
- ID card data export (photo + details) for a printing vendor \[OB-12\]

**Academics**

- Departments, programs, years, semesters, sections, classes, subjects and subject groups
- Timetable (built by hand) \[MD-06\]; online classes with Zoom, Google Meet or Microsoft Teams meetings created automatically \[OB-07\]
- Assignments and homework; study material
- Attendance
- Exams and results, including backlog tracking and supplementary exam registration \[EX-08\]
- GPA / CGPA using a configurable grading scheme (grade points, credits) set by the university or standalone institution \[OB-06\]
- Year-end promotion

**Finance**

- Fee policy, fee structures, installments, scholarships, concessions, late fees and waivers
- Online payments (UPI, cards, net banking, wallets) and offline payments; receipts; reminders; daily collection report; period lock

**Leave, communication and reports**

- Student and staff leave
- Notices, messages, notifications (in-app, push, SMS, email), community feed, events, complaints, student notes, policies
- Fixed reports with filters and PDF / Excel export; a custom report builder comes later \[OB-15\]
- Exports in Tally, UDISE+, AISHE and affiliating-university formats \[PR-06\]

**Governance**

- Approval chains, delegation, audit logs, data protection requests, RBAC mapping

##### 4.2 In scope – Phase 2

- Payroll (payslips only; salaries are paid outside EDU 360) \[OB-09, OB-10\]
- Library
- Placement
- Admissions
- WhatsApp messages \[CM-07\]

##### 4.3 In scope – Phase 3

- Hostel
- Transport
- Alumni (records only, no alumni login)
- Research and publications
- API and integration governance

##### 4.4 Moved out of v1 (later phases)

- Staff attendance \[OB-08\]; workload and performance monitoring \[OB-03, OB-04\]
- Exam moderation \[OB-05\]; re-evaluation \[R2-07\]
- Certificate and transcript generation \[OB-11\]; e-resource downloads \[OB-14\]; accreditation templates such as NAAC criteria \[OB-17\]
- Fee refunds \[R2-21\]; tax on student fees \[R2-22\]; tax on platform invoices (open item 5)

##### 4.5 Out of scope

- Physical biometric devices; ID card printing systems (EDU 360 only exports the data)
- External MOOC content hosting; third-party content creation tools
- Physical infrastructure, campus surveillance, hostel hardware, vehicle tracking hardware
- Native mobile apps in v1
- Paying salaries (EDU 360 produces payslips only) \[OB-10\]

##### 4.6 Scope boundaries

- EDU 360 manages digital records and workflows only; physical processes stay with the institution.
- External systems connect through file exports in v1 and APIs later.
- Legal compliance depends on each institution's requirements; EDU 360 provides configurable controls (Section 22).

##### 4.7 Stakeholders

Product Owner and platform staff; tenant Management; university management and governance officers; college and school management; department heads; faculty and teachers; academic support and non-teaching staff; college students; school students where login is switched on; parents and guardians; applicants.

#### 5. System overview

EDU 360 is a multi-tenant system that manages the operational lifecycle of educational institutions and acts as each tenant's **single source of truth**.

**5.1 Platform structure.** Hierarchical and multi-tenant: System → Tenant → Institution → Department → Program → Year → Semester → Section → User (schools: Class → Section). Each level works within defined authority boundaries.

**5.2 Role architecture.** Every user is assigned one or more roles. A role decides functional access, data visibility, reporting scope and its place in approval chains. A user may hold several roles; each role keeps its own scope, and the user gets each (role + scope) pair, never a wider mix \[HI-14\]. The user works in one role at a time with a role switcher; the active role shows in the header and in every audit log entry \[HI-15\]. Institution Admins can also build fully custom roles (Section 6.3).

**5.3 Modular design.** Independent but integrated modules: Academic, Student Lifecycle, Staff, Finance, Placement, Library, Leave, Communication, Reporting, Governance, and the Phase 2–3 modules. Modules share data through the tenant's database and can be switched on or off per plan and per tenant.

**5.4 Data integration.** A common data model: no duplication, real-time synchronization, cross-module reporting, preserved history.

**5.5 Governance and control.** RBAC, approval chains, audit logs, compliance reporting and data protection.

**5.6 Operational coverage.** Tenant and university governance; college and school management; department academic delivery; class teaching; student and parent participation.

**5.7 Communication framework.** Notices, in-app and push notifications, SMS and email, direct messaging within the rules of Section 7.10, and the community feed.

**5.8 Reporting.** Fixed reports with filters and PDF / Excel export, limited to each role's scope, plus a buyer dashboard for Management, Principal, Registrar and Vice-Chancellor \[MK-11\].

**5.9 Scalability.** Many institutions on one platform, a growing user base, new features and new countries later.

**5.10 Operational philosophy.** Transparency, accountability, operational efficiency, academic quality and institutional compliance.

#### 6. Tenants, institutions, roles and permission letters

A tenant is the paying customer; colleges and schools inside it are institutions. Four roles are added, alumni login is removed, and institution Admins can build fully custom roles. Approval power never comes from a permission letter: it comes only from the approval chains in Section 7.

##### 6.1 Tenant and institution \[RL-01\]

- A **tenant** is the paying customer: a university (or group) with everything under it, a standalone college, or a standalone school. Each tenant has its own database by default; tenants on small plans share one database with row-level security \[TE-01\].
- Colleges and schools inside a tenant are **institutions**. They share the tenant's database but each sees only its own data.
- Only tenants are billed and suspended, and only by the platform. A University Admin can only **block** an institution's access, and only with Vice-Chancellor approval \[WF-15\].
- A standalone college can later join a university tenant; the platform team moves its data on request \[RL-02\].
- The platform team (Product Owner and platform roles) sits outside every tenant and never sees a tenant's academic, financial or personal data. The only exception: Support may view one ticket's data read-only for 24 hours when the tenant Admin grants it; every view is logged and the tenant can withdraw it \[WF-11\].

##### 6.2 Permission letters \[RL-03, RL-04\]

| Letter | Meaning | What it allows in practice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F – Full | Create, view, edit, delete within scope. No approving | Owns the records of the area: e.g. Librarian F on Library manages the whole catalog |
| M – Manage | Create, view, edit day-to-day records. No setup, no approving | Runs daily operations: e.g. Faculty M on Attendance marks attendance |
| C – Configure *(new)* | Set up rules and settings for the area | e.g. attendance rules, exam patterns, grading bands, library settings. In the matrix, Admin cells for Attendance, Exams, Academic and Library are “M + C” |
| A – Approve | View, and approve or reject what others submit | Only at the step the approval chain gives the role |
| V – View | Read within scope | Scope limits apply, e.g. a teacher sees only assigned students |
| R – Request | Submit requests for yourself or your child and track them | e.g. leave, certificate requests, record corrections |
| N – No access | Area hidden | Menu items do not appear |

- **Approval power comes only from the approval chains in Section 7.** F and M never include approving \[RL-03\]. A combined cell such as “M + A” means the role does both, at the chain step it holds.
- **The letter table is a summary.** Developers build from a detailed action list per role (for example MARKS\_ENTER, MARKS\_APPROVE\_HOD, RESULT\_PUBLISH, ATTENDANCE\_MARK, FEE\_STRUCTURE\_CREATE) \[RL-05\].
- **Restrictions win.** Where a letter and a role's Restrictions line disagree, the action list follows the Restrictions line. Example: an Admin with M on Exams can set up and monitor exams but cannot enter marks \[R2-18\].

##### 6.3 Custom roles \[R2-02\]

- Institution Admins can create fully custom roles and give any right to any role, including new roles.
- The standard roles and the permission matrix (Section 10) are the starting template every new institution receives.
- Every rights change is logged and the Principal / Management is notified (safeguard for the accepted risk in Section 25.2).
- Approval chains still apply: a custom role can sit in a chain only where the institution places it, and nobody approves their own request.
- This replaces the earlier rule that tenants cannot change role rights.

##### 6.4 New and removed roles

| Role | Level | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Management *(new)* | Tenant top (private institutions) | Views everything in its tenant; gives final approval on items the institution chooses, such as the Principal's own leave and, in standalone institutions, the fee policy and fee exceptions \[PR-07, R2-04, HI-11\] |
| University HR Manager *(new)* | University | Verifies university staff leave before the Registrar approves; keeps university staff records \[RL-09\] |
| Data Protection Contact *(new)* | Each tenant | Handles access, correction and deletion requests from students, parents and staff \[RL-08, R2-25\] |
| Student (School) *(new)* | School | Only where the school switches it on for chosen classes; sees timetable, homework, study material, attendance and results \[PR-04, R2-39\] |
| Alumni *(removed)* | External | Alumni do not log in; records stay with the institution \[R2-40\] |

Not added in v1: External Examiner (the Examination Clerk enters their marks) \[RL-11\], committee members \[RL-12\], counsellor or medical role \[RL-13\].

##### 6.5 Other role rules

- Security Supervisor, Housekeeping Supervisor, Security Staff and Driver logins are self-service only (profile, payslip, own leave, notices) and do not count against the plan's user limit \[RL-07\].
- University staff payroll is generated by the University Accountant *(Phase 2)* \[RL-10\].
- The IT Administrator and School IT Support may reset passwords, unlock and deactivate accounts, and assign **non-sensitive roles**: roles with no approval, finance, HR or exam rights (for example Office Staff, Library Assistant, Driver, Security). All other role assignment is done by the Admin \[MX-04, open item 9\].

##### 6.7 Role name standards

- “Library Admin” is the **Librarian**; “Examination Controller” / “Controller of Exams” is the **Controller of Examinations**.
- “Faculty” means Professor, Associate Professor or Assistant Professor.
- **Mentor / class coordinator** is an assignment given by the HOD to a faculty member for one class or section, not a separate role. It carries final approval for short student leave.
- “Accountant” alone means the College or School Accountant of that institution.

#### 7. Business rules and approval chains

These rules are binding; every workflow in Sections 11–14 follows them. Approvers approve or reject only, leave approval depends on how long the leave is, and nobody ever approves their own request.

##### 7.0 How every approval works

- **Approve or reject only.** There is no “send back” \[R2-01\]. A remark is required on reject and optional on approve \[AP-24\].
- **A rejection ends the request.** The requester may submit a new one; the old one stays in history \[AP-02\]. Rejected marks are entered again as a new submission.
- **Bulk approval.** Approvers can select many requests and approve them together with one optional comment; each item is logged separately \[AP-25\].
- **No automatic movement.** If an approver does not act, the system sends reminders only. A request never moves on by itself \[AP-03\].
- **No self-approval.** Nobody approves their own request or acts at two steps of the same request. The system skips them to the next approver and logs why \[AP-04\]. If the approver at a step is the requester, that step is skipped \[AP-05\].
- **Simultaneous action.** If two approvers act at the same moment, the first one wins; the second sees “already actioned by \<name>” \[TE-09\].
- **Deactivated approvers.** When a user is deactivated, their pending approvals move to whoever now holds that role, and the Admin is warned \[WF-26\].
- **Every decision is logged** with the approver, active role, time, remark and the request's before / after state.

**Delegation** \[AP-06 to AP-10\]

- Any approver can hand over approvals to a same-or-higher role for set dates.
- The delegate gets the approval right for those dates only, and it is logged \[AP-07\].
- A delegate cannot delegate again \[AP-08\].
- When the delegation ends, pending items go back to the original approver.
- The approver can cancel a delegation at any time; this is logged.

##### 7.1 Approval chains

College Admin monitors only \[AP-11, AP-13\] |
