##### 7.2 Leave rules

- **Leave types** are configurable per institution. Defaults – students: Sick, Personal, On-duty; staff: Casual, Sick, Earned, Maternity / Paternity, Duty, Loss of pay \[LV-01\].
- **Units:** full day, half day or per period \[LV-02\].
- **Late application:** leave can be applied up to 3 days after the absence (configurable) \[LV-03\].
- **Documents:** a medical note or other document can be uploaded on any leave; never required in v1 \[R2-10\].
- **Overlaps:** a request that overlaps an existing one is blocked, and the existing request is shown \[LV-05\].
- **Parents of college students** are notified of every request and every decision \[LV-06\].
- **Cancelling:** before the start date the requester can cancel; after it, cancelling needs the final approver \[LV-07\].
- **Counting days:** weekends and holidays inside a leave are not counted, using the calendar. Institutions can switch on a “sandwich” rule \[LV-08\].
- **Staff balances:** HR (in schools, the School Admin) credits a yearly number per leave type. No carry-forward or encashment. The system checks the balance and warns; loss of pay is flagged and HR (in schools, the School Admin) confirms it before payroll \[R2-09, LV-10\]. The leave year is the calendar year by default (configurable) \[WF-32\].
- **Substitutes:** when approving staff leave, the HOD or Principal assigns a substitute, who can mark attendance for those dates \[LV-11\].
- **On duty** (sports, placement drives) is treated as approved leave \[LV-12\].
- **Effect on attendance:** approved leave does not count against attendance %; making this configurable is a later phase \[LV-13\].
- **States:** Pending (current approver named) → Approved or Rejected; Cancelled.

##### 7.3 Attendance rules

- **Who marks:** only the faculty or teacher assigned to that subject, class and section, or a substitute assigned by the HOD or Admin for that date \[AT-03\].
- **How often:** college – once per subject period. School – twice a day by the teacher; per period is optional \[AT-01\].
- **Window:** attendance can be marked until midnight the same day; after that only through a correction request \[AT-02\].
- **Statuses:** Present, Absent, On approved leave, Not held. “Late” is removed everywhere, including reports; old “Late” marks import as Present \[R2-23, open item 13\]. A teacher or HOD marks a cancelled period “Not held”; it is left out of the percentage \[AT-12\].
- **Percentage:** configurable per institution, starting from the default formula in Section 20 \[AT-05, R2-37\].
- **Minimum attendance:** configurable per subject and overall \[AT-06\].
- **Alerts:** an in-app alert per subject, sent immediately and only when the student is absent, plus one SMS summary per day \[AT-07, R2-36\].
- **Term lock:** the Principal locks the term; then no attendance or marks can change. Unlocking needs a reason, lasts at most 3 days and relocks automatically; the HOD and Admin are notified \[R2-08, AT-09\].
- **Bulk upload:** allowed for the assigned teacher, or for the Admin with Principal approval \[AT-11\].
- **Not supported:** attendance shortage condonation \[AT-08\].
- Every change keeps the original value, the new value and both users in the audit log.

##### 7.4 Exam and result rules

- **Who owns what (university):** the Registrar owns programs and exam rules. The Controller of Examinations runs exam schedules, the marks process and result publishing \[R2-06\].
- **Exam schedules:** the Controller schedules university exams. The College Admin or Examination Clerk schedules internal exams within the calendar; either can do it \[WF-18\].
- **Exam patterns and grading:** the Admin configures patterns (internal / external split) within the Registrar's rules. Grading is absolute, with configurable grade bands \[EX-16\]; GPA / CGPA use the configurable grading scheme (Section 20).
- **Marks states:** Draft (teacher can edit) → Submitted (locked for the teacher) → HOD Approved / Class Teacher Reviewed → Principal Approved → Published. Rejected → the teacher sees the remark and enters a new submission; faculty cannot edit marks after submitting \[R2-01\].
- **Special codes:** AB (absent), MP (malpractice), WH (withheld), medical-absent \[EX-02\].
- **Checks:** marks above the maximum or below zero are blocked; a big jump from the previous exam shows a warning \[EX-17\].
- **External marks:** the Examination Clerk uploads them; the HOD checks them; they follow the same approval chain \[EX-01\].
- **Publishing:** results can be published only after the final approval. The Publish button stays disabled until then. Publishing notifies students and parents.
- **Withdrawing a published result:** the Controller (college) or Principal (school) can withdraw it with a reason; everyone is notified; it is logged \[EX-07\].
- **Re-evaluation is not in v1.** Students and parents can only view results \[R2-07\].
- **Backlogs:** backlog tracking and supplementary exam registration are in v1 \[EX-08\].
- **Hall tickets:** generated by the Examination Clerk or Admin; withheld for low attendance or any overdue fee amount, each check switchable \[R2-20\]. The Principal can override for one student with a reason; logged \[EX-09\].

##### 7.5 Fee rules

**Policy and structure**

- The fee policy (fee heads, allowed ranges, scholarship schemes, penalty policy) is set by the University Finance Director, or in a standalone institution by Management (else the Principal).
- The Accountant builds the fee structure, installments, scholarships and late-fee rules within the policy; the structure goes live after Principal approval.
- **Outside the policy range:** blocked. The Accountant can raise an exception request (Section 7.1) \[R2-03\].
- **Fee edits before the session starts:** the structure locks at session start. A new fee version mid-session applies to new admissions and future installments only; amounts already billed stay \[FE-02\].
- **Students joining mid-year:** full fee or pro-rata, configurable per fee head \[FE-03\].
- **One student account:** hostel, mess and transport fees are fee heads in the same student ledger, with one receipt series \[FE-22\]. Admission application fees are paid through the gateway into the ledger and carried to the student account on admission \[FE-23\].
- **Scholarship vs concession:** a scholarship is a scheme with rules for many students; a concession is a one-off discount for one student, approved by the Principal \[FE-17\].

**Payments**

- **Methods:** whatever the gateway supports – UPI, cards, net banking, wallets \[FE-30\]; offline cash or cheque entered by the Accountant.
- **Part payments:** not allowed; only full installments \[FE-04\]. Overpayment is kept as credit for the next due \[FE-05\].
- **Gateway charges:** the institution chooses who pays them (institution or payer) \[FE-06\].
- **When a payment counts as paid:** only when the gateway confirms by verified webhook or server check. States: Started → Pending → Paid or Failed \[FE-07\]. A browser “success” page alone never marks it paid.
- **Manual marking:** the Accountant can mark an online payment paid by hand only by entering the gateway reference number; this also covers payments stuck in Pending \[R2-33\].
- **Duplicates:** a second confirmation with the same gateway payment ID is ignored; one receipt only \[FE-09\].
- **Cash control:** a daily collection report goes to the Principal \[R2-33\].

**Receipts, late fees and reports**

- **Receipts are never edited.** A wrong receipt is cancelled with a reason and Principal approval; its number stays as “void”; a new receipt is issued \[FE-12\]. Numbering is per institution, per financial year, with no gaps and a configurable prefix \[FE-13\].
- **Late fees:** configurable \[FE-18\]. A waiver needs Principal approval and is logged \[FE-19\].
- **Locked months:** unlocked only with Principal approval and a reason; logged \[FE-20\].
- **Reports:** by financial year (April–March) and by academic year \[FE-21\].
- **No-dues check:** dues must be cleared before a transfer certificate or other certificates; the Principal can override with a reason \[FE-24\].
- **Teachers** see only “dues pending: yes / no”, never amounts \[FE-27\].
- **Reminders:** automatic 7 days before the due date, on the due date, and 3 and 10 days after (configurable); manual reminders also allowed \[FE-29\].
- **Not in v1:** refunds \[R2-21\], tax on fees \[R2-22\], sibling discount \[FE-25\], paying for several children at once \[FE-26\], a direct connection to accounting software \[FE-28\] (the Tally-format export file is in v1 \[PR-06\]), cheque-bounce handling \[FE-10\].

##### 7.6 Payroll rules *(Phase 2)*

- The Payroll Officer configures salary structures and deductions and generates payroll from approved leave (staff attendance is a later phase, so loss of pay comes from leave).
- Schools have no HR Manager or Payroll Officer: the School Accountant generates school payroll and the School Principal approves totals only *(v2.1)*.
- The Principal approves **totals only** (by department and staff type) and does not see individual salaries. The Finance Director also sees totals only \[R2-05, open item 7\].
- The Payroll Officer and HR Manager see individual salaries (in schools, the School Accountant who generates payroll); the Accountant sees totals only for reconciliation \[PY-04\].
- Both the Payroll Officer and the HR Manager can change salary structures \[PY-08\]. The Payroll Officer's own salary changes need the HR Manager \[PY-05\].
- Back-dated increments: arrears are calculated automatically \[PY-02\].
- EDU 360 produces payslips only; salaries are paid outside the system \[OB-10\].
- Not supported: hourly pay for guest faculty \[PY-03\], loans and advances \[PY-07\]. Later: corrections after approval \[PY-01\], Form 16 and tax declarations \[PY-06\].

##### 7.7 Risk flags

| Flag | Default rule |
| --- | --- |
| Attendance risk: Normal | Attendance at or above 75% |
| Attendance risk: Warning | 65% up to 75% |
| Attendance risk: Critical | Below 65% |
| Continuous absence | Absent 3 or more working days in a row |
| Low marks | Below the subject pass mark |
| Academic risk | Any of: low marks, attendance Warning or Critical, continuous absence, 2 or more missed assignments in a month |

- Each institution can change the thresholds \[RK-01\].
- Flags are recalculated right after every attendance or marks change \[RK-02\].
- A flag clears automatically when the student no longer meets the rule; teacher remarks are kept \[RK-03\].
- Parents are alerted only when the level changes (for example Normal → Warning) \[RK-04\].
- Flagged students appear on the risk lists of the teacher, HOD and Principal and on the parent dashboard with teacher notes.

##### 7.8 Placement rules *(Phase 2)*

- The Placement Officer sets eligibility per job (for example CGPA, active backlogs, department, year). The system filters eligible students automatically; only eligible students can apply.
- Eligibility is re-checked at shortlisting; the Placement Officer sees a warning and decides \[PL-01\].
- After placement, a student can apply only for jobs above a package threshold (configurable) \[PL-02\].
- Students keep a placement profile with resume upload \[PL-05\].
- Job packages are visible on posts; individual offers are visible to the student, parent and placement team only; reports show totals \[PL-07\].
- Interview results: Selected, Rejected, Waitlisted. The student accepts or declines offers in the system; the Placement Officer marks the student Placed.
- Not in v1: off-campus offers \[PL-03\], recruiter logins \[PL-04\], internships \[PL-06\].

##### 7.9 Library rules *(Phase 2)*

- One copy can be issued to one user at a time. Only the Librarian updates inventory. Issue limits per role are set in library settings.
- Barcode labels are printed by the system and used with a USB scanner; manual entry also allowed \[LB-03\].
- Fines are configurable per role \[LB-04\]. The Library Assistant collects fines; only the Librarian waives them, with no limit \[LB-05, LB-06\].
- Later: fines into the student ledger \[LB-01\], lost-book charges \[LB-02\].

##### 7.10 Communication rules

- Teachers message students (college) and parents; parents message the class teacher and the office; students message their teachers. **Students cannot message other students** \[CM-01\].
- **Quiet hours:** (9 pm–7 am) nobody can send messages to teachers or parents, and automatic alerts created in this window are held and delivered at 7 am. Sent at once: emergency notices, and security messages the user triggers (one-time login codes, password reset, new-phone alert) \[CM-02, CM-18\].
- Parents contact the Principal through the office only \[CM-03\].
- Class messages are one-way broadcasts from the teacher; replies come as private messages \[CM-05\].
- Attachments: PDF, JPG, PNG up to 10 MB, virus-scanned \[CM-06\].
- Comments pass an automatic bad-language filter; Admin and Principal can also hide them (logged) \[CM-10\]. No “report abuse” button \[CM-04\].
- Community posts: like and comment only; no share in v1 \[R2-30\].
- Users cannot switch off notifications \[CM-14\]. Each institution ticks which extra notifications it wants \[CM-16\].
- SMS carries only the subject or heading; details are inside the app \[CM-15\].
- Failed SMS or email: the sender sees it; the Admin sees a list of parents with wrong numbers \[CM-17\].
- Each institution registers its own SMS sender ID and templates under India's DLT rules \[CM-08\].
- Every message and notice is stored and traceable.
- Not in v1: WhatsApp (Phase 2) \[CM-07\], read acknowledgments \[CM-12\], photo consent \[CM-09\], other languages \[CM-13\].

##### 7.11 Complaints and issues

- Students and parents raise complaints; the Principal or Admin assigns each to an owner, who resolves or escalates it. The HOD resolves department student issues or escalates them to the Principal.
- No categories or time limits \[CP-01\]; no anonymous complaints \[CP-02\]; no reopening or rating \[CP-04\]; staff cannot raise complaints \[CP-05\]. Committees: later \[CP-03\].

##### 7.12 Academic calendar

- The university sets semester dates and university holidays for all its institutions; institutions add local holidays and events. A standalone institution sets its own calendar.
- Local holidays on exam days are blocked with a warning \[CL-01\].
- When the university changes the calendar mid-year, institutions are notified and affected timetables and exams are flagged \[CL-02\].
- The weekly-off pattern (for example alternate Saturdays) is configurable per institution \[CL-03\].

##### 7.13 Tenant lifecycle

- **States:** Created → Trial → Active → Suspended → Archived → Deleted \[CL-06\].
- **Trial:** 30 days, sample data allowed \[MK-05\]. When the trial ends, the tenant becomes read-only until it pays \[R2-24\].
- **Suspension** is done by the Product Owner by hand \[R2-24\].
- **Retention** is set when the tenant is created \[CL-08\]. After it ends, the system creates a deletion request for the Data Protection Officer to approve \[CL-07\].
- **Deletion certificate:** after deletion, a small record (who, when, what) is kept by the platform \[CL-10\].
- **Export:** CSV / Excel per module plus a ZIP of documents, with a data dictionary \[CL-09\]. Download links expire after 24 hours.
- **User limit:** warning at 90%; new users blocked at 100%; the Admin can request an upgrade \[WF-01\].
- **Cancellation:** no refunds in v1; after cancelling, a full data export stays available for 90 days \[MK-09, open item 4\].

##### 7.14 Audit and data rules

- Every create, edit, delete, approval, login, export and denied attempt is logged with the user, active role, time, old value and new value.
- Viewing sensitive records (ID numbers, salaries, health notes) is also logged \[AU-01\].
- Sensitive fields are masked in the log (ID numbers, bank details, health) \[AU-04\].
- Denied attempts are logged; repeated attempts alert the Admin \[AU-05\].
- Logs are kept in write-once storage, separate from the main database, with integrity checks. No role can edit or delete them \[AU-06\].
- Audit log retention is set when the tenant is created \[AU-02\].
- Anyone who can view audit logs can export them; the export is logged \[AU-03\]. Each role sees logs only for its own scope.
- Admin bulk corrections may touch any data, but changes to attendance, marks or fees go through the normal approval chain \[R2-32\].
- Only the last 4 digits of Aadhaar (or similar national ID) are stored \[R2-34\].

#### 8. Functional modules

EDU 360 has 29 modules: 20 in Phase 1, 4 in Phase 2 and 5 in Phase 3. Every module from Version 1.0 is kept; the numbering now follows the phases (the old-to-new mapping is in Section 19.4). Each Phase 1 and Phase 2 module below explains what it does, who uses it, its main screens, its rules, what goes in and out, its notifications and its edge cases.

| Phase | Modules |
| --- | --- |
| Phase 1 | 8.1 Users, roles and access · 8.2 Institution setup and academic structure · 8.3 Timetable and online classes · 8.4 Attendance · 8.5 Examinations · 8.6 Results · 8.7 Assignments, homework and study material · 8.8 Fees · 8.9 Leave · 8.10 Communication · 8.11 Community feed and events · 8.12 Complaints and issues · 8.13 Student notes · 8.14 Policies and documents · 8.15 Staff records · 8.16 Risk monitoring · 8.17 Reports and dashboards · 8.18 Data import, search and IDs · 8.19 Governance and data protection · 8.20 Platform administration |
| Phase 2 | 8.21 Payroll · 8.22 Library · 8.23 Placement · 8.24 Admissions |
| Phase 3 | 8.25 Hostel · 8.26 Transport · 8.27 Alumni · 8.28 Research and publications · 8.29 API and integration governance |

##### 8.1 Users, roles and access *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Gives every person exactly one account per identity, the right roles with the right scope, and a safe login.

**Users.** Admins (create users, roles), IT Administrator / School IT Support (resets, unlocks, non-sensitive roles), every user (login, profile, role switcher).

**What it does**

- **Accounts:** single creation and bulk upload; staff log in with email and password; students (college) with Student ID and password; parents with a mobile one-time code and an optional password; applicants with a mobile or email one-time code.
- **First login:** students receive a printed one-time password that must be changed at first login and expires in 7 days \[R2-35\]; parents activate the link from the admission form with a code sent to their mobile \[WF-22\].
- **Roles and scope:** standard roles from the template, plus fully custom roles built by the Admin \[R2-02\]. Each role is assigned with a scope (institution, department, class, subject, child). A user with several roles works in one at a time through the role switcher \[HI-15\].
- **Guardians:** up to 3 per child, each with their own login; one is “primary” for fees and leave \[WF-24\]. Parents are matched by mobile number to avoid duplicates \[WF-21\].
- **Security:** passwords of at least 8 characters, common passwords blocked, forced change every 120 days; two-step login for platform roles, Admins, Principal, Accountant, HR and Payroll \[NF-08, NF-09, R2-12\]; lockout for 15 minutes after 5 wrong passwords (Admin can unlock early) \[NF-07\].
- **Sessions:** idle timeout 15 minutes for Admin, finance and HR roles, 60 minutes for teachers, parents and students; “remember this device” for 60 days for parents and students; one phone and one computer at a time \[WF-35, R2-11\].
- **Role change:** the user is logged out at once and sees the new role's screens at next login; permission changes take effect within 1 minute \[WF-27, TE-10\].

**Key screens.** Users list; Create / bulk upload users; Roles and rights editor; Role switcher; Profile; Security settings.

**Rules.** Deactivating a user moves their pending approvals to the new role holder and warns the Admin \[WF-26\]. Changing or blocking a guardian needs Principal approval \[WF-23, WF-25\]. A new parent phone number is verified with a code and an alert goes to the old number \[WF-30\]. Every rights change is logged and notifies the Principal / Management.

**Inputs / outputs.** In: user details, role, scope. Out: accounts, login credentials, role assignments, audit entries.

**Edge cases.** A staff member who is also a parent has two accounts (Section 2.1). A parent with children in two tenants has two logins. Self-service roles (security, housekeeping, drivers) do not count against the user limit \[RL-07\].

##### 8.2 Institution setup and academic structure *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Builds the skeleton every other module uses: institutions, departments, programs, years, semesters, sections, classes, subjects, subject groups and the calendar.

**Users.** University Admin (institutions as Draft, calendar, departments and courses for any college), Vice-Chancellor (activates institutions), College / School Admin (own structure), Registrar (programs and exam rules), HOD (subject and faculty allocation), Principal (promotion approval).

**What it does**

- Creates institutions as Draft; the Vice-Chancellor activates them; the plan limits how many \[WF-16, WF-14\].
- Departments → Programs → Years → Semesters (configurable per year) → Sections for colleges; Classes → Sections for schools \[HI-01, HI-02\].
- Subjects and **subject groups** that mix students from several sections (electives) \[HI-05\].
- Subject allocation to faculty; mentor / class coordinator assignment; class teacher assignment.
- Academic calendar: semester dates and holidays from the university; local holidays and events from institutions; weekly-off pattern \[CL-03\].
- **Year-end promotion:** the Admin runs bulk promotion; the Principal approves; failed or detained students are left out with a reason; detained students stay with status “Detained” \[HI-03\].
- Grading scheme (grade points, credits, grade bands) set by the university or standalone institution \[OB-06\].

**Rules.** The HOD must be a faculty member of that department \[WF-20\]. Local holidays on exam days are blocked with a warning \[CL-01\]. A mid-year university calendar change notifies institutions and flags affected timetables and exams \[CL-02\].

**Outputs.** The structure tree, class lists, allocation lists, calendar.

##### 8.3 Timetable and online classes *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Plans who teaches what, where and when, and runs online classes.

**Users.** Admin, HOD, Department Coordinator (build); faculty, students, parents (view).

**What it does**

- Builds the timetable by hand in v1; automatic generation comes later \[MD-06\].
- Allocates faculty and rooms; publishes timetables by class, faculty and room.
- Creates Zoom, Google Meet or Microsoft Teams meetings automatically for online periods, through a platform-built integration in Phase 1 \[OB-07, open item 10\].

**Rules.** Teacher or room double-booking shows a warning, not a block \[MD-05\].

**Outputs.** Timetable views; meeting links on the period.

##### 8.4 Attendance *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Records and monitors attendance accurately and alerts parents at once.

**Users.** Faculty / teachers and substitutes (mark), HOD (corrections in college), School Principal or Vice-Principal (corrections in school), Admin (rules, monitoring, bulk upload with approval), Principal (term lock), students and parents (view).

**What it does**

- Marking per subject period (college) or twice a day (school, per period optional), with statuses Present, Absent, On approved leave, Not held \[AT-01, R2-23\].
- Correction requests after midnight; bulk upload; substitutes for dates \[AT-02, AT-03, AT-11\].
- Attendance percentage per subject and overall (Section 20), minimum rules per subject and overall \[AT-06\].
- Summaries, analytics, defaulter lists and risk lists.

**Key screens.** Mark attendance; Correction requests; Attendance summary (class, department, institution); Defaulter list; Attendance rules.

**Rules.** Section 7.3.

**Notifications.** In-app absence alert per subject immediately; one daily SMS summary; risk-level change alerts.

**Edge cases.** A cancelled period is “Not held” and left out of the percentage \[AT-12\]. Approved leave and on-duty are not counted as absent. Edits after a term lock are refused.

##### 8.5 Examinations *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Runs exam setup, schedules, hall tickets and marks entry.

**Users.** Registrar (exam rules), Controller of Examinations (university schedules, marks process), Admin and Examination Clerk (internal schedules, hall tickets, external marks upload), faculty and teachers (marks), HOD, Class Teacher, Principal (approvals).

**What it does**

- Exam patterns (internal / external split) and grade bands.
- Exam schedules: university exams by the Controller; internal exams by the College Admin or Examination Clerk \[WF-18\].
- Hall tickets with automatic eligibility checks (attendance, overdue fees) and Principal override \[EX-09\].
- Marks entry with special codes AB, MP, WH and medical-absent, range checks and jump warnings \[EX-02, EX-17\].
- Backlog tracking and supplementary exam registration \[EX-08\].

**Rules.** Section 7.4. Admins set up and monitor exams but cannot enter marks \[R2-18\]. Moderation is a later phase \[OB-05\].

**Outputs.** Schedules, hall tickets, marks lists, backlog lists.

##### 8.6 Results *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Calculates, approves and publishes results.

**Users.** HOD, Class Teacher, Principal (approve), Controller / College Admin / School Principal / School Admin (publish), students and parents (view).

**What it does**

- Calculates grades, GPA and CGPA from approved marks (Section 20).
- Runs the approval chain and enables Publish only after final approval.
- Publishes grade sheets and notifies students and parents; keeps result history; supports withdrawal with a reason \[EX-07\].

**Rules.** Re-evaluation is not in v1; results are view-only for students and parents \[R2-07\].

**Outputs.** Grade sheets; pass % and subject analysis; performance reports.

##### 8.7 Assignments, homework and study material *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Gives and tracks coursework.

**Users.** Faculty and teachers (create, evaluate), college students (submit), parents (track), Principal (compliance view).

**What it does**

- Assignment creation with subject, instructions and due date; study material upload.
- College students upload submissions. The teacher picks allowed file types per assignment from the safe types the system accepts \[MD-02, TE-11\].
- Late submissions are allowed until the teacher closes the assignment and are marked “Late” \[MD-01\].
- School homework: the teacher marks the status (Completed, Pending, Not submitted); parents see it \[MD-04\].
- Evaluation, marks and feedback; missed-assignment alerts.

**Rules.** No plagiarism check \[MD-03\].

##### 8.8 Fees *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Manages everything a student owes and pays, with full control over cash and approvals.

**Users.** Finance Director or Management (policy), Accountant (structures, collections, receipts), Principal (approvals, daily report), Admin (view), students and parents (pay), teachers (dues yes / no only).

**What it does**

- Fee policy, fee structures and versions, fee heads (including hostel, mess, transport in one ledger), installments, scholarships, concessions, late-fee rules.
- Online payments through the gateway (UPI, cards, net banking, wallets) and offline entry; receipts with gap-free numbering per institution and financial year.
- Student ledger with paid, pending, overdue and credit balance.
- Automatic and manual reminders; daily collection report to the Principal; monthly, scholarship and outstanding reports by financial and academic year; financial period lock.

**Key screens.** Fee policy; Fee structure; Exception requests; Student ledger; Payments; Manual payment entry; Receipts; Concessions; Scholarships; Reminders; Reports; Lock period.

**Rules.** Sections 7.1 and 7.5.

**Notifications.** Fee due and overdue reminders; payment received; payment failed (if the institution ticks it).

**Edge cases.** Gateway success without confirmation stays Pending; duplicate confirmations give one receipt; overpayment becomes credit; mid-year joiners pay full or pro-rata.

##### 8.9 Leave *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Handles student and staff leave with the right approver and the right effect on attendance and payroll.

**Users.** Students, parents, staff (apply); mentors, Class Teachers, HODs, HR, Principal, Registrar, Management (approve); Admin (monitor).

**What it does**

- Applications by full day, half day or period, with optional document, up to 3 days after the absence.
- Length-based routing to the final approver; staff balance checks and loss-of-pay warnings; substitute assignment.
- Automatic attendance adjustment on approval; leave history.

**Rules.** Sections 7.1 and 7.2.

**Notifications.** Every stage notifies the requester; college parents get every request and decision.

##### 8.10 Communication *(Phase 1; WhatsApp Phase 2)*

**Purpose.** Official, traceable communication.

**Users.** Admin, Principal, HOD, teachers, Accountant, Placement Officer, students, parents.

**What it does**

- Notices at university, institution, department and class level, with approval where Section 7.1 requires it; emergency notices on all channels.
- Direct messages and class broadcasts; meeting notices; Principal instructions.
- Notification center with in-app, push, SMS and email delivery and delivery status.

**Rules.** Section 7.10 (quiet hours, who can message whom, attachments, SMS content, DLT).

**Outputs.** Delivery status; failed-delivery lists for the Admin.

##### 8.11 Community feed and events *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Shares institution life (events, achievements, cultural programs, sports, placement news, photos, videos, announcements) and runs events.

**Users.** Admin and Principal (post, approve), teachers, HOD, Placement Officer (post for approval), parents, college students and staff (view, like, comment).

**What it does**

- Posts with photos and videos; approval queue for posts that need it; a notification for every approved post.
- Like and comment only; share is removed in v1 \[R2-30\]. Comments pass an automatic bad-language filter; Admin and Principal can hide comments (logged) \[CM-10\].
- Events: proposal → Principal approval → published; RSVP / registration only \[MD-23, AP-18\].

**Edge cases.** No “report abuse” button \[CM-04\]; photo consent is a later phase \[CM-09\].

##### 8.12 Complaints and issues *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Logs, assigns and resolves complaints from students and parents and student issues in departments.

**Users.** Students and parents (raise); Admin, Principal, HOD (assign, resolve, escalate); University Admin (escalated complaints).

**Rules.** Section 7.11: no categories, time limits, anonymity, reopening or rating; staff cannot raise complaints.

##### 8.13 Student notes: discipline and health *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Records behavior, discipline and health notes for a student.

**Users.** Class Teacher, Subject Teacher, faculty and Principal (add) \[WF-38\]; Principal (review, instruct); parents (view).

**Rules**

- A wrong note is fixed by adding a linked correction note; the original stays \[MD-19\].
- Health notes follow the same rule in college as in school \[R2-29\]. The School Admin switches health notes on or off for parents \[WF-34\].
- Parents see discipline notes immediately \[MD-21\].
- Notes are deleted 1 year after the student leaves, unless on legal hold \[MD-22\].
- Notes are not “student records”; viewing health notes is logged \[AU-01\].

##### 8.14 Policies and documents *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Holds university policies, department documents and accreditation evidence.

**Users.** University Admin (policies), Registrar (drafts), HOD (department documents), Accreditation Coordinator, Compliance Officer.

**Rules.** A published university policy applies to all institutions under it. Staff must read and accept new policies; acceptance is tracked \[MD-24\]. Accreditation templates (such as NAAC criteria) are a later phase \[OB-17\].

##### 8.15 Staff records *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Keeps staff profiles, service records and documents.

**Users.** HR Manager, HR Executive, University HR Manager, Principal, Admin.

**What it does.** Staff profiles; service records; staff documents (degrees, ID) uploaded and verified by HR \[MD-25\]; yearly leave credit per leave type. Staff attendance and workload / performance monitoring are later phases \[OB-08, OB-03, OB-04\].

##### 8.16 Risk monitoring *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Flags attendance and academic risk automatically so teachers and parents act early.

**Users.** Teachers, HOD, Principal, Admin (risk lists); parents and college students (own status).

**Rules.** Section 7.7: recalculated on every change, cleared automatically, parents alerted only on level change. Risk action plans are a later phase \[RK-05\].

##### 8.17 Reports and dashboards *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Gives every role the numbers it needs within its scope.

**What it does**

- Fixed reports with filters and PDF / Excel export: attendance, defaulters, risk, exams, pass %, results, fees (daily, monthly, outstanding, scholarship), leave, communication delivery, audit. A custom report builder comes later \[OB-15\].
- **Buyer dashboard** for Management, Principal, Registrar and Vice-Chancellor: fees collected, attendance and results at a glance \[MK-11\].
- Statutory exports in Tally, UDISE+, AISHE and affiliating-university formats \[PR-06\].
- Reports by financial year and academic year for finance \[FE-21\].

##### 8.18 Data import, search and IDs *(Phase 1)*

- **Import templates** for students, staff, parents, fee dues and past results; the platform team helps with the first import \[MD-26\].
- **Bulk upload:** the whole file is checked first and errors are shown row by row. The user then imports only a clean file, or imports the good rows and keeps the bad rows (with reasons) in a list to fix and add later \[MD-27\].
- **Global search** by name, ID or phone, for roles allowed to see students \[MD-28\].
- **Student ID** generated automatically; the pattern is configurable \[MD-29\].
- **Student status:** Applicant → Active → On hold → Withdrawn / Transferred / Dropped → Graduated → Alumni, plus Detained \[MD-30, open item 6\]. Admin “delete” only changes status to Withdrawn; there is no hard delete \[MX-09\].
- **ID numbers:** only the last 4 digits of Aadhaar (or similar national ID) are stored \[R2-34\].
- **ID card data export** (photo + details) for a printing vendor \[OB-12\].

##### 8.19 Governance and data protection *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Approval workflows, audit logs, compliance and personal-data requests.

**Users.** Governance officers, Data Protection Contact, Data Protection Officer, Admins.

**What it does**

- Audit logs (Section 7.14) with export.
- Personal-data requests (access, correction, deletion) from students, parents and staff, handled by the tenant's Data Protection Contact; no fixed time limit \[R2-25, PV-06\].
- Full-tenant export and deletion requests approved by the DPO.
- **RBAC mapping layer:** keeps the permission matrix and the live permissions in step, including each institution's custom roles and rights \[R2-02\].
- Compliance reports and accreditation document storage.

##### 8.20 Platform administration *(Phase 1)*

**Purpose.** Runs EDU 360 as a SaaS product.

**Users.** Product Owner, Platform Admin, Billing Manager, Support Manager, Release Manager, Data Protection Officer.

**What it does**

- Tenants and lifecycle (Trial → Active → Suspended → Archived → Deleted).
- Plans built by ticking modules and features; several pricing types (per student per year by default, flat, per module); usage types such as SMS and storage \[MK-03, MK-04, WF-07\].
- Billing with invoices; SMS charged per message; no tax and no refunds in v1 (open items 4 and 5).
- Support tickets raised by any user; tenant-granted read-only access per ticket for 24 hours \[WF-11\].
- Built-in usage counts on the Product Owner dashboard (logins, attendance marked, fees paid online); no outside analytics tool \[R2-13\].
- Security policy, backup and retention settings, platform audit logs.
- Releases: one version for all tenants; app-only rollback \[R2-26\].
- Allowed integration types list (platform roles never see a tenant's keys or webhooks) \[MX-02\].

##### 8.21 Payroll *(Phase 2)*

**Purpose.** Produces correct, approved payslips for every staff member. Salaries are paid outside EDU 360 \[OB-10\].

**Users.** Payroll Officer (structures, generation), HR Manager (verify, structures), Principal (approves totals), University Accountant and Finance Director (university staff), School Accountant and School Principal (school payroll, no HR step), Accountant (totals for reconciliation), staff (own payslips).

**What it does**

- Salary structures with components and deductions; changes by the Payroll Officer or HR Manager; the Payroll Officer's own salary changes need the HR Manager \[PY-05, PY-08\].
- Monthly payroll generation using approved leave and loss-of-pay confirmed by HR.
- Arrears for back-dated increments calculated automatically \[PY-02\].
- Approval by totals (department and staff type); payslip release; salary history; payroll reports.

**Key screens.** Salary structures; Run payroll; Verification; Approval (totals); Payslips; History; Reports.

**Rules.** Sections 7.1 and 7.6. Individual salaries are visible only to the Payroll Officer and HR Manager; viewing them is logged.

**Outputs.** Payslips, payroll register, totals by department and staff type.

**Edge cases.** No hourly pay for guest faculty, loans or advances \[PY-03, PY-07\]; corrections after approval and Form 16 are later \[PY-01, PY-06\].

##### 8.22 Library *(Phase 2)*

**Purpose.** Manages physical and digital library resources.

**Users.** Librarian, Library Assistant, students, faculty, parents (view), Admin (settings).

**What it does**

- Catalog and ISBN management; digital library records; barcode labels printed by the system for a USB scanner, or manual entry \[LB-03\].
- Library cards for students and faculty; issue and return with automatic due dates; reservations with a queue; fines configurable per role \[LB-04\].
- Inventory audit; damaged and lost book tracking; issue, fine and inventory reports.
- Student and faculty self-service: search, reserve, see issued books and fines.

**Rules.** Section 7.9: one copy to one user; only the Librarian updates inventory and waives fines; the Library Assistant collects fines.

**Edge cases.** E-resource downloads, fines into the student ledger and lost-book charges are later phases \[OB-14, LB-01, LB-02\].

##### 8.23 Placement *(Phase 2)*

**Purpose.** Runs campus recruitment from company to placed student.

**Users.** Placement Officer, students, parents (view), College Admin (creates the officer), Principal (reports).

**What it does**

- Company profiles; job posts with role, package, eligibility and deadline; automatic eligibility mapping; job alerts to eligible students and their parents.
- Student placement profile with resume upload \[PL-05\]; applications; shortlisting with a re-check of eligibility \[PL-01\]; interview scheduling (online / offline); results (Selected, Rejected, Waitlisted).
- Offer letter upload; offer acceptance by the student; marking Placed; package threshold for placed students \[PL-02\].
- Reports by department, company and package; company feedback; placement history; placement notices and community posts.

**Rules.** Section 7.8. Individual offers are visible only to the student, parent and placement team \[PL-07\].

**Edge cases.** Off-campus offers, recruiter logins and internships are later phases.

##### 8.24 Admissions *(Phase 2)*

**Purpose.** Runs the digital admission lifecycle up to a ready student account.

**Users.** Admission Officer, College / School / University Admin, Principal (approves merit lists), applicants (log in with a one-time code), Accountant (application fee view).

**What it does**

- Application forms per session; online applications with document upload; application fee paid through the gateway into the ledger \[FE-23\].
- Merit list generation; Principal approval of the final list; seat allocation.
- On confirmation, student and parent accounts are created automatically and the parent link comes from the form \[WF-22\].
- Admission reports.

**Rules.** Role-based approval; audit logs; data validation before account creation. Reserved-category seats, tie-breakers, waitlists, document re-upload and admission enquiries are later phases \[MD-07 to MD-11\]; delegating merit-list approval is later \[WF-37\].

##### 8.25 Hostel *(Phase 3)*

Blocks and rooms; room allocation and student hostel assignment; vacancies; mess fees as fee heads in the student ledger; hostel attendance; hostel complaints; reports. Users: Hostel Warden, Hostel Staff, College / School Admin, Accountant (view), students and parents (view). The Warden manages hostel assignments only. Out-pass / gate pass is later \[MD-14\].

##### 8.26 Transport *(Phase 3)*

Routes; vehicles; driver assignment; student route mapping and pickup points; transport fees as fee heads; reports. Users: Transport Manager, Driver, Transport Staff, Admin, students and parents (route, driver contact, pickup point). Drivers see only name, photo and pickup point, never phone numbers or addresses \[MD-15\].

##### 8.27 Alumni *(Phase 3)*

The Records Officer or Controller confirms graduation; the alumni record is created automatically and can also be added or removed by hand \[MD-12\]. Alumni profiles, academic and placement history, employment, communications and event invitations, reports. Alumni do not log in \[R2-40\]; the Alumni Coordinator manages the records. Donations are later \[MD-13\].

##### 8.28 Research and publications *(Phase 3)*

Research projects, faculty publications, journal submissions, conferences, grants and reports. Faculty enter records, the HOD verifies, the Research Coordinator approves grant records. Approval in standalone colleges is later \[MD-16\].

##### 8.29 API and integration governance *(Phase 3)*

API keys, webhooks, third-party system mapping, access control, integration audit logs and usage reports. Platform roles manage only the list of allowed integration types; they never see a tenant's keys or webhooks \[MX-02\]. Institutions creating their own API keys is later \[MD-17\]. The meeting-tool integration for online classes is built by the platform in Phase 1 and does not wait for this module.

#### 10. Master role permission matrix (Version 2.1)

The matrix covers 70 roles across 28 feature areas. **Bold** values changed in Version 2.0 (26 cells); Version 2.1 changes 4 more cells (Section 19.2). Reasons are in Section 19.2 and the Excel change logs. *(new)* marks the 4 roles added in Version 2.0; the Alumni row is removed. All 35 Version 1.0 corrections are accepted \[MX-31\]. The document and the companion Excel are kept in sync by hand \[DC-06\]. Letters follow Section 6.2; **approval power comes only from the chains in Section 7**.

**Rules on top of the matrix**

- Scope always limits access: for example a College Admin with F on Users manages only their own college; a parent sees only their own children.
- Restrictions lines win over letters \[R2-18\]: an Admin with M on Exams sets up and monitors exams but cannot enter marks.
- Every staff user can always see their own profile, payslips and notices and request their own leave.
- Students and parents can pay their own fees from V on Finance, and like and comment from V on Community.
- Platform roles have N on every tenant feature area, except the DPO's limited Governance view described below \[MX-01, R2-19\]. For platform roles, Reports and Analytics are platform-level only.
- Custom roles built by an institution start from these rows and are tracked by the RBAC mapping layer.

##### 10.1 Feature areas

Tenant (tenant lifecycle) · Billing (plans, platform invoices) · Feature Ctrl (module and feature switches) · Analytics (usage for own scope) · Support (platform tickets) · Releases · Data Protect (backup, retention, data-protection approvals) · Setup (institution structure) · Users (accounts and roles) · Academic (configuration, courses, subjects, timetable, assignments, study material) · Attendance · Exams (exams, marks, results) · Finance (student fees, institutional finance) · HR / Payroll · Leave (approvals) · Comm (notices, notifications, messages) · Placement · Library · Reports · Records (student records) · Admissions · Hostel · Transport · Community (feed and events) · Alumni · Research · Governance (audit, compliance, accreditation, policies) · Integrations.

| Principal (College), School Principal | Records | V | Plus approval of certificate / TC requests and record corrections \[MX-12\] |
| Parent (School) | Records | **V+R** | Views own child's record; requests certificates (bonafide, TC) and record corrections \[MX-18\] |
| Student (College) | Records | R | Views own record; requests certificates and corrections \[MX-19\] |
| College Admin, School Admin | Records | F | “Delete” only changes status to Withdrawn; no hard delete \[MX-09\] |
| Alumni Coordinator | Records | V | Graduated students only \[MX-22\] |
| Librarian, Hostel Warden, Transport Manager, Office Staff | Records | V | Limited fields: name, ID, class, photo, parent contact as needed \[MX-23\] |
| School Principal, School Admin | Exams | A / M+C | Both also hold RESULT\_PUBLISH, used only after Principal approval \[AP-16\] |
| College Admin *(v2.1)* | Exams | M+C | Also holds RESULT\_PUBLISH for standalone and external-university colleges, used only after Principal approval \[HI-10\] |
| Registrar *(v2.1)* | Exams | **M+C** | Owns exam rules: patterns and grading scheme; does not enter marks \[R2-06\] |
| School Accountant *(v2.1)* | HR / Payroll | **M** | Generates school payroll (Phase 2); School Principal approves totals |
| Student (College) | Exams | V | View only; re-evaluation not in v1 \[R2-07\] |
| Subject Teacher | Leave | V | Student leave for own classes \[MX-17\] |
| Management | Leave, Finance | A | Principal's own leave where assigned; in standalone institutions the fee policy and fee exceptions |
| Management *(v2.1)* | Integrations | **N** | Integrations means API keys and webhooks; Management does not need to see them |
| Data Protection Officer | Governance | V | Data-protection items only; not tenant audit logs \[MX-01, R2-19\] |
| Product Owner, Platform Admin, Release Manager, DPO | Integrations | F / M / V / V | Allowed integration types only \[MX-02\] |

#### 11. Role workflows – all roles and Platform

Sections 11–14 give the screen-level workflow of every role. *(new)* marks workflows written from permissions; *(changed)* marks steps changed in Version 2.0. Steps not marked stay as in Version 1.0.

##### 11.0 Rules for every role

- **Idle timeout:** Admin, finance and HR roles 15 minutes; teachers 60 minutes; parents and students 60 minutes, with “remember this device” for 60 days \[WF-35, R2-11\].
- **Devices:** each user can be logged in on one phone and one computer at a time; logging in on a new one logs out the old one \[R2-11\].
- **Passwords:** at least 8 characters, common passwords blocked, forced change every 120 days \[NF-08, R2-12\]. Lockout for 15 minutes after 5 wrong passwords; the Admin can unlock early \[NF-07\].
- **Two-step login** for platform roles, Admins, Principal, Accountant, HR and Payroll \[NF-09\].
- **Role change:** the user is logged out immediately and sees the new role's screens at next login \[WF-27\].
- **Role switcher:** a user with several roles works in one at a time; the active role shows in the header and in every audit entry \[HI-15\].
- **Approvals:** approve or reject only, with bulk approval, reminders, no self-approval and delegation (Section 7.0).

##### 11.1 Product Owner

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | Platform URL → email, password → two-step code | Product Owner dashboard | Own session |
| 2. Overview | Tenants by state (Trial / Active / Suspended), revenue, active users, system health; built-in usage counts: logins, attendance marked, fees paid online \[R2-13\] | Business and system status | Product planning |
| 3. Plans | Menu → Subscription Management → Plans → Create New Plan | Plan form | – |
| 4. Create plan *(changed)* | Name; pricing type (per student per year default, flat, per module); modules and features ticked with checkboxes; user, storage, SMS and API limits; usage types (SMS, storage) \[MK-03, MK-04, WF-07\] → Save | New subscription option | Future tenants |
| 5. Modules for plan | Plan → Module Settings → toggle (e.g. Library ON, Placement OFF) | Tenants on this plan get only these modules | Tenant functionality |
| 6. Features inside a module | Module → Feature Control → toggle features | Sub-features controlled | Module users |
| 7. Tenants | Menu → Tenants → Create Tenant (or from a sales demo request \[MK-15\]) | Tenant form | – |
| 8. Create tenant *(changed)* | Type (University / College / School), name, email, plan, start date, retention period, backup retention → Create | Tenant created in **Trial** (30 days, sample data allowed) with its own database, or in the shared database on small plans \[CL-06, MK-05, CL-08, TE-01\] | That tenant |
| 9. Activate | Tenant → Status → Activate after payment | Trial ends as Active; otherwise read-only after 30 days \[R2-24\] | Tenant users |
| 10. Branding *(changed)* | Tenant Settings → Branding: logo on all plans; colors and custom domain on higher plans \[R2-14\] | Branded system | All tenant users |
| 11. Tenant features | Tenant → Features → enable or disable modules | Modules appear or disappear | Tenant users |
| 12. User limits *(changed)* | Tenant → Limits → max users; warning at 90%, block at 100% \[WF-01\] | Limit enforced | Tenant Admins |
| 13. Billing review | Tenant → Billing → review invoices prepared by the Billing Manager | Invoice official | Tenant finance |
| 14. Discount *(changed)* | Apply Discount → % → confirm; only the Product Owner gives discounts \[MD-34\] | Invoice reduces; logged | Tenant |
| 15. Support tickets | Menu → Support → open ticket | Issue understood | Product quality |
| 16. Escalate | Escalate | Support must resolve faster | Support staff |
| 17. Usage analytics | Analytics → module usage, user activity (anonymous, combined; customers can opt out) \[PV-07\] | Roadmap input | – |
| 18. Revenue | Revenue → monthly revenue, churn, renewals due (reminders from 60 days) \[MK-23\] | Business strategy | – |
| 19. Security | Security → password and session policy | Platform security | All users |
| 20. Backup *(changed)* | Backup retention is set when the tenant is created \[WF-02\] | Recovery assured | Tenant |
| 21. Audit logs *(changed)* | Platform audit logs only \[WF-03\] | Compliance | – |
| 22–24. Releases *(changed)* | One version for all tenants; app-only rollback \[R2-26\] | All tenants updated together | All users |
| 25. Suspend | Tenant → Status → Suspend (by hand) \[R2-24\] | Access lost; data kept | Tenant users |
| 26. Archive | Tenant → Archive | Data kept, access removed | Tenant |
| 27. Export | Request full-tenant export → DPO approves | CSV / Excel per module + documents ZIP + data dictionary | Tenant |
| 28. Delete *(changed)* | Requested by the tenant's Admin or the Product Owner → Product Owner confirms → export → retention met → DPO approves \[AP-23\] | Tenant deleted; deletion certificate kept | Tenant |
| 29. Logout | Logout | – | – |

**Restrictions:** never touches attendance, exams, results, students, fees or payroll; cannot approve exports or deletions (Data Protect M) \[MX-03\].

| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Dashboard | Tenants in setup, failed tenant setups, open tickets, system health | Operational overview |

| 3. Tenant settings *(changed)* | Limits, features, branding within the plan; any change beyond the plan needs the Product Owner \[WF-06\] | Tenant configured |

| 5. Support and releases | Reassign tickets; schedule releases | Smooth operations |

| 2. Billing cycle *(changed)* | Generate invoices from plan, students and usage; SMS charged per message \[MK-10\]; billing cycle configurable \[MK-06\] | Invoices ready |

| 6. Reports | Revenue, collections, outstanding | Financial visibility |

No tax configuration and no platform refunds in v1 (open items 4 and 5). After cancelling, a full data export stays available for 90 days \[MK-09\].

| Step | Action | Impact |

| 3. Escalate | To engineering or the Release Manager | Faster fix |
| 4. Resolve | Resolution → Close; requester notified | Ticket closed |

SLA monitoring is removed in v1 \[R2-27\].

| Step | Action | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |

| 4. Rollback *(changed)* | App-only rollback | Stable version restored |

| Step | Action | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |

| 4. Retention | Approves retention changes | Rules enforced |

#### 12. Role workflows – Tenant and University level

These roles supervise rather than operate. They set structure, calendar, policy and fee policy, approve what reaches their level, and monitor every institution under them.

##### 12.1 Management *(new)*

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | Tenant URL → credentials → two-step code | Management dashboard | Own session |
| 2. Buyer dashboard | Fees collected, attendance and results at a glance, per institution \[MK-11\] | Ownership view | – |
| 3. View anything | Every tenant area, view only | Full oversight | – |
| 4. Principal's leave | Leave → Pending → Approve / Reject (where assigned) \[R2-04\] | Principal's leave decided | Principal |
| 5. Standalone fee policy | Finance → Fee Policy → set fee heads, ranges, schemes \[HI-11\] | Accountant builds structures within it | Accountant, Principal |
| 6. Fee exceptions (standalone) | Finance → Exception Requests → Approve / Reject (before the Principal) | Out-of-range fee allowed or blocked | Accountant |
| 7. Custom-role alerts | Notifications when an Admin changes role rights | Safeguard against misuse | Admin |
| 8. Self-approval visibility | Sees any Principal self-approval logged when nobody is above the Principal | Accountability | Principal |

##### 12.2 Data Protection Contact *(new)*

| Step | Action | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Requests inbox | Access, correction and deletion requests from students, parents and staff \[R2-25\] | All personal-data requests in one place |
| 2. Verify and act | View the record (limited fields), arrange the correction or export with the Admin, record the outcome | Request closed |
| 3. Log | Every request and action logged under Governance | Evidence for audits |

No fixed time limit in v1 \[PV-06\]; a lawyer check is pending (Section 25.2).

**Restrictions:** never enters marks, marks attendance, processes payroll or takes fee payments; HR / Payroll is view only \[MX-07\]; cannot enter marks despite M+C on Exams \[R2-18\].

##### 12.11 Governance officers

Audit, Compliance, Accreditation, Quality Assurance and Legal Officers view reports and records and own their governance area: the Audit Officer reviews audit logs and records findings; the Compliance Officer prepares compliance reports; the Accreditation Coordinator maps evidence to criteria; QA and Legal approve items in their area. “Approve items” stays generic \[WF-19\]. College Audit Officer and the college Accreditation Coordinator do the same for one college.

#### 15. Notifications and alerts

Every alert goes to the in-app notification center and as a push notification on the installable app \[OB-13\]. SMS carries only the subject or heading; details are in the app \[CM-15\]. Users cannot switch notifications off \[CM-14\]. Between 9 pm and 7 am nobody can send messages to teachers or parents, and automatic alerts are held until 7 am. Emergency notices go out on all channels at once, and security messages the user triggers (login codes, password reset, new-phone alert) are sent immediately \[CM-02, CM-18\]. WhatsApp is Phase 2 \[CM-07\].

##### 15.1 Standard notifications

| Trigger | Message (example) | Sent to | Channel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Student absent | “Your child was absent today in Subject X.” – per subject, immediately, only when absent | Parent; college student | In-app, push |
| Daily absence summary | One summary of the day's absences | Parent | SMS (once a day) \[AT-07, R2-36\] |
| Absent without approved leave | “Unapproved absence detected.” | Parent | In-app, push |
| Continuous absence | “Your child has continuous absence. Please contact the school / college.” | Parent; class teacher / mentor | In-app, push, SMS |
| Risk level changed | Only when the level changes (e.g. Normal → Warning) \[RK-04\] | Parent, college student, teacher, HOD | In-app, push, email |
| Low marks | “Your child has scored low in Subject X.” | Parent, college student | In-app, push |
| Assignment or homework missed | “Your child missed an assignment submission.” / “Your child has not completed homework.” | Parent, college student | In-app, push |
| New assignment or homework | Title and due date | Students, parents | In-app, push |
| Result published / withdrawn | Result available / withdrawn with reason | Students, parents | In-app, push, SMS, email |
| Exam schedule, hall ticket ready | Exam update | Students, parents | In-app, push, email |
| Leave stage changed | Approved or rejected at each stage | Requester; college parent always \[LV-06\] | In-app, push, SMS |
| Approval waiting / reminder | Pending item (reminders only; nothing moves on its own) | Approver | In-app, push, email |
| Fee reminder | 7 days before, on the due date, 3 and 10 days after | Students, parents | In-app, push, SMS, email |
| Payment received | Receipt available | Payer | In-app, push, email |
| Daily collection report | Day's payments | Principal | In-app, email |
| Notice published | Notice title | Notice audience | In-app, push, email |
| Emergency notice | Heading | Everyone in scope | All channels, any time |
| Community post approved | New post | Parents, students, staff | In-app, push |
| Term unlocked / relocked | Unlock reason and expiry | HOD, Admin | In-app |
| Job posted, shortlisted, interview, offer *(Phase 2)* | Job alert / “You are shortlisted.” / “Your child is shortlisted.” / offer received | Eligible students and parents | In-app, push, SMS, email |

##### 15.2 Optional notifications (each institution ticks what it wants) \[CM-16\]

Account created; password reset; new-device login; role changed; delegation started or ended; term locked; hall ticket withheld; payment failed; trial ending.

##### 15.3 Delivery failures \[CM-17\]

A failed SMS or email shows to the sender; the Admin sees a list of parents with wrong numbers. Each institution registers its own SMS sender ID and templates under India's DLT rules \[CM-08\]. Attendance is always saved first; alerts are retried automatically and failures are visible to the Admin \[TE-21\].

#### 16. System architecture

EDU 360 v1 runs on AWS in India only, with React, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL and REST, separate services from day one, Keycloak for login, RabbitMQ or Amazon SQS for messages, and OpenSearch for search. Each tenant gets its own database by default.

&#91;embedded content: EDU 360 architecture, Version 2.0 · web app, gateway, Keycloak, services, data\]

The installable web app talks only to the gateway; Keycloak and the access service check identity and rights, then each service works on the tenant's own database in India.

##### 16.1 Final technical decisions

| Topic | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Front end | React, one responsive web app, installable on phones with push notifications; drafts saved when the connection drops \[OB-13, PR-03\] |
| Services | Separate Spring Boot services from day one \[TE-02\] |
| Database | PostgreSQL; own database per tenant by default; shared database with row-level security for small plans \[TE-01\] |
| Message queue | RabbitMQ or Amazon SQS \[TE-03\] |
| Login system | Keycloak: passwords, one-time codes, two-step login, SSO \[R2-17\] |
| Cloud | AWS only in v1; design kept portable to Azure \[TE-05\] |
| Data location | India regions only (AWS Mumbai / Hyderabad) \[TE-06\] |
| Tenant detection | From the login token; must match the subdomain; the X-Tenant-ID header only for API keys and never trusted alone \[TE-07\] |
| Repeated clicks | Every payment and approval call carries a unique request key; repeats are ignored \[TE-08\] |
| Concurrent approvals | First action wins; the second sees “already actioned by \<name>” \[TE-09\] |
| Permission changes | Take effect within 1 minute; a changed user is logged out at once \[TE-10, WF-27\] |
| Files | Virus scan; allowed types only; download links expire after 15 minutes; every download checked against permissions \[TE-11\] |
| Exports | Download links expire after 24 hours; downloads logged \[TE-12\] |
| Search | OpenSearch from day one \[TE-13\] |
| Domains | Subdomain for all; custom domain on higher plans \[TE-14, R2-14\] |
| Time zone | Per tenant, default India time \[TE-15\] |
| API versions | Old version supported for 12 months after a new one \[TE-16\] |
| Sensitive fields | Field-level encryption \[TE-17\]; Aadhaar last 4 digits only \[R2-34\] |
| Tenant setup failure | Retried safely; half-made tenants cleaned up; Platform Admin alerted \[TE-19\] |
| Attendance and alerts | Attendance saved first; alerts retried automatically; failures visible to the Admin \[TE-21\] |
| Audit logs | Write-once storage separate from the main database, with integrity checks \[AU-06\] |
| Environments | Development, Staging (like production, fake data) and Production \[R2-15\] |
| Security test | One outside security test before launch \[R2-28\] |
| Next document | A field-by-field data dictionary \[TE-20\] |

##### 16.2 Services

| Service | Responsibilities |
| --- | --- |
| Platform and Tenant | Tenants, Trial / Active lifecycle, plans and limits, feature switches, billing, usage counts, releases |
| Identity (Keycloak) | Login, one-time codes, two-step login, SSO, sessions, devices |
| Access and RBAC | Roles, custom roles, action lists, scopes, delegation, RBAC mapping |
| Users and Records | Users, guardians, students, staff records, IDs, statuses, imports, search |

| Attendance | Marking, corrections, Not held, substitutes, term lock, risk recalculation trigger |
| Exams and Results | Patterns, schedules, hall tickets, marks, approval chains, GPA / CGPA, publishing, withdrawal, backlogs |
| Finance | Fee policy, structures and versions, exceptions, installments, scholarships, concessions, gateway payments, receipts, ledger, reminders, period lock |
| Leave | Student and staff leave, length-based routing, balances, substitutes |
| Communication | Notices, messages, notifications, push, SMS (DLT), email, community, events, complaints, student notes, policies |
| Reporting | Fixed reports, buyer dashboard, statutory exports, PDF / Excel |
| Governance | Approval engine, audit logs, data-protection requests, exports, deletion |
| Phase 2 services | Payroll, Library, Placement, Admissions, WhatsApp |
| Phase 3 services | Hostel, Transport, Alumni, Research, API governance |
| Supporting | File storage with virus scan, OpenSearch, scheduler, payment and meeting-tool adapters |

##### 16.3 Key data flows

**Tenant onboarding.** Sales creates the tenant from a demo request → Platform service records it (Trial) → provisioning creates the tenant database and runs migrations (retried safely on failure) → Keycloak realm and first Admin created → invitation sent → audit entry.

**Mark attendance.** Teacher's token carries tenant, role and assignments → Attendance service checks assignment or substitute and the midnight window → saves rows first → publishes an event → Notification service sends per-subject in-app alerts and queues the daily SMS summary → Risk recalculates flags.

**Publish results.** Draft → Submitted → HOD (or Class Teacher review) → Principal → Publish enabled for the Controller / College Admin / School Principal or School Admin → grade sheets generated → students and parents notified → audit entries. A rejection closes the submission; the teacher creates a new one.

**Student leave.** Request → Leave service computes working days (calendar, sandwich rule) and length → routes to the final approver for that length → approval adjusts attendance → every step notifies the requester (and college parent).

**Fee payment.** Payment started with a unique request key → gateway → verified webhook or server check marks it Paid → one receipt per gateway payment ID → ledger updated → daily collection report.

##### 16.4 REST API

OAuth2 / OpenID Connect through Keycloak; JWT tokens carry tenant, roles, active role, scopes and permissions. Versioned paths (/v1, /v2); old versions supported for 12 months. Standard status codes with structured errors and an audit id; pagination, filters and sorting; bulk endpoints for CSV / XLSX with row-level validation; unique request keys on payment and approval calls; rate limits per plan. Endpoint groups: /platform, /auth, /tenants/{tid}/users, /structure, /timetable, /attendance, /exams, /results, /fees, /payments, /leave, /notices, /messages, /community, /reports, /governance, and the Phase 2–3 groups.

##### 16.5 Data model (main entities)

| Area | Entities |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | Plan (pricing type, modules, limits, usage types), Tenant (type, state, retention, domain, branding), Invoice, SupportTicket, Release, DeletionCertificate |
| Identity | User, Role, CustomRole, Permission / Action, UserRole (scope, effective dates), Delegation, Device, Guardian (primary flag) |
| Structure | Tenant, Institution (status Draft / Active / Blocked), Department, Program, Year, Semester, Section, Class, Subject, SubjectGroup, MentorAssignment, AcademicCalendar, WeeklyOff |
| People | StudentProfile (status incl. Detained), StaffProfile, StaffDocument, Assignment (several per staff) |
| Academic | Timetable, MeetingLink, Assignment, Submission (late flag), StudyMaterial, Promotion |
| Attendance | Attendance (Present / Absent / On approved leave / Not held), AttendanceCorrection, TermLock, RiskFlag |
| Exams | ExamRule, ExamPattern, GradeBand, Exam, HallTicket, Marks (Draft / Submitted / Approved / Rejected / Published, special codes), Result, Backlog, SupplementaryRegistration |
| Finance | FeePolicy, FeeStructure (version), FeeException, Installment, Scholarship, Concession, Payment (Started / Pending / Paid / Failed, gateway ID, request key), Receipt (void flag), LateFeeWaiver, PeriodLock, Credit |
| Leave | LeaveType, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest (unit, days counted, route, final approver), Substitute |
| Communication | Notice, Message, Notification, Delivery, CommunityPost, Comment, Event, RSVP, Complaint, StudentNote (correction link), Policy, PolicyAcceptance |
| Governance | ApprovalRequest, ApprovalStep, AuditLog (write-once), DataRequest, ExportRequest |
| Phase 2–3 | Payroll, Payslip; LibraryBook, Loan, Reservation, Fine; Company, Job, Application, Interview, Offer; ApplicationForm, MeritList; Hostel, Room; Route, Vehicle; Alumni; ResearchProject, Grant; ApiKey, Webhook |

Attendance and marks are partitioned by academic year in each tenant database.

##### 16.6 Deployment (AWS, India regions)

| Layer | AWS service |
| --- | --- |
| Web front end | CloudFront + S3 (installable web app; subdomain per tenant) |
| Gateway | API Gateway + Application Load Balancer |
| Compute | EKS running separate Spring Boot services |
| Identity | Keycloak cluster |
| Database | RDS PostgreSQL, one database per tenant (shared with row-level security for small plans) |
| Messages | Amazon SQS or RabbitMQ |
| Cache | ElastiCache (Redis) for sessions and permission cache |
| Search | OpenSearch |
| Files and backups | S3 with virus scanning and lifecycle rules |
| Audit | Write-once storage (e.g. S3 Object Lock) |
| Secrets | Secrets Manager |
| Monitoring | CloudWatch, Prometheus, Grafana |
| CI/CD | Pipeline → ECR → EKS; Development, Staging, Production |

The design stays portable to Azure (AKS, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Service Bus, Blob Storage) but v1 runs on AWS only.

##### 16.7 Integrations

- Payment gateway (Razorpay by default) with verified webhooks; UPI, cards, net banking, wallets.
- SMS provider under DLT rules, with each institution's sender ID and templates.
- Email service; push notifications for the installable app.
- Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams meetings, built by the platform in Phase 1.
- File exports in Tally, UDISE+, AISHE and affiliating-university formats; direct connections later.
- SSO through Keycloak (optional).

##### 16.8 Implementation checklist

- [ ] Tenant provisioning with retry and clean-up; Keycloak realm per tenant
- [ ] Action lists per role, scopes, custom roles, role switcher, RBAC mapping
- [ ] Approval engine: approve / reject only, no self-approval, skip logic, bulk approval, reminders, delegation, concurrency
- [ ] Length-based leave routing; working-day counting
- [ ] Attendance window, Not held, substitutes, term lock with timed unlock
- [ ] Marks states, special codes, range checks, publish-after-approval, withdrawal
- [ ] Fee policy ranges and exceptions; payment states; idempotent receipts; gap-free numbering
- [ ] Write-once audit logs with masking and sensitive-view logging
- [ ] Notification service: quiet hours, emergency override, daily SMS summary, DLT templates, failure lists
- [ ] Pass/fail checks in Section 21 automated before release

These targets are final decisions; the word “proposed” from Version 1.0 is removed.

| Area | Final target |
| --- | --- |
| Availability | 99.5% monthly in the first year; 99.9% after \[NF-01\] |
| Performance | 95% of pages under 2 s; 95% of API calls under 500 ms; attendance for 60 students saved under 1 s \[NF-02\] |
| Peak load | 10× normal for 1 hour on results day and fee deadlines, load-tested on Staging \[NF-03, QA-05\] |
| Scale | No fixed v1 target; later phase \[NF-04\] |
| Devices | Current Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox, plus Android Chrome up to 2 versions old; 360 px phones \[NF-05\] |
| Accessibility | WCAG 2.1 AA on parent, student and teacher screens \[NF-06\] |
| Language | English only in v1 \[CM-13\] |
| Security | Lockout for 15 minutes after 5 wrong passwords; Admin can unlock early \[NF-07\]. Passwords and two-step login as in Section 11.0 \[R2-12, NF-09\]. Field-level encryption for sensitive fields; one outside security test before launch |
| Backup and recovery | At most 15 minutes of data lost; back online within 4 hours \[NF-10\]. Backup retention set per tenant \[WF-02\] |
| Retention | Set per tenant when it is created \[CL-08, AU-02\] |
| Data location | India only (AWS Mumbai / Hyderabad) \[TE-06\] |
| Notifications | In-app within 1 minute; SMS and email handed to the provider within 5 minutes \[NF-13\] |
| Permission changes | Effective within 1 minute \[TE-10\] |
| Maintenance window, support SLA | Not in v1 \[NF-11, R2-27\] |

#### 18. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Tenant | The paying customer: a university (or group) with everything under it, a standalone college or a standalone school; has its own database by default (small plans share one) |
| Institution | A college or school inside a tenant |
| Management | Owner / trust role above the Principal in private institutions |
| Product Owner | The company that owns and runs EDU 360 |
| Plan | Subscription package: pricing type, ticked modules and features, limits |
| Trial | 30-day tenant state before Active; read-only after it ends until payment |
| Data Protection Officer (DPO) | Platform role that approves full-tenant exports and deletions |
| Data Protection Contact | The tenant's person who handles personal-data requests |
| RBAC | Role-based access control |
| Scope | The part of the hierarchy a role applies to |
| F / M / C / A / V / R / N | Full / Manage / Configure / Approve / View / Request / No access (Section 6.2) |
| C (Configure) | Permission letter for setting up rules and settings |
| Action list | Detailed per-role permissions (e.g. MARKS\_ENTER, RESULT\_PUBLISH) that developers build from |
| Custom role | A role an institution Admin creates with any rights |
| Role switcher | Control for a user with several roles to choose the active one |
| Approval chain | Ordered approvers for a request (Section 7.1) |
| Delegation | Temporary hand-over of approvals to a same-or-higher role |
| Exception request | Request to save a fee outside the policy range |
| Concession | One-off discount for one student, approved by the Principal |
| Scholarship | Scheme with rules for many students |
| Daily collection report | The day's payments, sent to the Principal |
| Fee policy | Rules (heads, ranges, schemes) within which fee structures are set |
| Program | A course of study in a department (e.g. B.Sc. Physics), with years and semesters |
| Subject group | Students from several sections taking one subject |
| Mentor / class coordinator | Faculty member assigned to a section; final approver for short student leave |
| Not held | Attendance mark for a cancelled period; left out of the percentage |
| Term lock | Principal's lock on attendance and marks; unlock lasts at most 3 days |
| Attendance risk / academic risk | Flags from Section 7.7 |
| Hall ticket | Admit card for an examination |
| Backlog | A failed subject to be cleared in a supplementary exam |
| Detained | Student status for a student not promoted at year end |
| No-dues check | Dues must be cleared before certificates or TC |
| Deletion certificate | Record of who deleted a tenant, when and what |
| Staging | Copy of production with fake data, used for testing |
| DLT | India's registration system for SMS sender IDs and templates |
| SSO | Single sign-on with the institution's identity system |
| HOD | Head of Department |
