#### 20. Default formulas

Every institution starts with these formulas and can change them \[R2-37, AT-05, OB-16\].

| Measure | Default formula |
| --- | --- |
| Attendance % (per subject) | Present ÷ (periods held − periods on approved leave) × 100. “Not held” periods and holidays are not counted as held |
| Attendance % (overall) | Same formula, adding up all subjects |
| Attendance risk | Normal ≥ 75%; Warning 65–75%; Critical < 65% \[RK-01\] |
| Pass % | Students who passed ÷ students who appeared (AB not counted) × 100 |
| GPA (one semester) | Sum of (grade point × credits) ÷ sum of credits |
| CGPA | Same formula across all completed semesters |
| Outstanding fees | Amount billed + late fees − scholarships − concessions − amount paid − credit balance |
| Fees paid online % | Amount paid online ÷ total amount paid × 100 |
| Placement % *(Phase 2)* | Students placed ÷ eligible students who registered × 100 |
| Weekly active teachers % | Teachers who logged in at least once in the last 7 days ÷ active teacher accounts × 100 |
| Parent login % | Parents who logged in during the last 30 days ÷ parent accounts × 100 |
| Trial-to-paid % | Trials that became paid ÷ trials that ended × 100 |
| Renewal rate | Tenants that renewed ÷ tenants due for renewal × 100 |

Worked example: a student with 40 periods held in a subject, 2 of them on approved leave, and 30 present has 30 ÷ (40 − 2) × 100 = 78.9%, which is Normal.

#### 21. Pass/fail checks for high-risk rules

These checks cover permissions, approvals, money and marks only \[R2-41\]. QA writes all other test cases \[DC-04\]. Every one must pass before release.

| # | Situation | Must happen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A user from one tenant asks for a record of another tenant (changes the ID in the address or API) | Refused; nothing shown; attempt logged; Admin alerted on repeats \[AU-05\] |
| 2 | A parent changes the student ID to another child's | Refused; nothing shown |
| 3 | A platform role (Support, Billing, Platform Admin) tries to read tenant academic or fee data through screens, API or export | Refused, unless the tenant Admin has granted Support read-only access for that ticket (24 hours); every view is logged \[WF-11\] |
| 4 | A user with two roles submits a request and is also the next approver | Their step is skipped; the reason is logged \[AP-04\] |
| 5 | Someone calls “publish results” before the final approval | Refused; no result published; no notification sent |
| 6 | A teacher not assigned to a class marks its attendance | Refused, unless assigned as substitute for that date \[AT-03\] |
| 7 | A teacher edits attendance after midnight | Refused; only a correction request is allowed \[AT-02\] |
| 8 | Attendance or marks are edited after the term is locked | Refused; an unlock needs a reason and relocks after 3 days \[AT-09\] |
| 9 | Marks are rejected | The old submission stays locked; the teacher must make a new submission \[R2-01\] |
| 10 | A fee value outside the policy range is saved | Refused unless an exception was approved by the Finance Director (or Management) and the Principal, or by the Principal alone where there is no Management \[R2-03\] |
| 11 | The browser shows “payment success” but the gateway has not confirmed | Payment stays Pending; no receipt \[FE-07\] |
| 12 | The gateway sends the same confirmation twice | One payment, one receipt \[FE-09\] |
| 13 | The Accountant marks an online payment paid by hand | Allowed only with a gateway reference number; logged \[R2-33\] |
| 14 | A receipt is cancelled | Needs Principal approval; its number stays as “void” \[FE-12\] |
| 15 | An Admin bulk-corrects marks, attendance or fees | Changes go into the approval chain, not straight into the records \[R2-32\] |
| 16 | Two approvers act on the same request at once | First wins; the second sees “already actioned by \<name>” \[TE-09\] |
| 17 | A user's role is changed while they are logged in | Logged out at once; new rights at next login \[WF-27\] |
| 18 | A delegate approves after the delegation dates | Refused; pending items are back with the original approver \[AP-09\] |

#### 22. Privacy and legal

- Data protection rules are generic and configurable per institution \[PV-01\].
- The institution owns its data; EDU 360 processes it on the institution's behalf under a data processing agreement signed with each customer \[PV-02\].
- Parents give consent during admission or onboarding; it is recorded with the date \[PV-03\].
- College parents see attendance, results and fees by default. The student is told and can ask the institution to limit this (legal check needed) \[PV-04\].
- After a data breach, the platform tells the institution within 24 hours; the institution informs the authorities and people as the law requires \[PV-05\].
- Personal-data requests are handled by the tenant's Data Protection Contact; no fixed time limit \[PV-06, R2-25\].
- Platform analytics use only anonymous, combined numbers; customers can opt out \[PV-07\].
- No AI features in v1 \[PV-08\]. Only the last 4 digits of Aadhaar are stored \[R2-34\].
- All data stays in India (AWS Mumbai / Hyderabad) \[TE-06\].
- Terms of service, privacy policy and the data processing agreement are written by the internal team \[PV-09\].
- Lawyer checks before launch: PV-04, college health notes visible to parents (R2-29), and no time limit for data requests (PV-06).

#### 23. Testing and release

- Every rule and workflow step gets an ID \[DC-03\]. Each rule ID has at least one positive, one negative and one permission test \[QA-06\].
- Environments: Development, Staging (like production, generated fake data) and Production \[R2-15\]. Only generated fake data is used for testing \[QA-03\].
- Load tests on Staging for results day and fee deadlines (10× normal for 1 hour) \[QA-05\].
- One outside security test before launch \[R2-28\]; security claims are used in marketing only after it.
- The QA lead signs off acceptance testing \[QA-01\]. The Product Owner decides each time whether a release can go out with known bugs \[QA-04\].
- Pilot with 3–5 institutions for one term before public launch \[QA-07\]; KPI targets are set after the pilot.
- Releases go to all tenants as one version; rollback is app-only \[R2-26\].

##### 25.2 Risks accepted

| Decision | Risk | Safeguard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fully custom roles \[R2-02\] | An Admin could give themselves any right, such as entering marks | Every rights change is logged and the Principal / Management is notified (built in) |
| Cheque bounce not handled \[FE-10\] | A bounced cheque stays “paid” until the receipt is cancelled | Accountant cancels the receipt with Principal approval |
| Cash checked only by the daily report \[R2-33\] | One person still takes and records cash | Principal reviews the daily report every day |
| No time limit for data requests \[PV-06\]; generic privacy law \[PV-01\] | India's data protection law may set deadlines | Lawyer check before launch |
| College health notes visible to parents \[R2-29\] | College students are adults | Lawyer check together with PV-04 |
| Audit logs exportable by anyone who can view them \[AU-03\] | Logs can still reveal sensitive activity | Exports are logged; sensitive fields masked |
| Separate services from day one \[TE-02\] | More cost and time for the first release | None needed if the team is ready |
| Release with known bugs decided case by case \[QA-04\] | Serious bugs may ship | Product Owner decision each time |
| No platform tax in v1 (open item 5) | Invoices may need GST under Indian tax law | Confirm with a tax adviser before the first invoice |

## F.3 Version 3.2 Section 26 tab (replaced by the V3.3 tab in Part II)

### 26. Action list per role (new in Version 3.0)

This tab is Section 26 of the EDU 360 Final Master Product Document, Version 3.2. It sits in its own tab because of its size; the rest of the document is in the main tab.

EDU 360 has 262 actions: 219 in Phase 1, 32 in Phase 2 and 11 in Phase 3. Version 3.2 adds 8 actions: 270 in all (226 in Phase 1, 32 in Phase 2, 12 in Phase 3) [D-002, F-7, F-11, F-12, F-13]. Each action is one thing a user can do; developers build every access check from it, testers test every line, and institution Admins pick from it when they build custom roles [R2-02, RL-05]. The companion Excel (EDU 360 Action List V3.1) also gives, for every action, the full rules the system checks, what is never allowed and the source, plus a role-by-action grid.

#### 26.1 Rules for every action

1. Approval actions act only at the chain step the role holds (Section 7.1); nobody approves their own request or acts at two steps of one request – the step is skipped and logged [AP-04]. Added in 3.2: there is no self-approval anywhere, including the Principal's own leave [D-002].
2. Every action is checked on the server against role, scope and state – never only in the screen. Added in 3.1: rights are scope-bound and never inherit broader access by accident; a user with several roles acts in one active role at a time [PQ-16, PQ-17].
3. Every create, edit, delete, approval, export, login, denied attempt and view of sensitive data is logged [7.14, AU-01, AU-05]. Added in 3.1: actions that view, export, correct or delete sensitive personal or financial data are marked in the Sensitive data column of the Action List V3.1; their rights are given explicitly, never by default [PQ-66].
4. Platform roles never reach tenant data, except Support under tenant-granted 24-hour ticket access [WF-11].
5. A delegate can use approval actions only for the delegated dates [AP-07]. Added in 3.2: delegation goes to a same-or-higher role, or to the one designated deputy – Principal → Vice-Principal (college and school); the deputy never acts on a request they raised, are the subject of or already acted on [D-001].
6. A role can also get any action through a custom role; “Never allowed” items stay blocked whatever the custom role says.

#### 26.2 Role groups used below

| Group | Roles |
| --- | --- |
| Everyone with a login | All 70 roles, including platform roles and applicants |
| All tenant users | Every staff role, college and school students, and parents |
| All tenant staff | Every tenant role except students, parents and applicants |
| Self-service-only roles (3.2) | Driver, Security Supervisor, Security Staff, Housekeeping Supervisor – profile, payslip, own leave and notices only [RL-07, F-6] |
| Tenant Admin (3.2) | The top Admin of the tenant: University Admin in a university tenant; College Admin or School Admin in a standalone tenant [F-12] |

# Appendix G — V3.3 Change Table (source, carried in full)

The table applied to build Part II; Appendix D shows where each row landed.

## EDU 360 – Main Document Version 3.3: Change Table

27 Oct 2026 · applies to *EDU 360 – Final Master Product Document (Version 3.2)* → Version 3.3

### How to use this table

- Every row names the section and the exact place in the Version 3.2 main document, quotes the Version 3.2 wording that is affected (shortened with … where long), and gives the Version 3.3 wording to add. All Version 3.3 wording carries the marker **“Changed in 3.3”**.
- Following the change rule [R2-42] and the Version 3.2 practice, nothing is deleted: a changed sentence keeps its Version 3.2 wording, and the “Changed in 3.3” note goes beside it. Where a row says **Add**, the text is new; where it says **Replace label**, only a version label or count changes.
- **Decision** names the Product Owner decision behind each row: C1–C13 and answers 1–10 (27 Oct 2026), and the letter-gap decisions (#1–#114 of the letter-gap workbook; 95 accepted as proposed, 19 changed). **Derived** marks a change that follows from a decision through an existing rule (D-003: a role that approves in an area carries A) but was not separately decided; these are listed again in Part E.
- The companion files carry the same changes: *EDU 360 Action List V3.3* (278 actions; column N “Changed in V3.3”; Change Log V3.3 sheet with every role list before and after) and *EDU 360 Master Permission Matrix V3.3* (71 roles; lavender cells with “V3.2 X → V3.3 Y [ref]” comments; Change Log V3.3 sheet). The Section 26 tab is replaced by *EDU360_V3_3_Section26_Action_List_per_Role.md*.

**Totals after Version 3.3:** 71 roles (Governing Body Approver added) · 28 feature areas · 278 actions (234 Phase 1, 32 Phase 2, 12 Phase 3; 8 new, all Phase 1) · 101 actions marked sensitive (85 + 13 leave actions with medical attachments + 3 new) · 68 matrix letters changed, 55 kept letters confirmed as backed, 1 row added.

### Part D – New Section 12.12 Governing Body Approver (Changed in 3.3)

#### 12.12 Governing Body Approver *(Changed in 3.3)*

Used only in a tenant where there is no Management. The Tenant Admin creates the account (TENANT_TOP_USERS_CREATE) with two-step login. The role approves or rejects, and sees, only the leave requests for which it is the set approver, and sees no other data [C6, C7, C13, answer 6].

| Step | Action (screen path) | Impact | Affects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Login | Tenant URL → credentials → two-step code | Approver dashboard: pending leave requests only | Own session |
| 2. Principal's leave | Leave → Pending → Approve / Reject (PRINCIPAL_LEAVE_APPROVE), for a standalone college or school, or a college or school under a university that set this role as approver | Principal's leave decided | Principal |
| 3. Vice-Chancellor's leave | Leave → Pending → Approve / Reject (SENIOR_LEAVE_APPROVE) | Vice-Chancellor's leave decided | Vice-Chancellor |
| 4. Data Protection Contact's leave | Leave → Pending → Approve / Reject, for a dedicated Data Protection Contact (SENIOR_LEAVE_APPROVE) | Leave decided | Data Protection Contact |
| 5. Approver changes | Notified whenever the Admin or University Admin changes the leave approver | Accountability | Admin |
| 6. Logout | Logout | Session ends | – |

**Restrictions:** No other tenant data. Remark required on reject. Never approves its own request. The fee fallbacks to the Principal where there is no Management (HI-11, R2-03) stay unchanged [C6].
